title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
山西鄉試錄序
聖天子顯道崇化嚮厲材賢思以
興致太平甚盛嘉靖丙午天
下當復
獻賢書維時山西巡按監察御
史齊〔宗道〕祗慎乃事豫物章
軌罔不飭備考試官〔京〕學正
===
蔡〔芝〕同考試官學正龍〔興〕薛
〔緯〕教諭陳〔一元〕何〔汝璋〕崔〔一〕
〔元〕彭〔冀衢〕以先巡按監察御
史陳〔豪〕檄聘至於是左布政
使張〔文奎〕左參政葛〔守禮〕司
提調按察使戴〔䝉〕僉事李〔蓁〕
司監試偕入院迺進先攝提
punctuated:
山西鄉試錄序

聖天子顯道崇化，嚮厲材賢，思以興致太平，甚盛。嘉靖丙午，天下當復獻賢書。維時山西巡按監察御史齊〔宗道〕祗慎乃事，豫物章軌，罔不飭備。考試官〔京〕學正蔡〔芝〕、同考試官學正龍〔興〕、薛〔緯〕，教諭陳〔一元〕、何〔汝璋〕、崔〔一〕〔元〕、彭〔冀衢〕，以先巡按監察御史陳〔豪〕檄聘至。於是左布政使張〔文奎〕、左參政葛〔守禮〕司提調，按察使戴〔䝉〕、僉事李〔蓁〕司監試，偕入院，迺進先攝提
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Shanxi Provincial Examination

The sagely Son of Heaven makes the Way manifest and exalts moral transformation, encouraging the talented and worthy with the intention of bringing about an age of great peace. How splendid! In the bingwu year of Jiajing [1546], the realm was once again due to submit its lists of worthy men. At this time, Qi Zongdao, Regional Inspector and Investigating Censor for Shanxi, attended reverently and conscientiously to his duties. Supplies, regulations, and procedures [?] were all put in order and made ready.

The Examiner, Cai Zhi, an Instructor at a capital school [?], and the Associate Examiners—Instructors Long Xing and Xue Wei, and School Instructors Chen Yiyuan, He Ruzhang, Cui Yiyuan, and Peng Jiqu—arrived in response to an official invitation from the preceding Regional Inspector and Investigating Censor, Chen Hao. Zhang Wenkui, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Ge Shouli, Left Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner, took charge as Proctors; Dai Meng, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner, and Li Zhen, Assistant Provincial Surveillance Commissioner, took charge of supervising the examination. They entered the examination compound together and then admitted [the candidates selected by] the former acting education …

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
學事副使李〔良〕提學副使俞
〔洛伯〕分巡僉事江〔南〕所選士
二千有奇羣而校之登茲錄
者六十有五人將以上春官
對
大廷異日爲
天子使嗚呼茲六十有五人者是
===
誠助太平者非邪今內自公
卿外自藩臬而下小大百執
事皆莫不由茲選然求以當
上意者蓋僅僅見豈科舉之制非
選辟之具抑古者明王所與
興理不盡出於文學議論之
臣而文學議論之臣固藝焉
punctuated: 學事副使李〔良〕、提學副使俞〔洛伯〕、分巡僉事江〔南〕所選士二千有奇，羣而校之，登茲錄者六十有五人，將以上春官，對大廷，異日爲天子使。嗚呼！茲六十有五人者，是誠助太平者非邪？今內自公卿，外自藩臬而下，小大百執事，皆莫不由茲選。然求以當上意者，蓋僅僅見。豈科舉之制非選辟之具？抑古者明王所與興理，不盡出於文學議論之臣，而文學議論之臣固藝焉
translation_en:
…the more than two thousand candidates selected by Li Liang, the vice commissioner who had previously served as acting education intendant; Yu Luobo, the vice commissioner serving as education intendant; and Jiang Nan, the assistant surveillance commissioner overseeing a circuit. They were assembled and examined, and sixty-five men were entered in this record. They will proceed to the Ministry of Rites, answer before the imperial court, and in days to come serve the Son of Heaven. Ah! Are these sixty-five men truly those who will help bring about great peace?

Today, from the dukes and ministers at court and the provincial administration and surveillance commissioners in the provinces downward, all officials, great and small, enter service through this selection. Yet those who meet His Majesty’s expectations are scarcely to be found. Could the civil-service examination system be unsuited to selecting and recruiting officials? Or is it that those with whom the enlightened kings of antiquity brought about good government did not all come from among ministers versed in literary learning and argument, while ministers versed in literary learning and argument are merely practitioners of an art…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
已邪天地山川之緼蓄靈異
也必有所附麗宣罍匪若人
其孰當之
陽龍二五之會
離明章徹
高朗四被又必有瑰瑋特達之
士象時而出匪斂聚於科目
===
亦曷由致之然士方未遇凡
凡擁詩書誦習涸思雕蟲以
其藝桐高秉時取科第比服
有官最下者則萎焉熸焉縻
好爵私寵斷効志於凡民不
可過庸篤也其能卽詩書所
稱古今之變皇帝王伯之略
punctuated: 已邪？天地山川之緼蓄靈異也，必有所附麗宣罍，匪若人，其孰當之？陽龍二五之會，離明章徹，高朗四被，又必有瑰瑋特達之士象時而出，匪斂聚於科目，亦曷由致之？然士方未遇，凡凡擁詩書誦習，涸思雕蟲，以其藝桐高秉時取科第。比服有官，最下者則萎焉熸焉，縻好爵，私寵斷，効志於凡民，不可過庸篤也。其能卽詩書所稱古今之變、皇帝王伯之略，
translation_en: …and nothing more? The numinous powers stored up in Heaven and Earth, mountains and rivers must find something in which to lodge and through which to manifest themselves [?]. If not such men, who could bear them? At the conjunction of yang and the dragon, of two and five [?], when radiant brightness shines clearly through and lofty light reaches everywhere, there must also be extraordinary men of exceptional attainments who emerge in response to the times. Unless they are gathered through the examination system, how else can they be brought into service? Yet while scholars have not yet found recognition, they commonly pore over the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents, reciting and studying them, exhausting their thoughts on the petty craft of literary composition. Through their literary skill, they attain examination success—the intervening wording is unclear [?]. Once they assume office, the lowest among them wither and lose their fire, entangled in fine official rank and treating the power to bestow favor and make decisions as their private possession [?]. In devoting themselves to the common people, they cannot be expected to show much steadfastness [?]. As for those who can draw upon the changes of past and present recounted in the Odes and Documents, and the strategies of august sovereigns, emperors, kings, and hegemons…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
抵掌不忘爲世所普賢者豈
少哉乃亦或不足於古人之
治如宋時士大夫然徒以文
學議論譁然相雜陸沉於獻
納授受之間無甚裨時事不
亦後人得失檢鏡之林耶然
以〔京〕所徵考宋人文學議論
===
猶類多可觀乃今士大夫視
宋人何如欲求以當
上意助太平要必有取誠不專於
文學議論徒以飾華溷聽爲
也夫爲衣者務以禦寒爲食
者務以充腹苟饑寒之弗顧
而姑炫玄黃錯鼎俎以夸�western
punctuated:
抵掌不忘，爲世所普賢者，豈少哉？乃亦或不足於古人之治，如宋時士大夫然，徒以文學議論譁然相雜，陸沉於獻納授受之間，無甚裨時事，不亦後人得失檢鏡之林耶？然以〔京〕所徵考，宋人文學議論，猶類多可觀。乃今士大夫視宋人何如？欲求以當上意、助太平，要必有取，誠不專於文學議論，徒以飾華溷聽爲也。
夫爲衣者務以禦寒，爲食者務以充腹。苟饑寒之弗顧，而姑炫玄黃、錯鼎俎，以夸�western
translation_en:
…clapping their hands in animated discussion and never forgetting these matters—could there be few such men whom the world generally esteems as worthy [?]? Yet some also fall short of the governance achieved by the ancients, like the scholar-officials of the Song, who merely mingled noisily in literary learning and debate, sinking into obscurity amid the presentation of counsel and exchanges between superiors and subordinates, without greatly benefiting the affairs of their time. Does this not provide later generations with a store of successes and failures to scrutinize and take as a mirror? Yet, judging by what I, 〔Jing〕, have investigated, the literary learning and discussions of Song men still generally offer much worth considering. How do today’s scholar-officials compare with those of the Song? If they seek to fulfill His Majesty’s intentions and contribute to an age of peace, they must have something of substance to offer; it certainly cannot consist exclusively in literary learning and debate, merely embellishing their words and confusing their listeners.
Those who make clothing strive to ward off cold; those who prepare food strive to fill the belly. If they disregard hunger and cold, merely displaying dark and yellow fabrics and setting out cauldrons and sacrificial stands in order to show off [corrupt text: �western] [?]…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
於人果何益者哉是故士無
尚言方今天下事所需於士
大夫者甚厚將借箸更僕終
日縷縷而莫之能旣也所貴
於士大夫必敦尚本實溫雅
愽大通達治體忠骾有氣質
敢於任事不齷齪進退與時
===
浮沉相上下者夫然後舉所
需而畀之天下太平可恃不
然吾懼其終也山西故多閒
人不可殫紀即耳目所睹聽
于今之顯融者鮮有浮靡流
浪之風其胥化則然又地鄰
上都介於戎狄頃且多事即齊民
punctuated:
於人，果何益者哉？是故士無尚言。方今天下事，所需於士大夫者甚厚，將借箸更僕，終日縷縷而莫之能旣也。所貴於士大夫，必敦尚本實，溫雅愽大，通達治體，忠骾有氣質，敢於任事，不齷齪進退、與時浮沉相上下者。夫然後舉所需而畀之，天下太平可恃。不然，吾懼其終也。
山西故多閒人，不可殫紀。即耳目所睹聽，于今之顯融者，鮮有浮靡流浪之風，其胥化則然。又地鄰上都，介於戎狄，頃且多事，即齊民
translation_en:
…before others—what benefit, indeed, could there be? Thus scholars should not prize mere words. At present, the affairs of the realm place very substantial demands upon scholar-officials. Were one to borrow chopsticks to lay out plans and keep changing attendants as the discussion continued, one could speak at length all day without exhausting the subject. What we value in scholar-officials is that they earnestly esteem fundamentals and substance, are gentle and refined, broad-minded and capacious, understand the principles of governance, are loyal and outspoken, possess strength of character, and dare to shoulder responsibilities, rather than fussing over advancement and retirement and rising and falling with the currents of the times. Only then can we entrust to them all that is required, and rely upon peace throughout the realm. Otherwise, I fear how it will end.
Shanxi has long had many men of leisure [?], too numerous to record exhaustively. Among those now eminent whom I have personally seen or heard of, few display a tendency toward superficial extravagance or unrestrained drifting. Their influence upon one another has made them so. Moreover, the region borders the imperial capital and lies amid the Rong and Di peoples; lately, too, it has faced many troubles. Even the common people…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
若總丱之童猶習聞理亂之
因廢興之故矧茲六十有五
人者之生於其鄉非特文學
議論炳炳烺烺流惟德之務侈
有令圖將異日爲
天子所材助致太平之業也孰禦
甚欲觀之語曰平地注水
===
去燥就濕均薪施火去濕就
燥言類應也
天子擇言用中人思作行不捐弃
其德以應名世　不佞尤有
望於二三執事者崇實黜浮
簡文證履俾能言之士蔑所
稱賢而褎然篤行君子相起
punctuated:
若總丱之童，猶習聞理亂之因、廢興之故，矧茲六十有五人者之生於其鄉，非特文學議論炳炳烺烺，流惟德之務，侈有令圖，將異日爲天子所材，助致太平之業也，孰禦？甚欲觀之。語曰：「平地注水，去燥就濕；均薪施火，去濕就燥。」言類應也。
天子擇言用中，人思作行，不捐弃其德以應名世。不佞尤有望於二三執事者：崇實黜浮，簡文證履，俾能言之士蔑所稱賢，而褎然篤行君子相起
translation_en:
…Even children with their hair tied in tufts are accustomed to hearing about the causes of order and disorder and the reasons for decline and resurgence. How much more must this be true of these sixty-five men born in this region! Not only do their literary learning and discussions shine brilliantly; they devote themselves to virtue [?] and cherish lofty, admirable designs. When, in days to come, the Son of Heaven employs their talents and they help bring about an age of great peace, who could stand in their way? I eagerly wish to witness it. As the saying goes: “Pour water on level ground: it leaves the dry places and moves toward the damp. Apply fire to evenly laid firewood: it leaves the damp places and moves toward the dry.” This speaks of the way like responds to like.
The Son of Heaven selects worthy counsel and applies what accords with the Mean. People aspire to cultivate their conduct, preserving their virtue so as to attain distinction in their age. I, unworthy as I am, place particular hopes in you gentlemen charged with this work: exalt substance and reject superficiality; scrutinize writings and verify conduct. Let those skilled merely in words have no grounds for being called worthy, while gentlemen outstanding in steadfast conduct rise together …

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
而彈冠焉斯非所以風之哉
是役也總督軍務兵部侍郎
翁〔萬達〕前巡撫山西今陝西
總督軍務兵部侍郎曾〔銑〕巡
撫都御史楊〔守謙〕巡撫大同
都御史詹〔榮〕燿武覿文嘉樂
逢掖巡按直隸監察御史黃
===
如桂巡鹽御史王〔忬〕宣猷振
雅式貞文敎總理糧儲戶部
郎中張〔旦〕主事馬〔愼〕刑部員
外郎徐〔文亨〕籌邊讞獄通觀
盛侍右布政使呂〔顒〕右𠫭政
徐〔守義〕王〔楊〕左𠫭議顧〔堅〕右
𠫭議蘇〔志臯〕李〔磐〕副使王〔崇〕
punctuated:
而彈冠焉，斯非所以風之哉？
是役也，總督軍務兵部侍郎翁〔萬達〕、前巡撫山西今陝西總督軍務兵部侍郎曾〔銑〕、巡撫都御史楊〔守謙〕、巡撫大同都御史詹〔榮〕，燿武覿文，嘉樂逢掖。巡按直隸監察御史黃如桂、巡鹽御史王〔忬〕，宣猷振雅，式貞文敎。總理糧儲戶部郎中張〔旦〕、主事馬〔愼〕、刑部員外郎徐〔文亨〕，籌邊讞獄，通觀盛侍。右布政使呂〔顒〕、右𠫭政徐〔守義〕、王〔楊〕、左𠫭議顧〔堅〕、右𠫭議蘇〔志臯〕、李〔磐〕、副使王〔崇〕
translation_en:
…and dust off their caps in readiness for office. Is this not a means of inspiring them?
For this undertaking, Weng Wanda was Supreme Commander of Military Affairs and Vice Minister of War. Zeng Xian, formerly Grand Coordinator of Shanxi, was now Supreme Commander of Military Affairs in Shaanxi and Vice Minister of War. Yang Shouqian was Grand Coordinator and Censor-in-Chief. Zhan Rong was Grand Coordinator of Datong and Censor-in-Chief. Displaying military prowess and attending to literary achievement, they delighted in and esteemed the scholars in their broad-sleeved robes.
Huang Rugui was Regional Inspector of Zhili and Investigating Censor. Wang Yu was Salt-inspecting Censor. They promulgated sound policies and promoted refined learning, thereby upholding literary education.
Zhang Dan was Director in the Ministry of Revenue, with overall responsibility for grain reserves. Ma Shen was a Secretary. Xu Wenheng was Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice. They planned frontier affairs and reviewed judicial cases, and together witnessed the grand proceedings [?].
Lü Yong was Right Provincial Administration Commissioner. Xu Shouyi and Wang Yang were Right Vice Administration Commissioners. Gu Jian was Left Assistant Administration Commissioner. Su Zhigao and Li Pan were Right Assistant Administration Commissioners. Wang Chong was a Surveillance Vice Commissioner…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
劉〔璽〕張〔鎬〕彭〔大有〕艾〔希淳〕陳
〔耀〕僉事程〔綬〕蒲〔澤〕賀〔惠〕行太
僕寺卿孫〔鑾〕署都指揮僉事
崔〔憲〕吳〔熹〕王〔佐〕翊襄輸力防
範宣勤皆於法得書也書之
直隸滁州儒學學正周〔京〕謹
序
punctuated:
劉〔璽〕、張〔鎬〕、彭〔大有〕、艾〔希淳〕、陳〔耀〕，僉事程〔綬〕、蒲〔澤〕、賀〔惠〕，行太僕寺卿孫〔鑾〕，署都指揮僉事崔〔憲〕、吳〔熹〕、王〔佐〕，翊襄輸力，防範宣勤，皆於法得書也，書之。
直隸滁州儒學學正周〔京〕謹序。
translation_en:
…Liu Xi, Zhang Gao, Peng Dayou, Ai Xichun, and Chen Yao; Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Cheng Shou, Pu Ze, and He Hui; Sun Luan, Chief Minister of the Regional Court of the Imperial Stud; and acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Cui Xian, Wu Xi, and Wang Zuo all contributed their efforts in support and diligently maintained safeguards. All merit inclusion in this record according to the rules; thus I record them.
Respectfully composed as a preface by Zhou Jing, School Director of the Confucian School of Chuzhou, in the Metropolitan Region.

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試
監臨官
巡按山西監察御史齊宗道〔叔魯遼東廣寧右衛籍　山東鼎縣人戊戌進士〕
提調官
山西等處承宣布政使司左布政使張文奎〔應光陝西洛川縣人　丁丑進士〕
山西等處承宣布政使司左參政葛守禮〔與立山東德平縣人　己丑進士〕
監試官
山西等處提刑按察司按察使戴鱀〔時重浙江鄞縣人　丁丑進士〕
山西等處提刑按察司僉事李蓁〔森孝河南祥符縣人　乙未進士〕
===
考試官
直隸滁州儒學學正周京〔民仰福建莆田縣人　庚子貢士〕
直隸保定府易州儒學學正蔡芝〔卉伯廣西桂林中衛　官籍甲午貢士〕
同考試官
直隸揚州府通州儒學學正龍興〔子濬廣東海陽縣人　庚子貢士〕
河南歸德府睢州儒學學正薛緯〔子文湖廣竹山縣籍　江陵縣人丁酉貢士〕
直隸保定府蠡縣儒學教諭陳一元〔廷春廣東海陽縣人　庚子貢士〕
陝西漢中府金州旬河縣儒學教諭何汝璋〔子重四川壁山縣人　丁酉貢士〕
山東濟南府濱州霑化縣儒學教諭崔一元〔子仁廣西靈川縣人　庚子貢士〕
punctuated:
嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試。

監臨官：
巡按山西監察御史齊宗道〔叔魯，遼東廣寧右衛籍，山東鼎縣人，戊戌進士〕。

提調官：
山西等處承宣布政使司左布政使張文奎〔應光，陝西洛川縣人，丁丑進士〕。

第壹場

四書
夫子循循然善誘人，博我以文，約我以禮。
萬物並育而不相害，道並行而不相悖。小德川流，大德敦化。
資之深，則取之左右逢其原。

直，其正也；方，其義也。君子敬以直内，義以方外。
九二，利貞，中以爲志也。
君子之道，或出或處，或默或語。二人同心，其利斷金；同心之言，其臭如蘭。

translation_en:
First Session

Four Books
The Master skillfully guides people forward step by step. He broadens my learning through cultural refinement and restrains me through ritual propriety.
The myriad things grow together without harming one another; their ways proceed together without conflict. Lesser virtue flows like rivers; great virtue brings forth transformation in abundance.
When one draws deeply upon it, one encounters its source wherever one turns.

Book of Changes
Straightness signifies correctness; squareness signifies righteousness. The gentleman uses reverent attentiveness to make his inner self straight and righteousness to make his outward conduct square.
Nine in the second place: perseverance is beneficial, for he sets his purpose upon the mean.
The way of the gentleman is sometimes to enter public service and sometimes to remain in retirement, sometimes to be silent and sometimes to speak. When two people are of one mind, their sharpness can cut through metal; the words of those of one mind are fragrant as orchids.
The lines of the hexagrams imitate the movements of all things under Heaven.

Book of Documents
The virtue of cherishing life permeates the hearts of the people.
I shall indeed be able to carry out your instructions.
The sovereign establishes the supreme standard, gathers these five blessings, and distributes them widely among his common people.
In establishing government, appoint administrators, judicial officers, and governors as the three principal offices. The guards, keepers of the robes, and equerries …

punctuated:
小尹、左右攜僕、百司、庶府、大都、小伯、藝人、表臣、百司、太史、尹伯、庶常吉士。

詩
孑孑干旄，在浚之郊。素絲紕之，良馬四之。彼姝者子，何以畀之？
天子命我，城彼朔方。赫赫南仲，玁狁于襄。
有馮有翼，有孝有德，以引以翼。豈弟君子，四方爲則。顒顒卬卬，如圭如璋。令聞令望，豈弟君子，四方爲綱。鳳凰于飛，翽翽其羽，亦集爰止。藹藹王多吉士，維君子使，媚于天子。鳳凰于飛，翽翽其羽，亦傅于天。藹藹王多吉人，維君子命，媚于庶人。鳳凰鳴矣，于彼高岡。梧桐生矣，于彼朝陽。菶菶萋萋，雝雝喈喈。
儀式刑文王之典，日靖四方。伊嘏文王，既右享之。

秋，公伐邾。〔隱公七年〕夏，覃師師會齊人、鄭
translation_en:
…the lesser administrators, attendants and personal servants on the left and right, the various officials and officers of the storehouses, those governing great cities and lesser chiefs, skilled men, ministers serving beyond the court, the various officials, the Grand Scribe, chief administrators, and the many worthy men in regular service.

Book of Odes
Tall stands the banner with its yak-tail tassel in the outskirts of Jun. White silk threads border it; four fine horses draw the carriage. That admirable gentleman—what shall we give him?
The Son of Heaven commanded us to fortify that northern region. Illustrious was Nan Zhong: he drove off the Xianyun.
There are men to support and men to assist, men of filial devotion and virtue, to guide and to sustain. The gracious and kindly lord is a model for the four quarters. Dignified and lofty, like a gui tablet and a zhang tablet of jade, with fine reputation and high esteem, the gracious and kindly lord is the guiding cord of the four quarters. Phoenixes fly, their wings rustling; together they alight and rest. In abundant array, the king has many worthy officers; the lord employs them, and they win the affection of the Son of Heaven. Phoenixes fly, their wings rustling; they rise to the heavens. In abundant array, the king has many worthy men; the lord appoints them, and they win the affection of the common people. Phoenixes call upon that high ridge. Wutong trees grow on its sun-facing slope. Lush and luxuriant are the trees; harmonious and clear are the birds’ calls.
Follow and emulate the statutes of King Wen, daily bringing peace to the four quarters. That great King Wen has accepted and enjoyed the offerings.

Spring and Autumn Annals
In autumn, the duke attacked Zhu. 〔Seventh year of Duke Yin〕 In summer, Tan Shishi [?] joined men of Qi and Zheng …

論

人伐宋。辛未，取郜；辛巳，取防。〔隱公十年〕
春，王正月，公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯侵蔡。蔡潰，遂伐楚，次于陘。楚屈完來盟于師，盟于召陵。〔僖公四年〕
夏，楚人侵鄭。〔宣公三年〕冬，楚子伐鄭。〔宣公四年〕
宋公、陳侯、衛侯、曹侯會晉師于棐林，伐鄭。〔宣公元年〕公會晉師于瓦。〔定公八年〕
禮記
君子耆老不徒行，庶人耆老不徒食。
人情以爲田，故人以爲奧也。
禮樂刑政四達而不悖，則王道備矣。
仁義接賓主，有事，俎豆有數，曰聖；聖立而將之以敬，曰禮；禮以體長幼，曰德。德也者，得於身也。
第貳場
論
translation_en:
… men attacked Song. On the xinwei day, Gao was taken; on the xinsi day, Fang was taken. 〔Tenth year of Duke Yin〕
In spring, in the first month of the royal calendar, the duke joined the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao in invading Cai. Cai collapsed. They then attacked Chu and encamped at Xing. Qu Wan of Chu came to the army to make a covenant; the covenant was concluded at Shaoling. 〔Fourth year of Duke Xi〕
In summer, men of Chu invaded Zheng. 〔Third year of Duke Xuan〕 In winter, the Viscount of Chu attacked Zheng. 〔Fourth year of Duke Xuan〕
The Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, and the Marquis of Cao joined the army of Jin at Feilin and attacked Zheng. 〔First year of Duke Xuan〕 The duke met the army of Jin at Wa. 〔Eighth year of Duke Ding〕
Book of Rites
Elderly gentlemen do not travel on foot; elderly commoners do not eat meals without meat.
Human feelings are treated as a field to cultivate; thus people regard them as an inner sanctuary [?].
When rites, music, punishments, and government operate everywhere without conflict, the Way of the Kings is complete.
Benevolence and righteousness bring host and guest together [?]; when ceremonies are performed, the sacrificial stands and vessels have their prescribed numbers: this is called sageliness. When sageliness is established and carried out with reverence, this is called ritual propriety. When ritual propriety gives due expression to the distinction between elder and younger, this is called virtue. Virtue is what one acquires within oneself.
Second Session
Discourse

With consummate benevolence, Heaven and Earth become one body.

Since antiquity, none has surpassed Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu in matters of governance. title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
最著且要者能舉而言之乎漢唐宋諸
君有志於古者不可謂無其間若表章
六經若能通尚書若銳情經術若發揮
典籍若夜分觀書若專講春秋皆知從
事於學矣而其德其治皆不逮古遠甚
果何說乎洪惟我
太祖高皇帝天縱神聖不思而得其可見若
聖政記
大明日曆可以觀治
祖訓昭鑑錄可以觀德
觀心亭洪範圖可以觀學其他正大綱而舉
萬目交養互發者未易殫述可得言其
槩乎
列聖相承代有制作其著爲
文華寶鑑
御製帝訓
文華大訓名爲教
太子而
punctuated: 最著且要者，能舉而言之乎？漢唐宋諸君，有志於古者，不可謂無。其間若表章六經，若能通《尚書》，若銳情經術，若發揮典籍，若夜分觀書，若專講《春秋》，皆知從事於學矣，而其德其治，皆不逮古遠甚，果何說乎？洪惟我太祖高皇帝，天縱神聖，不思而得。其可見，若《聖政記》《大明日曆》，可以觀治；《祖訓》《昭鑑錄》，可以觀德；觀心亭、《洪範圖》，可以觀學。其他正大綱而舉萬目，交養互發者，未易殫述，可得言其槩乎？列聖相承，代有制作，其著爲《文華寶鑑》《御製帝訓》《文華大訓》，名爲教太子而
translation_en:
…can you identify and discuss the most notable and essential among them? Among the rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song, there were certainly some who aspired to emulate antiquity. Some elevated the Six Classics to prominence; some mastered the Book of Documents; some devoted themselves ardently to classical learning; some elucidated the canonical writings; some read far into the night; and some concentrated on studying the Spring and Autumn Annals. All knew to apply themselves to learning, yet their virtue and their governance fell far short of those of antiquity. How, indeed, can this be explained?
We reverently consider our Emperor Taizu Gao, endowed by Heaven with sagacity and spiritual understanding, who attained understanding without deliberation. Among the visible manifestations of this, the Record of Sagely Governance and the Daily Record of the Great Ming allow us to observe his governance; the Ancestral Instructions and the Record of the Illustrious Mirror allow us to observe his virtue; and the Pavilion for Contemplating the Mind and the Diagram of the Great Plan allow us to observe his learning. His other achievements—setting the main principles aright and attending to their myriad particulars, each nourishing and illuminating the other—cannot readily be recounted in full. Can you state their broad outlines?
The successive sage emperors each produced works in their reigns. Their writings include the Precious Mirror of the Hall of Literary Brilliance, the Imperially Composed Instructions for Emperors, and the Great Instructions of the Hall of Literary Brilliance. These were nominally intended to instruct the crown prince, yet…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
聖德
聖學於此具在其旨何居乎仰惟我
皇上恢宏
祖烈深探道源
至德如天誠有以立制禮作樂之本而天下化
中矣
聖學淵深未易窺測至於發其玄緒如
敬一箴心箴解視聽言動箴解遠有以契夫堯
舜禹湯文武不傳之秘近有以光夫
===
祖宗列聖之傳所以爲
聖子
神孫億萬年佑啓之圖者端在於是固嘗刻石
學宮諸士子得以莊誦潛心久矣請以
所能仰窺者鋪張揚厲之以爲
聖學之盛勿謗之曰不識不知而已
問經以載道史以載事固學者之所究心
而肆力焉者然刪述以後諸儒於六經
之旨歷代興衰之跡發明論記代有其
punctuated:
聖德聖學於此具在，其旨何居乎？仰惟我皇上恢宏祖烈，深探道源，至德如天，誠有以立制禮作樂之本，而天下化中矣。聖學淵深，未易窺測。至於發其玄緒，如《敬一箴》《心箴解》《視聽言動箴解》，遠有以契夫堯舜禹湯文武不傳之秘，近有以光夫祖宗列聖之傳。所以爲聖子神孫億萬年佑啓之圖者，端在於是。固嘗刻石學宮，諸士子得以莊誦潛心久矣。請以所能仰窺者鋪張揚厲之，以爲聖學之盛，勿謗之曰不識不知而已。

問：經以載道，史以載事，固學者之所究心而肆力焉者。然刪述以後，諸儒於六經之旨、歷代興衰之跡，發明論記，代有其
translation_en:
…sagely virtue and sagely learning are fully present in these works. What is their purport? We reverently consider how our Emperor has magnified his ancestors’ glorious achievements and probed deeply into the source of the Way. His supreme virtue is like Heaven: it truly provides the foundation for instituting rites and creating music, and all under Heaven is transformed toward the mean [?]. His sagely learning is profound and cannot readily be fathomed. As for works that disclose its subtle threads, such as the Admonition on Reverent Unity, the Explanation of the Admonition on the Mind, and the Explanations of the Admonitions on Looking, Listening, Speaking, and Acting, they accord with the untransmitted mysteries of the distant sovereigns Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu, while more recently bringing lustre to the tradition of the successive imperial ancestors. Precisely herein lies the plan to aid and guide his sagely sons and divine grandsons for countless ages. These works have already been carved on stone in the government schools, and you candidates have long been able to recite them reverently and ponder them deeply. Please expound and extol what you have been able reverently to discern, thereby setting forth the flourishing of sagely learning. Do not disparage it by saying merely that it is ‘without knowledge or understanding.’

Question: The classics convey the Way, and histories record events; these are certainly matters to which scholars devote their minds and exert their energies. Yet since Confucius’s work of editing and transmitting, scholars have elucidated, discussed, and recorded the purport of the Six Classics and the course of the rise and decline of successive dynasties. Every age has had its…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
人景行仰止請以晉之先哲表著者與
爾諸士論之於經若王通氏續經中說
之作亦有見斯道矣而或譏其僭若僞
者或稱其非荀楊所及與高於仲舒者
何無定論歟孫復氏尊王發微之著亦
有得春秋矣而或譏其淺若刻者或稱
其言簡義詳推見聖人之意者何所是
正歟至於邵子皇極經世一書則先儒
謂自易以來之所未有然又有議其專
===
於數學而上繼孔孟不傳之統乃獨歸
之程子何歟於史若董狐孔子稱其不
隱亦惟趙盾一事春秋從而書之夫爲
正卿而不討賊與首惡當有間矣乃不
蒙於末减何歟司馬遷朱子稱其才識
亦高今其史記一書盡易編年之法夫
創義例而師百代較其功誠傑然矣乃
不免於疵議何歟至於温公資治通鑑
一書則其君謂荀悅之所未及然又有
punctuated: 人。景行仰止，請以晉之先哲表著者與爾諸士論之。於經，若王通氏續經、中說之作，亦有見斯道矣，而或譏其僭若僞者，或稱其非荀楊所及與高於仲舒者，何無定論歟？孫復氏尊王發微之著，亦有得春秋矣，而或譏其淺若刻者，或稱其言簡義詳、推見聖人之意者，何所是正歟？至於邵子《皇極經世》一書，則先儒謂自易以來之所未有，然又有議其專於數學，而上繼孔孟不傳之統，乃獨歸之程子，何歟？於史，若董狐，孔子稱其不隱，亦惟趙盾一事，春秋從而書之。夫爲正卿而不討賊，與首惡當有間矣，乃不蒙於末减，何歟？司馬遷，朱子稱其才識亦高。今其《史記》一書，盡易編年之法。夫創義例而師百代，較其功誠傑然矣，乃不免於疵議，何歟？至於温公《資治通鑑》一書，則其君謂荀悅之所未及，然又有
translation_en:
…such men. Their lofty conduct inspires admiration. Let me discuss with you candidates those earlier worthies of Jin who were especially distinguished. In classical learning, take Wang Tong’s continuations of the Classics and his Sayings on the Mean (Zhongshuo): these show some insight into this Way. Yet some criticize them as presumptuous or spurious, while others declare that Xun Kuang and Yang Xiong could not equal him, and that he surpassed Dong Zhongshu. Why is there no settled judgment? Sun Fu’s Honoring the King and Elucidating Subtleties (Zunwang fawei) likewise grasps something of the Spring and Autumn Annals. Yet some criticize it as shallow or severe, while others praise its concise language and fully developed meanings, saying that it brings to light the sage’s intentions. What should be accepted as correct? As for Master Shao’s Supreme Principles for Ordering the World (Huangji jingshi), earlier Confucian scholars called it unprecedented since the Book of Changes. Yet others criticize his exclusive concentration on the study of numbers, and attribute solely to Master Cheng the continuation of the interrupted succession from Confucius and Mencius. Why is this?

In history, take Dong Hu: Confucius praised him for concealing nothing, but this concerned only the affair of Zhao Dun, which the Spring and Autumn Annals recorded following his account. Surely there should be a distinction between a chief minister who fails to punish a regicide and the principal perpetrator. Why, then, was he granted no mitigation? Zhu Xi praised Sima Qian’s talent and discernment as also being outstanding. His Records of the Historian (Shiji) completely changed the method of arranging history chronologically. In establishing principles and conventions that served as a model for a hundred generations, his achievement was truly exceptional. Why, then, has he not escaped criticism? As for the Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government (Zizhi tongjian) by the Duke of Wen, Sima Guang, his sovereign declared that even Xun Yue had not attained its standard. Yet there are also those who…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
病其謬於書法而上繼獲麟絕筆之經
乃猶待於朱子何歟爾諸士淹貫經史
行將奉石渠之對紬金匱之書以尊述
作之美請發所蘊而詳舉厥中毋讓
問移風易俗爲治者之先務表正風俗亦
士君子之所以自待也玆遇諸士大比
興賢請以冀方古今風俗與諸士揚搉
之可乎夫冀方堯舜禹之故都固比屋
可封之地於變時雍之民也三代以還
===
相沿未失迨今士大夫談者猶想望其
淳朴之休玆入境觀風因民問俗乃亦
有不盡如所聞者好樂無荒見之於詩
迺今之人得無有流而爲遊惰者乎絕
地天通垂之於書迺今之人得無有背
而爲誣惑者乎漆器之造古者不以許
帝今奇異玩好之器在閭閻間有之何
也繁纓之飾古者不以易邑今鉤膺絛
革之美於從騎中見之何也禹之衣服
punctuated:
病其謬於書法，而上繼獲麟絕筆之經，乃猶待於朱子，何歟？爾諸士淹貫經史，行將奉石渠之對，紬金匱之書，以尊述作之美。請發所蘊，而詳舉厥中，毋讓。
問：移風易俗，爲治者之先務；表正風俗，亦士君子之所以自待也。玆遇諸士大比興賢，請以冀方古今風俗與諸士揚搉之，可乎？夫冀方，堯舜禹之故都，固比屋可封之地，於變時雍之民也。三代以還，相沿未失。迨今士大夫談者，猶想望其淳朴之休。玆入境觀風，因民問俗，乃亦有不盡如所聞者。好樂無荒，見之於《詩》，迺今之人得無有流而爲遊惰者乎？絕地天通，垂之於《書》，迺今之人得無有背而爲誣惑者乎？漆器之造，古者不以許帝，今奇異玩好之器，在閭閻間有之，何也？繁纓之飾，古者不以易邑，今鉤膺絛革之美，於從騎中見之，何也？禹之衣服
translation_en:
…criticize its errors in historical writing; yet a work that would carry forward the Classic whose final entry records the capture of the unicorn still had to await Master Zhu. Why was this? You scholars are thoroughly versed in the Classics and histories. Soon you will offer responses at the Stone Canal Pavilion and draw out the writings preserved in the Golden Coffer, thereby honoring the excellence of transmitting and composing. Please bring forth your accumulated learning and set out in detail the sound judgments on these matters. Do not hold back.
Question: Transforming prevailing practices and changing customs is the foremost duty of those who govern. Serving as an example to rectify customs is also what gentlemen and scholars expect of themselves. Now that you scholars have assembled for the triennial examination to select worthy men, may I discuss with you the customs of the Ji region, ancient and modern? Ji was the region of the former capitals of Yao, Shun, and Yu. It was indeed a land where every household was worthy of enfeoffment, whose people were transformed and brought into harmony. From the Three Dynasties onward, these traditions were handed down without being lost. Even today, scholar-officials who discuss the region still look with admiration toward its admirable simplicity and honesty. Yet, on entering its territory to observe its practices and inquire among its people about their customs, I have found some things that do not entirely match what I had heard. ‘Delight in pleasure without excess’ appears in the Book of Odes. Can it be that people today have drifted into idle wandering and indolence? ‘Severing communication between earth and heaven’ is handed down in the Book of Documents. Can it be that people today have turned their backs on this and engage in deception and delusion? In antiquity, even an emperor was not countenanced in making lacquer vessels. Why, then, are curious and exotic objects for amusement now found among ordinary households? In antiquity, the privilege of ornamental horse trappings was not granted even in exchange for a town. Why, then, do we now see splendid breast ornaments, braided cords, and leather trappings among mounted attendants? As for Yu’s clothing…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
可惡何謂而大袖垂衣不惜全疋尭之
土階如舊何謂而假獸刻節僭擬雕牆
然則俗漸侈靡有不可長者矣至於鄉
鄰有闘欲其立焚債劵難矣豈俗崇禮
讓之志非耶兄弟相猶欲其七葉同居
難矣豈民尚義信之紀虛耶質成之國
棄田爲閒不知今之遜畔猶昨否也爭
訟之鄉望廬而返不知今之愧罪猶昨
否也有違養而被言者較之望雲思舍
===
能無愧乎有反目而肆毒者視之鎕敬
如賔何太遠乎然則俗漸澆薄有所當
戒者矣夫俗以地成今之地固古之地
也而民以時變今之人或不如古之人
厥咎何由玆欲少變今俗盡復古道是
必責之有位者不知作爲之道如何而
可諸士子修習三物講道有年必知淳
古之盛而思所以化導於其鄉者試著
其說于篇固將以徵賢能也
punctuated:
可惡，何謂而大袖垂衣，不惜全疋？尭之土階如舊，何謂而假獸刻節，僭擬雕牆？然則俗漸侈靡，有不可長者矣。至於鄉鄰有闘，欲其立焚債劵難矣，豈俗崇禮讓之志非耶？兄弟相猶，欲其七葉同居難矣，豈民尚義信之紀虛耶？質成之國，棄田爲閒，不知今之遜畔猶昨否也？爭訟之鄉，望廬而返，不知今之愧罪猶昨否也？有違養而被言者，較之望雲思舍，能無愧乎？有反目而肆毒者，視之鎕敬如賔，何太遠乎？然則俗漸澆薄，有所當戒者矣。
夫俗以地成，今之地固古之地也；而民以時變，今之人或不如古之人。厥咎何由？玆欲少變今俗，盡復古道，是必責之有位者。不知作爲之道如何而可？諸士子修習三物，講道有年，必知淳古之盛，而思所以化導於其鄉者。試著其說于篇，固將以徵賢能也。
translation_en:
…could be coarse and plain; why, then, do people wear broad sleeves and trailing robes, thinking nothing of using whole bolts of cloth? Yao’s earthen steps remained as before; why, then, do people fashion imitation beasts and carved architectural members [?], presumptuously emulating ornamented walls? Customs are thus gradually becoming extravagant and luxurious: these tendencies must not be allowed to grow. When neighbors quarrel, it would now be difficult to expect someone immediately to burn the debt contracts. Can the accounts of local respect for ritual propriety and yielding to others be false? When brothers scheme against one another, it would be difficult to expect seven generations to live together. Can the records of the people’s esteem for righteousness and trustworthiness be empty? In the states that sought an adjudication, people relinquished farmland to leave an intervening space. We do not know whether people today yield their field boundaries as they did in the past. In the community where people disputed and litigated, they would turn back upon seeing the dwelling. We do not know whether people today feel shame for wrongdoing as they did in the past. Some are accused of failing to support their parents: compared with the man who gazed at the clouds and thought of his parents’ home, can they be without shame? Some spouses turn against each other and give free rein to malice: how far removed they are from treating one another respectfully as honored guests [?]! Customs are thus gradually becoming shallow and mean: there is cause for warning.
Customs take shape through a locality, and the land today is certainly the same land as in antiquity. Yet people change with the times, and people today may fall short of those of antiquity. What is the source of this failing? We now wish to bring some change to present customs and fully restore the ancient Way. Responsibility for this must rest with those in office. But what methods of action would accomplish it? You candidates have cultivated the three branches of instruction—virtues, conduct, and arts—and have discussed the Way for years. You must know the flourishing simplicity of antiquity and have considered how to transform and guide your own communities. Set forth your explanations in writing, so that your worthiness and ability may be assessed.

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
問夷狄爲患自古有之而制禦之方惟攻
與守乃若征戍之策昔人論之詳矣然
獨以周爲中策而上策無聞焉抑不知
所謂策之上者果何代以有之歟後又
有變其說者謂周得其上而惟漢最出
其下果信然歟洪惟我
太祖高皇帝汛掃腥羶肇造函夏百七八十年
來
列聖相承創守一致迨我
===
皇上聖文神武超越百王雖絕域窮荒罔弗效
順迺者胡虜桀黠屢犯邊隅宣大三關
連年告警至厪
九重北顧之憂向也籌邊諸臣嘗慮攻守之無
策矣仰藉
神謨睿慮遠覽無收發言盈庭羣策畢用凡所
以制禦之道者已無弗備矣然而虜心
未見以悔禍膚功未見於宣揚豈所以
爲攻守之策未得其上歟抑兵不足以
punctuated: 問：夷狄爲患，自古有之，而制禦之方，惟攻與守。乃若征戍之策，昔人論之詳矣，然獨以周爲中策，而上策無聞焉。抑不知所謂策之上者，果何代以有之歟？後又有變其說者，謂周得其上，而惟漢最出其下，果信然歟？洪惟我太祖高皇帝汛掃腥羶，肇造函夏，百七八十年來，列聖相承，創守一致。迨我皇上聖文神武，超越百王，雖絕域窮荒，罔弗效順。迺者胡虜桀黠，屢犯邊隅，宣大三關連年告警，至厪九重北顧之憂。向也籌邊諸臣，嘗慮攻守之無策矣。仰藉神謨睿慮，遠覽無收，發言盈庭，羣策畢用，凡所以制禦之道者，已無弗備矣。然而虜心未見以悔禍，膚功未見於宣揚，豈所以爲攻守之策未得其上歟？抑兵不足以
translation_en:
Question: Troubles caused by the Yi and Di peoples have existed since antiquity, and the means of restraining them consist only of attack and defense. Earlier writers discussed strategies for campaigning and garrisoning in detail. Yet they ranked the Zhou strategy only as middling, while leaving the highest strategy unmentioned. In which dynasty, then, was this supposedly highest strategy actually practiced? Later, others revised this view, claiming that Zhou attained the highest rank, while Han ranked lowest of all. Is this truly so?

We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao swept away the rank and fetid foes and founded his realm throughout the Chinese lands. For the hundred and seventy or eighty years since then, successive sage sovereigns have maintained a single purpose in founding and preserving the dynasty. Now Our Emperor, in his sagely civil accomplishments and divine martial prowess, surpasses the hundred kings. Even the remotest regions and most distant wildernesses have all offered their submission. Recently, however, the northern foes have been unruly and cunning, repeatedly invading the frontier. Xuanfu, Datong, and the Three Passes have reported alarms year after year, causing the sovereign in his palace to turn his anxious gaze northward.

Previously, the ministers planning frontier affairs worried that they lacked a strategy for attack and defense. Relying respectfully upon Your Majesty’s divine plans and sagacious deliberations, whose far-reaching vision is without limit [?], proposals have filled the court, and every counsel has been put to use. Every means of restraining the enemy has thus been fully provided. Yet the foes show no remorse for bringing calamity upon themselves, and no great achievement has emerged to be proclaimed. Could it be that our strategies for attack and defense have not attained the highest standard? Or are our troops insufficient to…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
利戰戰不足以制勝歟說者謂洪武永
樂之初九邊制嚴所守不過數處然皆
據其總會扼其要害人聚力完易以制
勝頃因門戶失守堂奧過防堡寨日多
分戍日衆編派無度調遣不宜東警西
報顧此失彼皆緣衆分則兵數寡兵寡
則取勝難其亦有見之說否歟誠欲復
國初分守之地據總會要害之區當以何地
爲重而守備在所當先何險已失而修
===
復不可無講即攻守二事而酌量之抑
又不知孰緩而孰急也子諸士生長三
晉嘗親罹其患矣試言之以觀先憂之
志
問孔子曰足食足兵民信之矣夫兵食固
爲政之大要至以之備邊禦戎則又不
可一日缺焉者也山西兵食之敝茲甚
矣顧可以置而不講耶自兵言之沿邊
諸鎮伍籍有定數其初兵本□□定也
punctuated:
利戰，戰不足以制勝歟？說者謂洪武、永樂之初，九邊制嚴，所守不過數處，然皆據其總會，扼其要害，人聚力完，易以制勝。頃因門戶失守，堂奧過防，堡寨日多，分戍日衆，編派無度，調遣不宜，東警西報，顧此失彼，皆緣衆分則兵數寡，兵寡則取勝難。其亦有見之說否歟？誠欲復國初分守之地，據總會要害之區，當以何地爲重，而守備在所當先？何險已失，而修復不可無講？即攻守二事而酌量之，抑又不知孰緩而孰急也。子諸士生長三晉，嘗親罹其患矣，試言之，以觀先憂之志。
問：孔子曰：「足食，足兵，民信之矣。」夫兵食固爲政之大要，至以之備邊禦戎，則又不可一日缺焉者也。山西兵食之敝，茲甚矣，顧可以置而不講耶？自兵言之，沿邊諸鎮伍籍有定數，其初兵本□□定也。
translation_en:
…fight to advantage, or is fighting insufficient to secure victory? Some argue that in the early Hongwu and Yongle reigns, the defensive system of the Nine Border Commands was rigorous. Only a few places were defended, but all occupied strategic junctions and controlled vital points. With men concentrated and strength intact, victory was readily secured. Recently, because the gateways have been lost and the inner chambers excessively defended, forts and stockades have multiplied daily, and troops have been dispersed among ever more garrisons. Assignments lack proper limits, and deployments are ill judged. Alarms come from the east and reports from the west; attending to one place means losing another. All this results from dispersal: when forces are divided, troop numbers at each point are small, and with few troops victory is difficult. Does this argument contain genuine insight? If we truly wish to restore the separate defensive positions of the dynasty’s founding years and occupy strategic junctions and vital areas, which places should receive the greatest weight and priority in defensive preparations? Which strategic positions have been lost whose restoration must be considered? Weighing the two undertakings of attack and defense, we still do not know which can wait and which is urgent. You scholars were born and raised in the Three Jin region and have yourselves suffered these troubles. Explain your views, so that we may see your resolve to take thought for troubles before others do.
Question: Confucius said: “Make food sufficient, make military forces sufficient, and the people will have trust.” Troops and provisions are certainly essential matters of government; when it comes to defending the frontier and resisting incursions, neither can be lacking for even a single day. The deficiencies in Shanxi’s troops and provisions are now severe. Can we simply set them aside without discussion? Speaking first of troops, the military registers of the various frontier garrisons prescribe fixed numbers. Originally, the troops were established on the basis of □□ [?]…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
然或行伍虛於姦詭之逃亡戰守病於
老幼之單弱於是始有兵不足之憂而
招民兵以代守矣是非不善也然勇敢
未獲而濫充以游手之徒則無事坐費
衣糧有事不閑紀律其可得而用之乎
自食言之輸賦濟邊餽餉有常額其初
食未始不豐也然或遣負累於豪強之
兼併辦納歛於年歲之告凶於是始有
食不足之嘆而請
===
內帑以濟艱矣是非不可也然靡費不貲而
動經以數十萬之運恐東南之財力益
匱而內外之輕重失宜其可得而常繼
乎且歲發銀兩或開納例額或挖運通
倉國用果皆羨餘之財歲調兵馬或爲
延寧或爲遼薊諸鎮果非緊急之地是
不可以通慮乎今之議者皆曰大破常
格破格之言獨施於宣大三關是果經
國之遠猷否乎茲欲求兵强食足有均
punctuated: 然或行伍虛於姦詭之逃亡，戰守病於老幼之單弱，於是始有兵不足之憂，而招民兵以代守矣。是非不善也，然勇敢未獲，而濫充以游手之徒，則無事坐費衣糧，有事不閑紀律，其可得而用之乎？自食言之，輸賦濟邊，餽餉有常額，其初食未始不豐也。然或遣負累於豪強之兼併，辦納歛於年歲之告凶，於是始有食不足之嘆，而請內帑以濟艱矣。是非不可也，然靡費不貲，而動經以數十萬之運，恐東南之財力益匱，而內外之輕重失宜，其可得而常繼乎？且歲發銀兩，或開納例額，或挖運通倉，國用果皆羨餘之財？歲調兵馬，或爲延寧，或爲遼薊，諸鎮果非緊急之地？是不可以通慮乎？今之議者皆曰大破常格，破格之言獨施於宣大三關，是果經國之遠猷否乎？茲欲求兵强食足，有均
translation_en:
… Yet the ranks may be depleted by the desertion of crafty men, while fighting and defense are impaired by the frailty of the old and the young. Only then do concerns arise over insufficient troops, and civilian militia are recruited to take over garrison duties. This is not a bad measure in itself. But if brave men are not obtained and the ranks are instead indiscriminately filled with idlers, they merely consume clothing and provisions in peacetime and are unfamiliar with military discipline when trouble comes. Can such men be put to use?

As for provisions, tax deliveries to support the frontier and shipments of military supplies have fixed quotas; initially, provisions were by no means insufficient. Yet the burdens of delivery [?] may be aggravated by the engrossment of land by powerful families, and the collection and payment of taxes constrained [?] by years of crop failure. Only then do complaints arise over insufficient provisions, and funds are requested from the imperial treasury to relieve the difficulty. This is not inadmissible in itself. But expenditure is immense, and transfers frequently run to hundreds of thousands. I fear that the financial resources of the southeast will become increasingly depleted, and that the proper balance between the needs of the court and those of the provinces will be lost. Can this support be sustained indefinitely?

Moreover, silver is disbursed every year, whether by opening authorized channels for monetary contributions or by drawing upon and transporting stocks from the granaries at Tongzhou. Are the resources used for state expenditure truly all surplus funds? Troops and horses are transferred every year, whether for Yan and Ning—that is, Yansui and Ningxia—or for Liao and Ji—that is, Liaodong and Jizhou. Are these garrisons really not places facing urgent threats? Should these matters not be considered together? Those who discuss the matter today all advocate sweeping departures from established rules. Yet their proposals for departing from the rules apply only to Xuanfu, Datong, and the Three Passes. Is this truly a far-sighted plan for governing the state? Now, if we wish to secure strong troops and ample provisions, and to establish an equitable …

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
平專一之制爲經久不易之規果有何
道乎二者之外凡禦戎之策當今之務
諸士子各盡底所見以觀經世之學將
以轉聞於
上
punctuated: 平專一之制，爲經久不易之規，果有何道乎？二者之外，凡禦戎之策、當今之務，諸士子各盡底所見，以觀經世之學，將以轉聞於上。
translation_en: …a balanced and unified system, to serve as an enduring and unchanging rule: by what means, indeed, can this be achieved? Beyond these two matters, regarding all strategies for resisting foreign incursions and the pressing affairs of the present, let each candidate fully set forth [?] his views, so that his learning in statecraft may be assessed. These views will then be conveyed to His Majesty.

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
夫子循循然善誘人博我以文約我以禮
路王道
同考試官教諭彭　批　〔循循之教正于博約見之李類多費講惟此作得之宜録以冠多士〕
同考試官教諭崔　批　〔李博約之旨至微至大惟顔子知求之是篇根極理道其亦學顔子之學者歟〕
考試官學正蔡　批　〔博約互見其意得之〕
===
考試官學正周　批　〔講有源委〕
聖人之道著於教而必以其序焉夫君子學以
致其道也知序則幾矣兹夫子所以爲善教而
顔子所以爲好學與且夫道不可以一蹴而至
教不容以凌節而施故夫子之道道之極也吾
固以其無窮盡無方體而企之也難然夫子之
教教之的也吾則見其循循然善誘人而從之
也易導其始斯以掖其終施之無所於悖而序
不可紊焉見其進必欲見其止求之無所於拂
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

夫子循循然善誘人，博我以文，約我以禮。

路王道

同考試官教諭彭　批　〔循循之教，正于博約見之。李類多費講，惟此作得之，宜録以冠多士。〕

同考試官教諭崔　批　〔李博約之旨，至微至大，惟顔子知求之。是篇根極理道，其亦學顔子之學者歟？〕

考試官學正蔡　批　〔博約互見，其意得之。〕

考試官學正周　批　〔講有源委。〕

聖人之道著於教，而必以其序焉。夫君子學以致其道也，知序則幾矣。兹夫子所以爲善教，而顔子所以爲好學與！且夫道不可以一蹴而至，教不容以凌節而施。故夫子之道，道之極也，吾固以其無窮盡、無方體而企之也難。然夫子之教，教之的也，吾則見其循循然善誘人而從之也易。導其始，斯以掖其終，施之無所於悖，而序不可紊焉；見其進，必欲見其止，求之無所於拂
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“The Master skillfully guides people forward, step by step. He broadens me through cultural learning and restrains me through ritual propriety.”

Lu Wangdao

Associate Examiner Peng, Instructor (jiaoyu), comments: 〔The teaching that proceeds step by step is precisely manifested in broadening through learning and restraining through ritual. Others of this sort [?] expend many words explaining it; this composition alone grasps it. It should be selected to head the work of the candidates.〕

Associate Examiner Cui, Instructor (jiaoyu), comments: 〔The purport of broadening and restraining [the opening character is doubtful: 李] is supremely subtle and supremely great. Only Master Yan knew to seek it. This essay probes the principles of the Way to their roots; might its author also be one who pursues the learning of Master Yan?〕

Examiner Cai, Instructor (xuezheng), comments: 〔Broadening and restraining illuminate one another: the essay grasps their meaning.〕

Examiner Zhou, Instructor (xuezheng), comments: 〔The exposition traces both source and development.〕

The Way of the sage is made manifest in his teaching, which must follow its proper sequence. The gentleman learns in order to attain that Way; if he understands the sequence, he is close to it. Is this not why the Master was skilled in teaching and Master Yan devoted to learning? Now, the Way cannot be reached in a single leap, nor may teaching be imparted by overstepping the stages. Thus the Master’s Way is the utmost realization of the Way. Because it is inexhaustible and has no fixed shape or form, I indeed find it difficult to aspire to it. Yet the Master’s teaching is the standard of teaching. Seeing how skillfully he guides people step by step, I find it easy to follow him. He guides them at the beginning so as to support them through to the end; nothing in his instruction runs counter to what is proper, and its sequence must not be confused. Seeing their progress, he is determined to see them reach their resting place; nothing in what he asks of them runs against what is fitting …

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
而功不可缺焉何則學有淺深一道也道有體
用一原也以其散殊於天下燦然有章謂之文
以其統會於吾身渾然有則謂之禮故博我以
文而爲約禮之地道之用所以行而莫非體也
約我以禮而收博文之功道之體所以立而莫
非用也自所博而馴至其極焉蓋凡古今事物
以至仰觀俯察無一而非文則亦無一而非我
之所當博者或有所蔽如徑約何夫子所以博
我者未已也而我亦將融會貫通於巨細精粗
===
之曠矣自所約而漸底於純焉蓋凡人心之固
有出於天理之同然禮即此而無外則約之在
我而無他少有所虧如徒博何夫子所以約我
者恐後也而我亦將持循固守於大中至正之
規矣吁道之難企性非莫我具也敎之易從機
非莫我殊也忽以爲易者怠畏以爲難者畫斯
顏子之所嘆乎抑惟精惟一制事制心帝王之
道猶是也春秋之季夫子以博約一貫開萬世
聖學之傳而顏曾獨得之頴悟如賜疑且信焉
punctuated: 而功不可缺焉。何則？學有淺深，一道也；道有體用，一原也。以其散殊於天下，燦然有章，謂之文；以其統會於吾身，渾然有則，謂之禮。故博我以文，而爲約禮之地，道之用所以行，而莫非體也；約我以禮，而收博文之功，道之體所以立，而莫非用也。自所博而馴至其極焉，蓋凡古今事物，以至仰觀俯察，無一而非文，則亦無一而非我之所當博者。或有所蔽，如徑約何？夫子所以博我者未已也，而我亦將融會貫通於巨細精粗之曠矣。自所約而漸底於純焉，蓋凡人心之固有，出於天理之同然，禮即此而無外，則約之在我而無他。少有所虧，如徒博何？夫子所以約我者恐後也，而我亦將持循固守於大中至正之規矣。吁！道之難企，性非莫我具也；敎之易從，機非莫我殊也。忽以爲易者怠，畏以爲難者畫，斯顏子之所嘆乎？抑惟精惟一，制事制心，帝王之道猶是也。春秋之季，夫子以博約一貫，開萬世聖學之傳，而顏曾獨得之。頴悟如賜，疑且信焉。
translation_en:
…and no part of the effort may be omitted. Why is this? Learning has shallow and profound levels, but its Way is one; the Way has substance and function, but their source is one. Dispersed in its manifold forms throughout the world, displaying a brilliant pattern, it is called cultural learning; gathered together within oneself, forming an integrated whole governed by standards, it is called ritual propriety. Thus, by broadening my learning through culture and laying the groundwork for discipline through ritual propriety, the Master enables the Way’s function to operate, and none of this is apart from its substance. By disciplining me through ritual propriety and bringing broad cultural learning to fruition, he establishes the Way’s substance, and none of this is apart from its function.

Starting from broad learning, I advance gradually to its utmost extent. All affairs and things, ancient and modern, including everything observed by looking upward and examining downward, belong to cultural learning; thus there is nothing in which I should not broaden my learning. If some obscurity remains, how could I proceed directly to discipline? The Master never ceases to broaden my learning, and I too shall integrate and comprehend the vast range of things, great and small, refined and coarse. Starting from discipline, I gradually attain purity. Everything inherent in the human heart proceeds from the principles of Heaven that all share. Ritual propriety consists precisely in this and extends no further; disciplining myself therefore rests with me and requires nothing else. If there is the slightest deficiency, what use is mere breadth of learning? The Master is anxious lest he fall behind in disciplining me, and I too shall follow and firmly uphold the standards of perfect equilibrium and utmost rectitude.

Ah! Though the Way is difficult to reach, its nature is not something I lack [?]; though the teaching is easy to follow, individual capacities are not without differences [?]. Those who slight it as easy grow idle; those who fear it as difficult set limits to their own progress. Is this what Master Yan sighed over? Moreover, being discerning and single-minded, regulating affairs and regulating the heart—the Way of the sage emperors and kings was likewise this. At the close of the Spring and Autumn period, the Master united broad learning and discipline in one thread, inaugurating the transmission of sagely learning for all ages; yet only Yan Hui and Zeng Shen fully grasped it. Even one as perceptive as Ci held doubts alongside his belief…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
豈亦聞性與天道之時乎然仁非賜所及則亦
倘於知焉爾已爲邦之問斟酌四代禮樂而克
己復禮之目直請事焉內聖外王夫子固以與
回回亦自任之矣所謂好學而庶幾乎有志於
道者當合而觀之
萬物並育而不相害道並行而不相悖小
德川流大德敦化
李希洛
同考試官教諭陳　批　天道之大最難模擬此作渾然
===
成章再無費詞宜錄以式
同考試官學正薛　批　善言天道亦善窺聖人之蘊
者
考試官學正蔡　批　文氣渾成
考試官學正周　批　詞整意足
中庸卽造化功用之妙而著其德之盛焉甚矣
造化之德之盛也于妙用焉見之矣中庸指而
言之得非卽天道以明聖人歟其意葢謂聖人
者道之會也而天地者道之原也不觀天地則
punctuated:
豈亦聞性與天道之時乎？然仁非賜所及，則亦倘於知焉爾已。爲邦之問，斟酌四代禮樂，而克己復禮之目，直請事焉。內聖外王，夫子固以與回，回亦自任之矣。所謂好學而庶幾乎！有志於道者，當合而觀之。
萬物並育而不相害，道並行而不相悖，小德川流，大德敦化。
李希洛
同考試官教諭陳，批：天道之大，最難模擬。此作渾然成章，再無費詞，宜錄以式。
同考試官學正薛，批：善言天道，亦善窺聖人之蘊者。
考試官學正蔡，批：文氣渾成。
考試官學正周，批：詞整意足。
中庸卽造化功用之妙，而著其德之盛焉。甚矣，造化之德之盛也！于妙用焉見之矣。中庸指而言之，得非卽天道以明聖人歟？其意葢謂聖人者，道之會也；而天地者，道之原也。不觀天地，則
translation_en:
… Could this also have been when he heard about human nature and the Way of Heaven? Yet benevolence lay beyond Ci’s attainment; perhaps he approached it only in understanding [?]. In his question about governing a state, the rites and music of the four dynasties were weighed and considered; as for the particulars of overcoming oneself and returning to ritual propriety, he directly asked to put them into practice. To be inwardly a sage and outwardly a king: the Master certainly credited Hui with this capacity, and Hui also accepted it as his own responsibility. This is what is meant by loving learning and coming close to the Way! Those who aspire to the Way should consider these passages together.
“All things are nourished together without harming one another; their ways proceed together without conflicting. Lesser virtue flows like rivers; greater virtue brings forth abundant transformation.”
Li Xiluo.
Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “The greatness of the Way of Heaven is exceedingly difficult to depict. This composition forms a seamless whole, without a single superfluous phrase. It should be recorded as a model.”
Associate Examiner Xue, Instructor, comments: “One who speaks well of the Way of Heaven and also penetrates well into the sage’s profound inner understanding.”
Examiner Cai, Instructor, comments: “The writing’s spirit forms a seamless whole.”
Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: “The language is orderly and the meaning fully expressed.”
The Doctrine of the Mean takes the wondrous workings of creation and transformation to reveal the abundance of its virtue. How abundant indeed is the virtue of creation and transformation! It is visible in these wondrous workings. When the Doctrine of the Mean points this out and speaks of it, is it not using the Way of Heaven to illuminate the sage? Its meaning is, presumably, that the sage is where the Way converges, while Heaven and Earth are the source of the Way. If one does not observe Heaven and Earth, then …

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
無以見聖人矣天地之道何如彼天之覆焉地
之載焉萬物固群然並育于其間矣群則易至
于亂而戕也然本乎天者親上而各足其蕃息
之願本乎地者親下而咸若其滋長之休大以
成大小以成小何相害之有乎四時運焉日月
麗焉斯道固紛然並行于其中矣紛則易至于
背而馳也然寒極而暑生相禪不已日升而月
沉相代無窮明以生明歲以成歲何相悖之有
乎若此者抑何以致之哉蓋天地之道以其一
===
體而散殊于兩間則謂之小德是故太極判而
爲陰陽陰陽判而爲五行萬物各一其性也四
時各一其氣也日月各一其度也蓋浩乎川流
脉絡分明而往不息矣此其所以不害不悖者
乎否則物有雜揉道有變動而何以若是哉天
地之道以其萬殊而統會于一本則謂之大德
是故五行一陰陽陰陽一太極妙合而凝者萬
物之命也互爲其根者四時之序也互藏其宅
者二曜之精也蓋淵乎敦化根本盛大而出無
punctuated: 無以見聖人矣。天地之道何如？彼天之覆焉，地之載焉，萬物固群然並育于其間矣。群則易至于亂而戕也，然本乎天者親上，而各足其蕃息之願；本乎地者親下，而咸若其滋長之休。大以成大，小以成小，何相害之有乎？四時運焉，日月麗焉，斯道固紛然並行于其中矣。紛則易至于背而馳也，然寒極而暑生，相禪不已；日升而月沉，相代無窮。明以生明，歲以成歲，何相悖之有乎？若此者，抑何以致之哉？蓋天地之道，以其一體而散殊于兩間，則謂之小德。是故太極判而爲陰陽，陰陽判而爲五行。萬物各一其性也，四時各一其氣也，日月各一其度也。蓋浩乎川流，脉絡分明而往不息矣。此其所以不害不悖者乎？否則物有雜揉，道有變動，而何以若是哉？天地之道，以其萬殊而統會于一本，則謂之大德。是故五行一陰陽，陰陽一太極。妙合而凝者，萬物之命也；互爲其根者，四時之序也；互藏其宅者，二曜之精也。蓋淵乎敦化，根本盛大而出無
translation_en:
…there would be no way to comprehend the sage. What is the Way of Heaven and Earth like? Heaven covers all above, and Earth bears all below; the myriad things indeed grow together in their midst. When things gather, they readily fall into disorder and injure one another. Yet those rooted in Heaven cleave to what is above, each fulfilling its desire to multiply; those rooted in Earth cleave to what is below, all enjoying the blessings of growth. The great attain their greatness, and the small their smallness: how could they harm one another? The four seasons revolve, and the sun and moon shine; the many workings of this Way indeed proceed together within them. Amid such multiplicity, they readily diverge and run counter to one another. Yet when cold reaches its extreme, heat arises, and they succeed one another without cease; the sun rises and the moon sinks, and they alternate without end. Light follows light, and year completes year: how could they conflict with one another? How, then, is this brought about?

When the Way of Heaven and Earth disperses from its single substance into distinct manifestations between Heaven and Earth, it is called the lesser virtue. Thus the Supreme Ultimate divides into yin and yang, and yin and yang divide into the Five Phases. Each of the myriad things has its own nature; each of the four seasons has its own vital energy; and the sun and moon each have their own course. Vastly they flow like rivers, their channels clearly distinguished, proceeding without cease. Is this not why they neither harm nor conflict with one another? Otherwise, with things intermingling and the Way undergoing change, how could it be so?

When the myriad distinctions of the Way of Heaven and Earth are gathered together into a single root, it is called the greater virtue. Thus the Five Phases are one yin and yang, and yin and yang are one Supreme Ultimate. Wondrous union and condensation constitute the life-endowment of the myriad things; each being the root of the other constitutes the sequence of the four seasons; each harboring the other within its dwelling constitutes the vital essence of the two luminaries. Profound indeed is this abundant transforming power: its root is flourishing and great, and what issues from it is without…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
窮矣此其所以並育並行者乎否則物無盡藏
道無紀極而何以若是哉是則大德以爲本一
故神也即夫子之一理渾然也小德以爲用兩
故化也即夫子之泛應曲當也非天地不足以
擬聖人非聖人亦何以配天地哉蓋天地無言
之聖人聖人有爲之天地也仲尼配天吾無間
然矣獨惜夫世之言天者語小而忘大語聖者
尊天而卑人是尚爲能至道也乎雖然聖人不
可及已成章後達學者有定法焉循其序則聖
===
人可至而天者可幾矣噫此固子思子憂道之
微意也
資之深則取之左右逢其原
王銳
同考試官教諭何　批〔論理之文辭不煩而意盡真深〕
造自得之學者
考試官學正蔡　批〔文不爲題窘善言理者〕
考試官學正周　批〔體認真切〕
豫內而利外君子盡心之學也蓋合內外而無
punctuated:
窮矣。此其所以並育並行者乎？否則物無盡藏，道無紀極，而何以若是哉？是則大德以爲本，一故神也，即夫子之一理渾然也；小德以爲用，兩故化也，即夫子之泛應曲當也。非天地不足以擬聖人，非聖人亦何以配天地哉？蓋天地，無言之聖人；聖人，有爲之天地也。仲尼配天，吾無間然矣。獨惜夫世之言天者，語小而忘大；語聖者，尊天而卑人。是尚爲能至道也乎？雖然，聖人不可及已，成章後達，學者有定法焉。循其序，則聖人可至，而天者可幾矣。噫！此固子思子憂道之微意也。

資之深，則取之左右逢其原。
王銳。
同考試官教諭何批〔論理之文，辭不煩而意盡，真深〕造自得之學者。
考試官學正蔡批〔文不爲題窘，善言理者。〕
考試官學正周批〔體認真切。〕

豫內而利外，君子盡心之學也。蓋合內外而無
translation_en:
…without end. Is this not why things are nourished together and courses proceed together? Otherwise, things would constitute an inexhaustible profusion and the Way would have no governing bounds: how could they be thus? Thus the great virtue constitutes the foundation: being one, it is numinous. This is precisely the Master's single principle in its undivided wholeness. The lesser virtues constitute its functioning: being two, they bring about transformation. This is precisely the Master's responsiveness to everything, fitting each particular circumstance. Nothing short of Heaven and Earth suffices as an analogy for the sage; and who but the sage could match Heaven and Earth? Heaven and Earth are a sage without speech; the sage is Heaven and Earth in action. That Zhongni matches Heaven admits, in my view, of no objection. I regret only that those in the world who speak of Heaven discuss the small and forget the great, while those who speak of the sage exalt Heaven and demean humanity. Can this still be called attaining the Way? Nevertheless, though the sage may seem beyond reach, learners have a fixed method: complete each stage before advancing. Following this sequence, one can attain sagehood and approach Heaven. Ah! This is indeed the subtle intent behind Master Zisi's concern for the Way.

“When one draws deeply upon it, one finds its source wherever one turns.”
Wang Rui.
Associate Examiner He, Instructor, comments: “〔An essay expounding principle: its language is concise, yet its meaning is fully expressed. Truly one who deeply〕 advances in learning and grasps it for himself.”
Examiner Cai, School Instructor, comments: “〔The essay is not constrained by the topic; its author is skilled at discussing principle.〕”
Examiner Zhou, School Instructor, comments: “〔His personal understanding is genuine and precise.〕”

To be prepared within and effective without is the learning by which the gentleman fully realizes his mind. For the unity of inner and outer, without …

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
間者人心本然之體也君子所以盡其心亦養
識自致而已矣孟子極言其妙如此若謂君子
之學所貴乎自得者求之之心焉爾夫既深造以
道至於自得而居之安矣資之有不深乎夫資
之深者非取諸彼以益其所無也道本至足湛
而一者適充其量非求在外以強其所難也理
本至順靜而虛者斯會其全立天下之有以統
夫性神明所蘊形氣不得而窒焉敎天下之動
以統夫情天機所藏見聞不得而梏焉此其積
===
之也厚而不窮天下之至精由是以立則其發
之也裕而不匱天下之至變由是以通理自內
而資於事一本之所以萬殊特寂感之交耳奚
事於他求左之右之近取諸身而順應之矣事
自外而資乎理萬殊之所以一本特通復之間
耳何有於襲取取之左右不離乎心而時出之
矣吾心其猶源乎混混而有本矣乎日用其猶
委乎沛然而莫禦矣乎吁自得之妙有如此者
君子亦復其心之本體而已矣雖然豈易及哉
punctuated: 間者，人心本然之體也。君子所以盡其心，亦養識自致而已矣。孟子極言其妙如此。若謂君子之學所貴乎自得者，求之之心焉爾。夫既深造以道，至於自得，而居之安矣，資之有不深乎？夫資之深者，非取諸彼以益其所無也。道本至足，湛而一者適充其量；非求在外以強其所難也。理本至順，靜而虛者斯會其全。立天下之有以統夫性，神明所蘊，形氣不得而窒焉；敎天下之動以統夫情，天機所藏，見聞不得而梏焉。此其積之也厚而不窮，天下之至精由是以立；則其發之也裕而不匱，天下之至變由是以通。理自內而資於事，一本之所以萬殊，特寂感之交耳，奚事於他求？左之右之，近取諸身而順應之矣。事自外而資乎理，萬殊之所以一本，特通復之間耳，何有於襲取？取之左右，不離乎心而時出之矣。吾心其猶源乎，混混而有本矣乎！日用其猶委乎，沛然而莫禦矣乎！吁！自得之妙有如此者，君子亦復其心之本體而已矣。雖然，豈易及哉？
translation_en: …without division: this is the original constitution of the human mind. The gentleman fully realizes his mind simply by nurturing understanding [?] and attaining this for himself. Mencius thus describes its subtle wonder to the utmost. It is as though he were saying that what makes personal realization precious in the gentleman’s learning is simply the mind that seeks it. Once he has pursued his studies deeply in accordance with the Way, reached personal realization, and dwells securely in it, how could the resources he draws upon fail to be deep? Drawing deeply upon these resources does not mean taking something from elsewhere to supply what he lacks. The Way is inherently complete; one who is clear and undivided simply fulfills his capacity. Nor does it mean seeking externally to force what is difficult for him. Principle is inherently harmonious; one who is still and empty thereby comprehends it in its entirety. He establishes all that exists under Heaven so as to bring it together under human nature: the spiritual illumination contained within cannot be obstructed by bodily form and vital energy. He teaches all movement under Heaven [?] so as to bring it together under the feelings: the workings of Heaven stored within cannot be fettered by what is seen and heard. Thus his accumulation is ample and inexhaustible, and through it the utmost refinement of all under Heaven is established. His expression of it is consequently abundant and unfailing, and through it the utmost transformations of all under Heaven proceed freely. Principle comes from within and supplies resources for affairs. The way the single root becomes myriad distinctions is simply the interplay of stillness and response. Why seek elsewhere? Turning left or right, he draws upon what is close at hand in his own person and responds fittingly. Affairs come from without and draw upon principle. The way myriad distinctions share a single root lies simply in the passage between outward extension and return. What place is there for borrowing from others? Drawing upon it to left and right, he never departs from the mind, but brings it forth as circumstances require. Is not my mind like a spring, flowing ceaselessly because it has a source? Is not daily practice like its downstream flow, surging forth irresistibly? Ah! Such is the subtle wonder of personal realization. The gentleman simply restores the original constitution of his mind. Yet how could this be easy to attain?

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
一神兩化天之所以爲天也窮神知化聖之所
以爲聖也神不可致思化不可助長則深造以
道之極功也是故一理渾然泛應曲當者孔子
也集義養氣勿正勿助以不動其心則孟子願
學孔子而敘其所自得也噫計功謀利見小欲
速不知心體爲何物者又不獨告子而已易不
云乎精義入神以致用也利用安身以崇德也
蓋内外交相養也夫然後可以希聖夫然後可
以同天
===
易
直其正也方其義也君子敬以直内義以
方外
李希洛
同考試官教諭陳　批　〔敬自直義自方緩言之則非惟〕
此作得之
同考試官學正薛　批　〔夫子即坤道而發明心學道統〕
在是此篇似能窺其旨者
考試官學正蔡　批　〔發心學明切〕
punctuated:
一神兩化，天之所以爲天也；窮神知化，聖之所以爲聖也。神不可致思，化不可助長，則深造以道之極功也。是故一理渾然，泛應曲當者，孔子也；集義養氣，勿正勿助，以不動其心，則孟子願學孔子而敘其所自得也。噫！計功謀利，見小欲速，不知心體爲何物者，又不獨告子而已。《易》不云乎：「精義入神，以致用也；利用安身，以崇德也。」蓋内外交相養也。夫然後可以希聖，夫然後可以同天。

易
直，其正也；方，其義也。君子敬以直内，義以方外。
李希洛

同考試官教諭陳批：〔敬自直，義自方，緩言之則非惟〕此作得之。
同考試官學正薛批：〔夫子即坤道而發明心學道統〕在是，此篇似能窺其旨者。
考試官學正蔡批：〔發心學明切〕
translation_en:
The single numinous power and its twofold transformation are what make Heaven Heaven; fathoming that power and knowing transformation are what make the sage a sage. The numinous cannot be reached through deliberate thought, nor can transformation be helped along: this is the ultimate achievement of advancing deeply through the Way. Thus it was Confucius whose single, integrated principle enabled him to respond to all things with exact appropriateness. As for accumulating righteousness and nourishing vital energy, neither anticipating results nor assisting its growth, thereby keeping the mind unmoved—this was Mencius, aspiring to learn from Confucius, describing what he had attained for himself. Alas! Those who calculate achievements and seek profit, attend to petty things and desire quick results, and do not know what the original constitution of the mind is, are by no means limited to Gaozi. Does not the Book of Changes say: “Refining righteousness until one enters the numinous serves to bring it into practical use; making use beneficial and settling oneself serves to exalt virtue”? The inner and outer thus nourish each other. Only then can one aspire to sagehood; only then can one become one with Heaven.

Book of Changes
“Straightness is its correctness; squareness is its righteousness. The noble man uses reverence to straighten himself within and righteousness to square himself without.”
By Li Xiluo.

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: 〔“Reverence naturally brings straightness; righteousness naturally brings squareness. To speak of this loosely is not merely … [?]”〕 This essay grasps it.

Comment by Associate Examiner Xue, School Instructor: 〔“The Master elucidates the learning of the mind through the Way of Kun; the orthodox transmission of the Way”〕 lies here. This essay seems able to discern his intent.

Comment by Examiner Cai, School Instructor: 〔“The exposition of the learning of the mind is clear and precise.”〕

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正周　批〔是嘗盡心於內者〕
至德具於人心而君子學以成之焉夫人心之
體用直方具矣是故君子安內制外不可無學
也文言申坤六二爻之義若曰直方之德惟坤
有之惟六二得之也然豈外於人心者哉彼所
謂直者非有他也其人心本體之正也真性中
存知覺與俱而未發無欲而靜有主而虛也太
宇寧一未嘗向於一偏何私曲乎故直即此之
謂也所謂方者亦非有他也其人心裁制之義
===
也運量在我機括有感而遂通稱物而平順事
而恕也權度精切蓋將妙於泛應何弗齊乎故
方即此之謂也夫至德之具既不假於外求君
子之學知有在於交養且正無作爲之功而敬
可守也於焉尊其德性而夙夜惟寅不忘一念
於操持穎悟明命而時幾皆勅無容雜慮之妄
作由是莊敬強而收斂定神明得以固其靈主
一專而性情合物欲不得淆其靜無所於回而
亦無所於罔也內其自直矣乎義有可審之幾
punctuated:
考試官學正周，批〔是嘗盡心於內者〕。

至德具於人心，而君子學以成之焉。夫人心之體用，直方具矣。是故君子安內制外，不可無學也。《文言》申坤六二爻之義，若曰：直方之德，惟坤有之，惟六二得之也。然豈外於人心者哉？彼所謂直者，非有他也，其人心本體之正也。真性中存，知覺與俱，而未發無欲而靜，有主而虛也。太宇寧一，未嘗向於一偏，何私曲乎？故直即此之謂也。所謂方者，亦非有他也，其人心裁制之義也。運量在我，機括有感而遂通，稱物而平，順事而恕也。權度精切，蓋將妙於泛應，何弗齊乎？故方即此之謂也。夫至德之具，既不假於外求，君子之學，知有在於交養。且正無作爲之功，而敬可守也。於焉尊其德性，而夙夜惟寅，不忘一念於操持；穎悟明命，而時幾皆勅，無容雜慮之妄作。由是莊敬強而收斂定，神明得以固其靈；主一專而性情合，物欲不得淆其靜。無所於回，而亦無所於罔也，內其自直矣乎？義有可審之幾，
translation_en:
Examiner Zhou, School Instructor, comments: 〔This is someone who has devoted his utmost effort to the inner life.〕

Perfect virtue is inherent in the human heart, and the gentleman brings it to completion through learning. In both the substance and the functioning of the heart, straightness and squareness are already present. Thus, to bring peace within and regulate his conduct without, the gentleman cannot dispense with learning. The Commentary on the Words of the Text elaborates the meaning of the second, yin line of Kun, as though saying: the virtues of straightness and squareness belong to Kun, and its second, yin line embodies them. Yet could these lie outside the human heart? What is called straightness is nothing other than the rectitude of the heart’s original substance. The true nature abides within, accompanied by awareness; before it is aroused, it is still and free of desire, empty yet governed by a master. Its vast inner realm is tranquil and unified, never inclining to one side: what selfishness or crookedness could there be? This, then, is what straightness means. What is called squareness is likewise nothing other than the righteousness by which the heart judges and regulates. Deliberation and assessment lie within oneself; the heart’s mechanism, when stimulated, responds comprehensively, weighing things impartially and accommodating affairs with sympathetic understanding. Its weighing and measuring are exact and discerning, enabling it to respond with consummate skill to every circumstance: what could fail to be properly ordered? This, then, is what squareness means.

Since the possession of perfect virtue does not depend upon seeking it outside oneself, the gentleman knows that learning consists in nurturing these two aspects together. Rectitude requires no contrived effort, but can be preserved through reverent attentiveness. Thus he honors his virtuous nature, remaining reverent morning and night, never neglecting for a single thought to hold fast to it. He keenly apprehends Heaven’s luminous mandate and exercises vigilance at every incipient moment, allowing no distracting thoughts to arise recklessly. Through this, solemn reverence grows strong and inward concentration becomes settled, so that the heart’s spiritual awareness can preserve its numinous efficacy. Concentration on the One becomes undivided, and nature and feelings accord, so that material desires cannot disturb its stillness. There is neither deviation nor delusion: will the inner life not thereby become straight of itself? In righteousness there are incipient stirrings that can be examined…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
而用則行也於焉隨事而觀會通小大有定辯
決協順應之常因時而象物宜行止由之斟酌
盡化裁之變忠是參伍之不失則舉庶物而得
其情錯綜之有制則總百爲而括於度無所不
當而亦無所不一也外其自方矣乎是則合内
外而學始全兼體用而德乃大其又有疑其所
行者哉言學於六二深矣抑非夫子始言之湯
武身之用是道也以義制事以禮制心敬怠義
欲之旨昭昭也雖然極言之虞廷之意猶是也
===
而其傳遠矣孔門諸子有得而論著不外是也
而其説長矣後之爲定性書而每教人静坐着
其亦聖人之徒與論學者不迷於所從可也
文也者效天下之動者也
衛　心
同考試官教諭陳　批　諸作者類似推由此篇發得效
字義出録之
同考試官學正薛　批　文辭發揮人事所以前民用
正在此是篇又能發揮文辭者高薦高薦
punctuated:
而用則行也。於焉隨事而觀會通，小大有定，辯決協順應之常；因時而象物宜，行止由之，斟酌盡化裁之變。忠是參伍之不失，則舉庶物而得其情；錯綜之有制，則總百爲而括於度。無所不當，而亦無所不一也，外其自方矣乎！是則合内外而學始全，兼體用而德乃大，其又有疑其所行者哉？言學於六二深矣！抑非夫子始言之，湯武身之，用是道也。以義制事，以禮制心，敬怠義欲之旨昭昭也。雖然，極言之，虞廷之意猶是也，而其傳遠矣。孔門諸子有得而論著，不外是也，而其説長矣。後之爲定性書而每教人静坐着，其亦聖人之徒與？論學者不迷於所從可也。

文也者，效天下之動者也。
衛心

同考試官教諭陳批：諸作者類似，推由此篇發得效字義出，録之。

同考試官學正薛批：文辭發揮人事，所以前民用正在此。是篇又能發揮文辭者，高薦，高薦！
translation_en:
…and when put into practice, it proceeds. Thus, following each affair, one observes its connections and interrelations. Matters great and small have their proper determinations, and discrimination and decision accord with the constant principles of appropriate response. Adapting to the time, one models oneself on what is fitting for things; action and withdrawal follow from this, and careful deliberation fully encompasses the changing adjustments of transformation. Through unfailing comparison and cross-checking [?], one grasps the true circumstances of all things; through systematic interweaving, one gathers the hundred activities within their proper bounds. Nothing is inappropriate, and nothing lacks unity: will one’s outward conduct not thereby become square? Only by uniting the inner and outer does learning become complete; only by encompassing substance and function does virtue become great. Could one then have doubts about one’s actions? Profound indeed is the teaching on learning in the second yin line! Yet the Master was not the first to speak of it: Tang and Wu embodied it, employing this Way. “Regulate affairs through righteousness; regulate the mind through ritual propriety”: the meaning of reverence and negligence, righteousness and desire, is perfectly clear. Indeed, tracing the matter to its furthest source, the intent of the court of Shun was likewise this, and its transmission reaches far back. What the disciples of Confucius apprehended and set forth in their writings did not go beyond this, and their exposition was extensive. Was the later author of the Letter on Settling the Nature, who repeatedly taught people to sit quietly [?], not also a follower of the sages? Those who discuss learning need only avoid confusion about what they should follow.

“Writings are that which models the movements of all under Heaven.”
By Wei Xin.

Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “The other compositions are much alike. On consideration, this essay brings out the meaning of the word ‘models’; I have selected it for inclusion.”

Associate Examiner Xue, Instructor, comments: “The wording elucidates human affairs: precisely herein lies its capacity to guide the people’s practical activity. This essay, in turn, succeeds in elucidating that wording. Highly recommended, highly recommended!”

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正蔡　批　是玩辭有得者
考試官學正周　批　語意雋永可以言學易矣
大傳發爻辭之蘊一天下之至變焉蓋天下之
變動無窮而爻之所具猶是也是固切於前民
用者乎大傳原卦爻之所具以推占筮之由顯
其意以為昔者聖人之作易也固將以前斯民
之用也而易之所以作者亦因民用之自然而
已且彖以言材周公謂其情偽盡而統體未分
是必爻焉有文然後事物該而待虛不匱於是
===
有文辭之係焉於剛柔之雜居而發揮以彰其
蘊於陰陽之異位而擬議以盡其詳所以然者
是豈外天下之動而為言耶誠以天下之動一
爻百慮其貞勝固無乎常形而會通典禮其至
賾皆可以示教故爻也者非他也稱名取類發
揮於剛柔者無非事變之紛紜彰往察來擬議
於陰陽者要皆物理之散見靜躁殊途動固無
定用也然物宜昭其象文辭體其撰所以示典
常以指險易者雜而不越何莫而非用之所在
punctuated:
考試官學正蔡　批：是玩辭有得者。
考試官學正周　批：語意雋永，可以言學易矣。
大傳發爻辭之蘊，一天下之至變焉。蓋天下之變動無窮，而爻之所具猶是也，是固切於前民用者乎！大傳原卦爻之所具，以推占筮之由，顯其意以為：昔者聖人之作易也，固將以前斯民之用也，而易之所以作者，亦因民用之自然而已。且彖以言材，周公謂其情偽盡而統體未分，是必爻焉有文，然後事物該而待虛不匱。於是有文辭之係焉，於剛柔之雜居而發揮以彰其蘊，於陰陽之異位而擬議以盡其詳。所以然者，是豈外天下之動而為言耶？誠以天下之動，一爻百慮，其貞勝固無乎常形，而會通典禮，其至賾皆可以示教。故爻也者，非他也，稱名取類，發揮於剛柔者，無非事變之紛紜；彰往察來，擬議於陰陽者，要皆物理之散見。靜躁殊途，動固無定用也，然物宜昭其象，文辭體其撰，所以示典常以指險易者，雜而不越，何莫而非用之所在
translation_en:
Examiner Cai, Director of Education, comments: “This is someone who has gained understanding by pondering the wording.”
Examiner Zhou, Director of Education, comments: “The language and meaning reward prolonged reflection. One may indeed speak of this as studying the Changes.”
The Great Commentary brings out the profundities of the line statements, unifying the utmost transformations of all under Heaven. The changes and movements of the world are inexhaustible, yet what the lines encompass remains just this. Is this not indeed closely concerned with guiding the people in their practical affairs? The Great Commentary traces what the hexagrams and lines encompass in order to explain the grounds for divination by milfoil, making its intention clear: when the sages of antiquity composed the Changes, they certainly intended to guide the people in their practical affairs; yet their composition of the Changes merely followed the natural course of those affairs.
Moreover, the hexagram judgments speak of inherent qualities. The Duke of Zhou considered that they exhausted what was genuine and false, but that the whole had not yet been differentiated. The lines therefore had to possess written statements; only then could affairs and things be comprehensively included, with an inexhaustible capacity to await what was as yet unfilled [?]. Thus verbal statements were attached: they elaborated upon the intermingling of firm and yielding lines to reveal their implications, and made comparisons and deliberated upon the different positions of yin and yang to exhaust their particulars. Why was this so? Could these statements possibly have been made apart from the movements of the world?
Indeed, in the movements of the world, a single line admits a hundred considerations. Their prevailing constancy has no fixed form; yet, through comprehensive understanding and the norms of ritual, even their deepest intricacies can serve as instruction. Thus the lines are nothing other than this: naming things and selecting analogous categories, what they elucidate through the firm and yielding is invariably the manifold complexity of changing affairs; revealing the past and discerning the future, what they compare and deliberate upon through yin and yang is, in essence, the principles of things appearing in diverse manifestations.
Stillness and agitation follow different paths, and movement certainly has no fixed application. Yet the appropriate dispositions of things make their images manifest, and the verbal statements embody their configurations. In showing constant norms and indicating danger and ease, they encompass variety without overstepping their bounds. What among them is not a locus of practical application…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
耶險夷異遇動固無定時也然法象淺其秘時
物順其情所以明憂患以決趨避者事肆而隱
何莫而非時之所措耶雜物撰德非中爻不備
爻而初辭擬之者先事而開其端者也承乘比
應以其至一者充之以至不一天下之能事畢
矣辯是與非亦非中爻不備矣而卒成之終者
即物而究其歸者也遠近愛惡以其所相類者
而錯之以所不類言乎天地之間備矣是爻之
係也聞乎天下者也而爻之所係者放乎天下
===
者也事該而情異此吉凶悔吝之所由以出也
雖然爻也者文也動也者迹也所以超於是而
妙其用焉者道也故先天立象以盡意不泥文
也後天立言以盡變不泥迹也君子學易以獲
天玩乎文而不滯於文博乎迹而不拘於迹也
不然外道而徒於爻焉動焉求之吾恐精微晦
而典禮荒文也迹也皆物也如妙用何
書
好生之德洽于民心
punctuated:
耶？險夷異遇，動固無定時也。然法象淺其秘，時物順其情，所以明憂患以決趨避者，事肆而隱，何莫而非時之所措耶？雜物撰德，非中爻不備。爻而初辭擬之者，先事而開其端者也。承乘比應，以其至一者充之以至不一，天下之能事畢矣。辯是與非，亦非中爻不備矣。而卒成之終者，即物而究其歸者也。遠近愛惡，以其所相類者而錯之以所不類，言乎天地之間備矣。是爻之係也，聞乎天下者也；而爻之所係者，放乎天下者也。事該而情異，此吉凶悔吝之所由以出也。雖然，爻也者，文也；動也者，迹也。所以超於是而妙其用焉者，道也。故先天立象以盡意，不泥文也；後天立言以盡變，不泥迹也。君子學易以獲天，玩乎文而不滯於文，博乎迹而不拘於迹也。不然，外道而徒於爻焉、動焉求之，吾恐精微晦而典禮荒。文也、迹也，皆物也，如妙用何？
書
好生之德洽于民心
translation_en:
…is it not? Encounters with danger and ease differ, and activity certainly has no fixed time. Yet the patterns and images make their secrets accessible, and the circumstances of the time accord with their true conditions. In clarifying anxieties and troubles so that one can decide what to pursue and what to avoid, affairs are displayed, yet their meaning remains hidden. How could any of this fail to be an appropriate response to its time? To bring together diverse things and set forth their qualities requires the middle lines for completeness. As for the lines and the initial statements that formulate them [?], these anticipate affairs and disclose their beginnings. Through the relationships of supporting, riding upon, adjacency, and correspondence, what is supremely unified is extended to encompass what is utterly diverse, and all that can be accomplished under Heaven is fully comprehended. Distinguishing right from wrong likewise requires the middle lines for completeness. What finally brings the conclusion to completion follows things through and investigates their ultimate outcome. Through distance and proximity, love and aversion, what is alike is intermingled with what is unlike, and everything between Heaven and Earth is fully expressed. Thus the statements attached to the lines are made known throughout the world, while what those statements concern extends throughout the world. Affairs are comprehensively embraced, but their circumstances differ: from this arise good fortune and misfortune, regret and humiliation. Nevertheless, the lines are textual forms, and activities are outward traces. What transcends these and makes their operation wondrous is the Way. Thus, preceding Heaven, images are established to express meaning fully, without becoming mired in textual forms; following Heaven, words are established to express change fully, without becoming mired in outward traces. The gentleman studies the Changes to apprehend Heaven. He contemplates its textual forms without becoming entangled in them and acquires broad knowledge of its traces without being confined by them. Otherwise, if one sets aside the Way and seeks only among the lines and activities, I fear that subtle principles will become obscured and established rites neglected. Textual forms and outward traces are both mere things: how could they suffice for wondrous operation?
