The person is one and the same, yet whether one acts for oneself or for other beings determines the distinction between public concern and private interest. Upon this depend smallness and greatness, nobility and baseness, preservation and destruction. Can those who understand benevolence fail to distinguish these?
The sage’s feeling of love for his own person is the same as that of ordinary people. He extends the love he bears himself to all embodied beings under Heaven; hence his benevolence is broad. Ordinary people’s feeling of love for their own persons is likewise the same as the sage’s. Yet through their self-love they harm all embodied beings under Heaven; hence their hearts are cruel. To love oneself and extend this love to all under Heaven is what is meant by taking all under Heaven as one’s own person. Among the myriad kinds and forms of beings, inseparable from one’s concern, none fails to benefit from this. To harm all under Heaven out of self-love is what is meant by abandoning one’s own person. In the end, even if one’s hands and feet become weak and numb, one will no longer be aware of it. What could be more lacking in benevolence? Such a person is an offender against the sages.
Someone asks: “Acting for oneself is wrong, then. But is someone without love benevolent?” The reply is: “A person of Chu who pays no heed to whether a person of Qin is well fed or emaciated certainly offers nothing to commend as benevolence. One who does not love his own parents but loves other people is said by the gentleman to violate virtue. Thus benevolence has a capacity that must be fully developed; benevolence also has distinctions that must be discerned.” Mengzi said: “Treat your kin with affection and extend benevolence to the people; extend benevolence to the people and love to other beings.”

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
言仁精矣然則何從求乎夫子告子貢曰能近
取譬可謂仁之方也已
表
擬宋以范仲淹叅知政事富弼爲樞密副
使謝表〔慶曆三年〕
衛心
同考試官教諭陳　批〔立意措詞皆有家數且陳述各〕
〔相將職守整嚴忠藎之志見于言表宜錄以式〕
同考試官學正薛　批〔陳謝之言恪寓忠愛之意亦燦〕
===
〔于典故者錄之〕
考試官學正蔡　批〔駢儷得體〕
考試官學正周　批〔典則可式〕
慶曆三年〔某〕月〔某〕日具官〔臣〕范〔仲淹〕〔臣〕富
〔弼〕伏蒙
聖恩以〔臣仲淹〕叅知政事〔臣弼〕爲樞密副使者
玉鼎分調爕理與鈞衡之寄
金符並宥謀謨贊帷幄之籌同時晉貳於元
寮異數咸超夫凡格責均任重義激
punctuated:
言仁精矣！然則何從求乎？夫子告子貢曰：「能近取譬，可謂仁之方也已。」

表
擬宋以范仲淹叅知政事、富弼爲樞密副使謝表〔慶曆三年〕
衛心
同考試官教諭陳批〔立意措詞皆有家數且陳述各〕〔相將職守整嚴忠藎之志見于言表宜錄以式〕
同考試官學正薛批〔陳謝之言恪寓忠愛之意亦燦〕〔于典故者錄之〕
考試官學正蔡批〔駢儷得體〕
考試官學正周批〔典則可式〕

慶曆三年〔某〕月〔某〕日，具官〔臣〕范〔仲淹〕、〔臣〕富〔弼〕伏蒙聖恩，以〔臣仲淹〕叅知政事、〔臣弼〕爲樞密副使者。玉鼎分調，爕理與鈞衡之寄；金符並宥，謀謨贊帷幄之籌。同時晉貳於元寮，異數咸超夫凡格。責均任重，義激
translation_en:
…These words express benevolence with precision! Where, then, should one seek it? The Master told Zigong: “To be able to draw an analogy from what is near at hand may be called the method of benevolence.”

Memorial
A thank-you memorial composed in the persons of Fan Zhongyan and Fu Bi upon their appointment under the Song as Vice Administrator and Vice Military Affairs Commissioner, respectively. 〔Third year of Qingli [1043].〕
By Wei Xin.

Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: 〔Both the conception and the wording show mastery of established methods. The account of the respective duties of chief councillor and military commander is orderly and rigorous. The resolve to serve with loyalty and devotion is evident beyond the words themselves. It should be selected as a model.〕
Associate Examiner Xue, School Instructor, comments: 〔The words expressing thanks respectfully convey loyalty and affection for the sovereign; they are also resplendent with historical allusions. Select it.〕
Examiner Cai, School Instructor, comments: 〔The parallel prose is appropriate in form.〕
Examiner Zhou, School Instructor, comments: 〔Classical and well regulated: worthy to serve as a model.〕

On the 〔specified〕 day of the 〔specified〕 month in the third year of Qingli, 〔your servants〕 Fan 〔Zhongyan〕 and Fu 〔Bi〕, holding the duly stated offices, humbly received Your Majesty’s gracious favor appointing 〔your servant Zhongyan〕 Vice Administrator and 〔your servant Bi〕 Vice Military Affairs Commissioner.

Sharing in seasoning the jade cauldron, one is entrusted with harmonizing government and helping hold its balance; jointly charged with the golden military tally, the other assists through counsel in the plans made within the command tent [?]. Together we have been advanced to serve as deputies to the highest officials; these exceptional honors alike exceed the ordinary rules. Our responsibilities are equal and our burdens weighty; a sense of duty stirs…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
懇深〔臣〕等誠惶誠恐稽首頓首上言竊惟明王
稽古以建官人臣隨時而效力仲虺之爲
左相商衡成一德之功司馬而置列卿周
政底四征之績寅恭道遠獮狝風微日下
傾葵竟寒盟於白馬軍中呼柤幸驗瑞於
蒼龍制匪相沿官不必備三臺禮別霸圖
互變於前朝二府權侔
皇憲實隆於
昭代
===
天廻斗柄倚
北闕之文昌星燿
宸樞臨中台之武帳省院兼資於論議長貳
並莞乎機宜法本無前人惟求舊豈宜下
品猥次崇階伏念〔臣仲淹〕術未通經乏仁
義丘墳之學〔臣弼〕才非名世忝賢良方正
之科自忘樸陋之無能各以愚忠而相許
圖百官弊如視掌條八事言本由衷蹇蹇
匪躬矢心鏤骨
punctuated:
懇深。〔臣〕等誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首上言：竊惟明王稽古以建官，人臣隨時而效力。仲虺之爲左相，商衡成一德之功；司馬而置列卿，周政底四征之績。寅恭道遠，獮狝風微。日下傾葵，竟寒盟於白馬；軍中呼柤，幸驗瑞於蒼龍。制匪相沿，官不必備。三臺禮別，霸圖互變於前朝；二府權侔，皇憲實隆於昭代。
天廻斗柄，倚北闕之文昌；星燿宸樞，臨中台之武帳。省院兼資於論議，長貳並莞乎機宜。法本無前，人惟求舊。豈宜下品，猥次崇階？伏念〔臣仲淹〕術未通經，乏仁義丘墳之學；〔臣弼〕才非名世，忝賢良方正之科。自忘樸陋之無能，各以愚忠而相許。圖百官弊，如視掌；條八事言，本由衷。蹇蹇匪躬，矢心鏤骨。
translation_en:
…our earnestness is profound. We, your servants, in utmost fear and trembling, bow our heads to the ground and submit this memorial: We humbly reflect that enlightened kings consult antiquity when establishing offices, while their ministers render service according to the needs of the time. When Zhonghui served as Left Counsellor, the guiding ministers of Shang achieved the work of united virtue; when the Minister of War was ranked among the chief ministers, Zhou government achieved success in campaigns toward the four quarters. The way of reverent service has grown distant, and the tradition of autumn hunting has waned [?]. Like sunflowers inclining toward the sun, loyalty nevertheless ended in the neglect of the white-horse covenant; within the army, the cry of “zha” fortunately confirmed the auspicious sign of the Azure Dragon [?]. Institutions need not simply follow their predecessors, nor need every office be filled. The Three Terraces differed in ceremonial standing, as designs for hegemony changed successively under former dynasties; the two chief councils possess comparable authority, and imperial institutions have indeed flourished in this illustrious age.
Heaven turns the handle of the Dipper, relying upon Wenchang, the constellation of literary administration, at the northern palace gate; stars shine about the imperial pivot, overlooking the military command tent at the Central Terrace. The Secretariat and the Bureau of Military Affairs alike contribute to deliberations, and their chiefs and deputies together attend to crucial affairs [?]. Though these arrangements are unprecedented, the men sought are those long known and trusted. How could men of such low worth as ourselves fittingly be placed among these exalted ranks? We humbly consider that I, your servant Zhongyan, lack mastery of the Classics and learning in benevolence, righteousness, and the ancient canonical writings; I, your servant Bi, possess no talent to win renown in the age and have undeservedly passed the examination for the Worthy and Good, Upright and Correct. Forgetting our own uncultivated inadequacy, we have each pledged ourselves to simple-hearted loyalty. In planning remedies for abuses among the officials, the problems seemed as plain as the palm of a hand; in setting forth proposals on eight matters, the words came from the heart. Unremitting in service, without regard for ourselves, we pledge our hearts and engrave that resolve upon our bones…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
明明在上妄意批鱗全生荷
天地之仁尸祿負生平之願巷遇風雲之會召
自
龍飛夢協弧矢之辰生逢鶴降足每蹶於千里
價敢待於連城秘館清華曾玷考文之直
詞林供奉非邀克讓之名釜魚假息於橫
山誰之過也牧馬鳴鑣於易水何以身爲
梵書安反側之心竊慕興劉之恥緒杖節
寒氊裘之氣猶懷返漢之孤蹤豈惟爭獻
===
納之儀況復養門庭之寇尚紆顯黜敢冒
同升雖
大智不遺於采葑而拙工終難於製錦祥非
鳳集深慚治郡之功名勇謝鷹揚豈有誓
師之韜略叩
帝閽於閶闔情竭辭函辱
天府之絲綸命申遣檄極知奎負勉服鴻私恭
惟
punctuated: 明明在上，妄意批鱗；全生荷天地之仁，尸祿負生平之願。巷遇風雲之會，召自龍飛；夢協弧矢之辰，生逢鶴降。足每蹶於千里，價敢待於連城？秘館清華，曾玷考文之直；詞林供奉，非邀克讓之名。釜魚假息於橫山，誰之過也？牧馬鳴鑣於易水，何以身爲？梵書安反側之心，竊慕興劉之恥緒；杖節寒氊裘之氣，猶懷返漢之孤蹤。豈惟爭獻納之儀，況復養門庭之寇！尚紆顯黜，敢冒同升？雖大智不遺於采葑，而拙工終難於製錦。祥非鳳集，深慚治郡之功名；勇謝鷹揚，豈有誓師之韜略？叩帝閽於閶闔，情竭辭函；辱天府之絲綸，命申遣檄。極知奎負，勉服鴻私。恭惟……
translation_en:
…With your radiant wisdom above us, we rashly ventured to touch the dragon’s scales in remonstrance. That our lives were preserved we owe to your benevolence, vast as Heaven and Earth; yet, drawing stipends without worthy service, we have betrayed our lifelong aspirations. We encountered a timely convergence of wind and cloud [?], summoned at your accession, when the dragon took flight; our dreams accorded with the day of bow and arrows, and our birth coincided with the crane’s descent. Our feet repeatedly stumble on the thousand-li journey: how could we presume to command the value of a jade worth a chain of cities? We once unworthily held duty assessing compositions in the pure splendor of the imperial library; in attendance among the literary academicians, we did not seek a reputation for humility and deference.

At Hengshan, fish in the cauldron were granted a brief respite—whose fault was this? Along the Yishui, grazing warhorses jingled their bridles—what use were we? Buddhist writings soothed hearts troubled by uncertainty; we privately admired the shameful legacy [?] of restoring the house of Liu. Bearing the envoy’s tally, we chilled the spirit of those clad in felt and fur, still cherishing the solitary example of the man who returned to Han. Was it merely a matter of competing in the forms of presenting counsel? Worse still, we nurtured bandits at our very gates! Even conspicuous dismissal would trouble you on our account: how dare we presume to rise together?

Although your great wisdom, in gathering turnips, does not discard their useful roots, a clumsy artisan can hardly weave brocade. Our auspicious achievements have brought no phoenixes to alight; we feel profound shame over our accomplishments and reputation in governing a prefecture. Our courage falls short of the soaring eagle’s: what strategic skill have we for pledging an army to battle? We knocked at the imperial portals, the gates of Heaven, pouring out our feelings in a written submission. We were honored with the silken words of an imperial decree, its command reiterated in a dispatched proclamation. Fully aware of our failings [?], we endeavor to accept this immense personal favor. We reverently reflect that…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
乾元建極
離照重熙斂五福而錫庶民覲耿光而揚大
烈達孝以天下養問安勤三駕之鑾輿率
土爲聖人氓振旅覲兩階之干羽太乙效
靈濡於湯野精禋下拂勾陳大官抑禮膳
於堯年仁愛上孚
穹昊雅樂務中和之本洋洋乎金聲玉振之大
成夷俘給唐鄧之田蕩蕩乎天覆地載之
無外桑陽氣而乘來南疇瑤冊紀三推之
===
之旌麾謂政可與知所以弘上公之化而
之裴度寤寐憶濟川之舟楫拊髀嘆細柳
屈道已軼於宣尼蔡功惟斷乃成事若資
黃鉞白旄霜凛西清之羽衛萊人不戰而
安聖不自聖牙籤錦軸奎纏東觀之圖書
廣鐸鞀之路節浮發帑輓粟飛芻安若泰
翠華儼六御之清塵書扆揭戶牖之銘納諫
貽謀而建圻北鄙
令典纘
punctuated: 乾元建極，離照重熙，斂五福而錫庶民，覲耿光而揚大烈。達孝以天下養，問安勤三駕之鑾輿；率土爲聖人氓，振旅覲兩階之干羽。太乙效靈，濡於湯野，精禋下拂勾陳；大官抑禮膳於堯年，仁愛上孚穹昊。雅樂務中和之本，洋洋乎金聲玉振之大成；夷俘給唐鄧之田，蕩蕩乎天覆地載之無外。桑陽氣而乘來南疇，瑤冊紀三推之之旌麾，謂政可與知，所以弘上公之化而之裴度。寤寐憶濟川之舟楫，拊髀嘆細柳。屈道已軼於宣尼，蔡功惟斷乃成，事若資黃鉞白旄，霜凛西清之羽衛。萊人不戰而安，聖不自聖，牙籤錦軸，奎纏東觀之圖書。廣鐸鞀之路，節浮發帑，輓粟飛芻，安若泰。翠華儼六御之清塵，書扆揭戶牖之銘，納諫貽謀而建圻北鄙，令典纘。
translation_en:
…The primal power of Heaven establishes the supreme standard; the radiance of the sun shines with renewed brilliance. You gather the five blessings and bestow them upon the common people, displaying resplendent virtue and proclaiming great achievements. Your consummate filial piety provides sustenance with the resources of the entire realm; in diligently inquiring after your parent’s well-being, your imperial carriage makes three journeys. Throughout the land, all are subjects of the sage. Returning troops display shields and feathered standards between the two stairways. Taiyi manifests divine efficacy, bringing moisture to the fields of Tang; your pure sacrifices reach down to touch Gouchen [?]. The palace kitchens reduce ceremonial meals in a year like Yao’s, and your benevolence wins the trust of Heaven above. Court music attends to the foundations of balance and harmony: magnificent is its perfection, with bronze bells sounding and jade chimes bringing it to completion. Captives from foreign peoples receive fields in Tang and Deng: vast is your embrace, excluding nothing, like Heaven covering and Earth supporting all.

“Mulberry,” the breath of yang, and coming to the southern fields [?]; a precious record commemorates the three pushes of the ritual plough, followed by “of the banners of command” [?]. It is said that one may participate in understanding government, thereby extending the transforming influence of the highest duke; the following reference to Pei Du is garbled [?]. Waking and sleeping, you recall the boat and oars needed to cross the river; striking your thigh, you sigh for Xiliu. “Bending the Way,” already surpassing Xuanni, Confucius [?]; the achievement at Cai—only through decisiveness was it accomplished. Affairs seem to rely upon the yellow battle-axe and white yak-tail standard; the imperial bodyguard in the western palace precinct is stern as frost. The people of Lai are brought to peace without battle. The sage does not regard himself as a sage. Ivory book labels and brocade scroll rollers adorn the books of the Eastern Library, where the constellation Kui gathers [?]. You broaden the channels of the bell and drum through which counsel reaches the ruler, curb extravagance, and open the treasury. Grain is transported and fodder sped onward, bringing security like Mount Tai [?]. The kingfisher-feather imperial standard lends solemnity to the purified path of the six-horse imperial carriage. Inscriptions are written upon the throne screen and displayed on doors and windows. You accept remonstrance and bequeath plans to posterity, establishing boundaries on the northern frontier [?]. Excellent statutes continue…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
樞必有副庶幾壯元老之猷兵民之本各
殊安危所係則一若選于衆豈無其人乃
憐〔臣仲淹〕罔避險艱俾分日領台階之印
且戒〔臣琦〕毋敢違越必刻期綴法從之班
揣分既踰受
知特異蓋
淵衷久注乎西北故
脊眷誤濫於芻蕘〔臣〕等敢不同心以濟利敢斷
金益道而行心存匪石集衆思以廣忠益
===
補衮隨鳳沼之鵷鸞求國士以佐時艱登
壇肅豹關之鎖鑰但知策駑而附驥敢云
好大而喜功廊廟江湖時沛域中之霖雨
甲兵俎豆坐銷塞上之烽烟惟狥國以忘
家庶先憂而後樂仰裨
廟勝寧虛靈武之謡上籍
勵管子之四維益堅晩節此〔臣〕等願效犬
馬以忠
punctuated: 樞必有副，庶幾壯元老之猷。兵民之本各殊，安危所係則一。若選于衆，豈無其人？乃憐〔臣仲淹〕罔避險艱，俾分日領台階之印；且戒〔臣琦〕毋敢違越，必刻期綴法從之班。揣分既踰，受知特異。蓋淵衷久注乎西北，故脊眷誤濫於芻蕘。〔臣〕等敢不同心以濟，利敢斷金；益道而行，心存匪石。集衆思以廣忠益，補衮隨鳳沼之鵷鸞；求國士以佐時艱，登壇肅豹關之鎖鑰。但知策駑而附驥，敢云好大而喜功？廊廟江湖，時沛域中之霖雨；甲兵俎豆，坐銷塞上之烽烟。惟狥國以忘家，庶先憂而後樂。仰裨廟勝，寧虛靈武之謡？上籍勵管子之四維，益堅晩節。此〔臣〕等願效犬馬以忠
translation_en:
…The Bureau of Military Affairs must have a deputy, so that the plans of the senior minister may be strengthened. Military and civil affairs differ in their foundations, yet the security or peril of the realm depends alike upon them. If men were selected from the multitude, could suitable candidates be lacking? Yet, taking pity on 〔your servant Zhongyan〕, who has never shunned danger or hardship, you have charged him to receive, on an appointed day [?], the seal of high ministerial office. You have also admonished 〔your servant Qi〕 not to disobey, but to join the ranks of your attendant officials by the appointed date. Measuring our capacities, we find these appointments already beyond our deserts; the recognition we have received is exceptionally great. Your profound concern has long been fixed upon the northwest, and thus your gracious regard [?] has mistakenly overflowed upon such humble woodcutters and grass-gatherers as ourselves.

How could 〔we, your servants〕 fail to unite our hearts in accomplishing the task, with a sharpness that dares to sever metal [?]? We shall proceed in accordance with the Way of Increase, our hearts steadfast, no stones to be turned. We shall gather the thoughts of many to broaden our loyal service, remedying deficiencies in government as we follow the phoenix-like worthies of the imperial court. We shall seek outstanding men to assist in these difficult times, ascending the commander's platform to secure the strategic frontier gates. We know only to spur our inferior steeds and follow the thoroughbreds; how could we presume to delight in grand undertakings and glorious achievements? Whether at court or far away among rivers and lakes, may we bring timely, abundant rain throughout the realm; through arms and ritual, may we extinguish the beacon fires along the frontier. Devoting ourselves to the state and forgetting our households, we hope to be first to take on its cares and last to enjoy its pleasures. Looking upward, we shall assist the court's victorious plans: how could we let the song of Lingwu prove empty? Drawing upon what is above [?], we shall uphold Guanzi's four cardinal principles and make our integrity in later life still firmer. This is why 〔we, your servants〕 wish to render the service of dogs and horses, in loyal devotion to…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
朝廷之職分而妄希塵露以益河嶽之高深
者也伏望
惟精惟一
學齊虞舜以重華
乃武乃文
德並唐堯而廣運
政先内治握君子小人消長之機
治底外寧察華夏蠻夷盛衰之理
皇道齊尊於北極
===
聖壽比固於南山龜瑞龍祥
寶命建九圍之式馬歸牛放
金甌保萬世之基〔臣〕等無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第叄場
punctuated:
朝廷之職分，而妄希塵露以益河嶽之高深者也。伏望惟精惟一，學齊虞舜以重華；乃武乃文，德並唐堯而廣運。政先内治，握君子小人消長之機；治底外寧，察華夏蠻夷盛衰之理。皇道齊尊於北極，聖壽比固於南山。龜瑞龍祥，寶命建九圍之式；馬歸牛放，金甌保萬世之基。〔臣〕等無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。

第叄場
translation_en:
…the duties owed to the court, and presumptuously hope that our dust and dew may add to the height of the mountains and the depth of the rivers. We humbly pray that, with discernment and singleness of purpose, Your Majesty may equal Shun of Yu in learning and renew his splendor; that, in martial and civil accomplishments alike, Your virtue may match Yao of Tang and extend its influence far and wide. In government, give precedence to order within, grasping the critical workings by which gentlemen and petty men advance or retreat; in governing, bring peace to the frontiers, discerning the principles behind the flourishing and decline of the Chinese realm and the non-Chinese peoples. May the imperial Way be as exalted as the North Star, and Your sagely longevity as enduring as the Southern Mountain. With auspicious tortoises and propitious dragons, may the precious Mandate establish a model for all nine regions; with warhorses returned and oxen set loose, may the golden vessel of the realm preserve its foundations for ten thousand generations. We, your servants, gaze toward Heaven and look up to Your sagely person, overcome with fervent emotion and trembling awe. We respectfully submit this memorial to express our gratitude and bring it to Your Majesty’s hearing.

Third Session

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
策
第一問
仇炅
同考試官學正龍　批〔我〕
皇祖
列聖及我
皇上至德淵微心學精與有未易窺測者子能鋪張揚厲且忠愛藹然是涵濡
聖化而有得者錄之以鳴
國家之盛
===
考試官學正蔡　批〔道統之言遠有端緒仰窺〕
聖製有得者也佳士佳士
考試官學正周　批〔是善闡揚〕
聖學者宜錄之以
獻
聖王懋格天之業而其出之也有本端立
治之本而其養之也有功篤日新之功而
其一之也有要夫人君代天理物莫急於
致治而脩德所以端本善則以神感化
punctuated:
策
第一問
仇炅
同考試官學正龍　批〔我〕皇祖、列聖及我皇上，至德淵微，心學精與，有未易窺測者。子能鋪張揚厲，且忠愛藹然，是涵濡聖化而有得者，錄之以鳴國家之盛。
考試官學正蔡　批〔道統之言，遠有端緒，仰窺〕聖製，有得者也。佳士！佳士！
考試官學正周　批〔是善闡揚〕聖學者，宜錄之以獻。
聖王懋格天之業，而其出之也有本；端立治之本，而其養之也有功；篤日新之功，而其一之也有要。夫人君代天理物，莫急於致治，而脩德所以端本，善則以神感化
translation_en:
Policy Essay
First Question
Qiu Jiong

Comment by Associate Examiner Long, an Instructor: Our imperial ancestor, the successive sage emperors, and our present emperor possess supreme virtue of profound subtlety. Their learning of the mind is refined [?], with depths not easily fathomed. You have been able to expound and extol it, while also displaying abundant loyalty and affection. You have thus gained something from immersion in the civilizing influence of the sage ruler. This essay is selected to proclaim the flourishing state of the dynasty.

Comment by Examiner Cai, an Instructor: Your discussion of the succession of the Way traces its origins far back. In reverently examining the imperial compositions, you have gained understanding. An excellent scholar! An excellent scholar!

Comment by Examiner Zhou, an Instructor: Here is someone skilled at elucidating the sage ruler’s learning. This essay should be selected for presentation to the throne.

The sage king diligently pursues the work of reaching Heaven, and what he brings forth has a foundation; he sets upright the foundation of government, and his cultivation of it involves sustained effort; he devotes himself to daily renewal, and there is an essential principle by which he unifies it. Now, for a ruler who orders all things on Heaven’s behalf, nothing is more urgent than achieving good government. Cultivating virtue is the means of setting the foundation upright, and perfecting the standards brings a wondrous power of moral transformation [?]…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
之機天下之大本也圖治固在於脩德而
務學廼所以明理通變以成懋昭之實天
下之大功也成德固在於務學而正心廼
所以涵養本源以收學問之功天下之大
要也不正其心不可以言學不務其學不
可以言德不脩其德不可以言治是故心
以貞學學以成德德以立治此天德王道
之端内聖外王之業也顧可以易言哉惟
我
===
皇祖造端於前
列聖繼承於後我
皇上益闡揚於今心學之妙德治之隆真非後
世帝王所能彷彿其一二者也愚蓋涵濡
聖化而有以得其槩矣敢遂言之粤自精一執
中之學始傳而欽明温恭之德丕著堯舜
之德天下之大德也堯舜之學天下之大
學也然皆本之於一心而要其成於厥中
之執故德盛治隆而時雍風動之化邈乎
punctuated:
之機，天下之大本也。圖治固在於脩德，而務學廼所以明理通變，以成懋昭之實，天下之大功也。成德固在於務學，而正心廼所以涵養本源，以收學問之功，天下之大要也。不正其心，不可以言學；不務其學，不可以言德；不脩其德，不可以言治。是故心以貞學，學以成德，德以立治，此天德王道之端、内聖外王之業也，顧可以易言哉？
惟我皇祖造端於前，列聖繼承於後，我皇上益闡揚於今，心學之妙、德治之隆，真非後世帝王所能彷彿其一二者也。愚蓋涵濡聖化，而有以得其槩矣，敢遂言之。粤自精一執中之學始傳，而欽明温恭之德丕著。堯舜之德，天下之大德也；堯舜之學，天下之大學也。然皆本之於一心，而要其成於厥中之執，故德盛治隆，而時雍風動之化邈乎
translation_en:
…the workings of transformation, the great foundation of all under Heaven. Seeking good government certainly depends on cultivating virtue; diligent learning is the means of understanding principles and responding to change, thereby achieving the reality of resplendent virtue. This is the great undertaking of all under Heaven. Perfecting virtue certainly depends on diligent learning; rectifying the mind is the means of nurturing the root and source, thereby bringing learning to fruition. This is the great essential of all under Heaven. Without rectifying the mind, one cannot speak of learning; without diligently pursuing learning, one cannot speak of virtue; without cultivating virtue, one cannot speak of government. Thus the mind makes learning upright, learning perfects virtue, and virtue establishes good government. This is the starting point of Heavenly virtue and the kingly Way, the undertaking of inward sagehood and outward kingship. How could it be spoken of lightly?
Our imperial ancestor laid the foundations in earlier times; the successive sage emperors carried them forward; and our present Emperor further elucidates them today. The subtlety of learning centered on the mind and the flourishing of government through virtue truly surpass anything of which later ages’ emperors and kings could approximate even a small part. Immersed in the sage’s transforming influence, I, in my humble understanding, have grasped its general outline and venture therefore to explain it. From the time when the teaching of refinement, single-mindedness, and holding fast to the Mean was first transmitted, the virtues of reverence, enlightenment, gentleness, and respect became greatly manifest. The virtue of Yao and Shun was the great virtue of all under Heaven; the learning of Yao and Shun was the great learning of all under Heaven. Yet both were rooted in the mind alone, and their fulfillment depended essentially on holding fast to the Mean. Thus virtue flourished and government prospered, while their transforming influence—bringing universal harmony and moving the people as the wind moves things—was so far-reaching…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
無以尚矣自是舜傳之禹禹傳之湯湯傳
之文武而祗台而顧諟而無斁而敬勝曰
以禮制心也曰日新又新也曰小心翼翼
也曰不泄不忘也夷考其治孰不本於德
而德孰不本於心學也哉自是一降而漢
再降而唐而宋其間願治之君非無懋學
之志若漢武帝表章六經矣光武能通尚
書矣唐太宗銳情經術矣玄宗發揮典籍
矣夜分觀書有若宋太宗者焉專講春秋
===
有若宋高宗者焉是非不知學也然徒事
於口耳章句之末未聞乎精一執中之旨
故德不底於純一而治僅止於小康終不
免於雜霸雜夷而柔懦之不振也洪惟我
太祖高皇帝誕膺
天命汛掃胡元揭日月於重明闢乾坤於再造
聖神本於天縱道學原於性成奉三無私正已
萃百順之美純一不已大心觀萬化之原
其作
punctuated:
無以尚矣。自是舜傳之禹，禹傳之湯，湯傳之文武，而祗台，而顧諟，而無斁，而敬勝。曰「以禮制心」也，曰「日新又新」也，曰「小心翼翼」也，曰「不泄不忘」也。夷考其治，孰不本於德，而德孰不本於心學也哉？自是一降而漢，再降而唐而宋，其間願治之君，非無懋學之志。若漢武帝表章六經矣，光武能通尚書矣，唐太宗銳情經術矣，玄宗發揮典籍矣，夜分觀書，有若宋太宗者焉；專講春秋，有若宋高宗者焉。是非不知學也，然徒事於口耳章句之末，未聞乎精一執中之旨，故德不底於純一，而治僅止於小康，終不免於雜霸雜夷，而柔懦之不振也。
洪惟我太祖高皇帝誕膺天命，汛掃胡元，揭日月於重明，闢乾坤於再造。聖神本於天縱，道學原於性成，奉三無私，正已萃百順之美，純一不已，大心觀萬化之原。其作
translation_en:
…nothing could surpass it. From this point Shun transmitted it to Yu, Yu to Tang, and Tang to Wen and Wu: reverently attending to one's virtue, keeping Heaven's luminous mandate constantly in view, remaining unwearied, and letting reverence prevail. Their teachings speak of “regulating the heart through ritual,” “renewing oneself daily and renewing oneself yet again,” being “circumspect and reverent,” and “neither slackening nor forgetting.” Examining their government dispassionately, whose did not rest upon virtue, and whose virtue did not rest upon learning concerning the heart? Thereafter came a decline to the Han, and further declines to the Tang and Song. Among them, rulers who desired good government were not without the resolve to study diligently. Han Wudi exalted the Six Classics; Guangwu mastered the Book of Documents; Tang Taizong devoted himself keenly to classical learning; Xuanzong expounded the canonical writings. There was Song Taizong, who read far into the night, and Song Gaozong, who concentrated on studying the Spring and Autumn Annals. These rulers were not ignorant of learning. Yet they occupied themselves merely with the peripheral matters of oral transmission and textual explication, without grasping the essential meaning of refinement and single-mindedness, and of holding fast to the Mean. Thus their virtue did not attain purity and unity, and their government achieved only modest peace and order. In the end, they could not avoid admixtures of hegemonic methods and barbarian ways, or the failure to rouse themselves from weakness and timidity.
We reverently reflect that our Taizu, the Exalted Emperor, magnificently received Heaven's Mandate and swept away the barbarian Yuan, raising the sun and moon to renewed brilliance and opening heaven and earth anew. His sageliness and spiritual insight were Heaven's gifts; his learning of the Way sprang from his innate nature. He upheld the three forms of impartiality—those of Heaven, Earth, and the sun and moon—and, rectifying himself, gathered together the excellence of every kind of accord. Unceasing in his purity and unity, he enlarged his heart to contemplate the source of all transformations. When he composed …

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
祖訓以貽謀也則正之以大綱析之以萬目曰
脩身之法也曰齊家之法也曰重民命則
肉刑之不施也曰戒黷武則諸夷之不伐
也而持守一章又是編之要道創守之規
備矣其作
昭鑑錄以垂訓也則採摭乎前古勾稽於故實
發其明禍福之源焉達吉凶之理焉廣爲
善之樂焉杜僭逆之萌焉而善惡備載又
觀法之本源行葦之恩篤矣凡此皆
===
聖德之廣運也是德也即堯舜禹湯文武之德
也而何者不本於學以成之也哉是故其
造觀心亭也則有以探義理之本而語宋
濂曰人心虛靈衆氣機出入操而存之爲
難朕罔敢自暇自逸此不顯亦臨之心也
註洪範圖則有以衍箕禹之疇而又曰天
人一理必以類應君能脩德則七政順度
雨暘應期災害不生此應天以實之意也
凡此皆
punctuated:
《祖訓》以貽謀也，則正之以大綱，析之以萬目：曰脩身之法也，曰齊家之法也，曰重民命則肉刑之不施也，曰戒黷武則諸夷之不伐也。而持守一章，又是編之要道，創守之規備矣。其作《昭鑑錄》以垂訓也，則採摭乎前古，勾稽於故實，發其明禍福之源焉，達吉凶之理焉，廣爲善之樂焉，杜僭逆之萌焉。而善惡備載，又觀法之本源，行葦之恩篤矣。凡此皆聖德之廣運也。是德也，即堯舜禹湯文武之德也，而何者不本於學以成之也哉？
是故其造觀心亭也，則有以探義理之本，而語宋濂曰：「人心虛靈，衆氣機出入，操而存之爲難。朕罔敢自暇自逸。」此不顯亦臨之心也。註《洪範圖》，則有以衍箕禹之疇，而又曰：「天人一理，必以類應。君能脩德，則七政順度，雨暘應期，災害不生。」此應天以實之意也。凡此皆
translation_en:
…the Ancestral Instructions (Zuxun), to leave plans for his descendants, he set matters straight through broad principles and distinguished them through myriad particulars: methods of cultivating oneself; methods of ordering the family; valuing the people's lives, hence refraining from mutilating punishments; and guarding against reckless warfare, hence refraining from attacking the various foreign peoples. The chapter on maintaining and preserving the inheritance is, moreover, the essential teaching of this compilation. Thus the rules for founding and preserving the dynasty are complete. In composing the Record of the Illuminating Mirror (Zhaojian lu) to transmit instruction, he gathered material from antiquity and examined historical precedents, elucidating the sources of misfortune and good fortune [?], making clear the principles of auspicious and inauspicious outcomes, enlarging the delight in doing good, and forestalling the first stirrings of usurpation and rebellion. Its comprehensive recording of both good and evil also provides the fundamental basis for discerning models to follow. Profound indeed is the benevolence exemplified in the poem “Luxuriant Reeds”! All these manifest the far-reaching operation of his sagely virtue. This virtue is the very virtue of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu. What part of it was not rooted in learning and perfected through it?
Thus, when he built the Pavilion for Contemplating the Mind (Guanxin ting), he thereby explored the foundations of moral principle. He told Song Lian: “The human mind is empty and numinous; the manifold workings of vital energy pass in and out. To hold fast to it and preserve it is difficult. I dare not permit myself leisure or ease.” This is the disposition expressed in the words, “Even where you are unseen, you are watched over.” In annotating the Diagram of the Great Plan (Hongfan tu), he elaborated the categories transmitted by Jizi and Yu. He further said: “Heaven and humanity share a single principle and necessarily respond to each other according to kind. If the ruler can cultivate virtue, the seven celestial regulators will follow their proper courses, rain and sunshine will arrive in season, and disasters will not arise.” This expresses the intention of responding to Heaven through substantive action. All these…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
聖學之深造也是學也即堯舜禹湯文武之學
也而何者不本於心以貞之也哉以是心
而爲學以是學而成德以是德而達治蓋
有以軼二帝三王而陋漢唐宋於不足言
矣伏讀
聖政記而有得焉曰大本定矣大分昭矣軍政
肅矣倖位杜矣僭侈抑而禮儀正矣內則
正而法制嚴矣其經綸之迹乎讀
大明日曆而有得焉曰功高萬古也得國之正
===
也獨秉全智也敬天勤民也家法之嚴也
兵政有統也其致治之本乎他若宏綱大
目備載於諸司職掌之中者其設官分職
體國經野則又取法乎周官而區畫其輕
重師意不泥其迹酌古必準以今故大綱
正而法度森然萬目張而綜理周密有難
以縷述者凡此皆本於德原於學存於心
而致之焉者也其不與堯舜禹湯文武之
時雍風動咸和怙冒者同一極盛也哉
punctuated:
聖學之深造也。是學也，即堯舜禹湯文武之學也，而何者不本於心以貞之也哉？以是心而爲學，以是學而成德，以是德而達治，蓋有以軼二帝三王，而陋漢唐宋於不足言矣。
伏讀《聖政記》而有得焉，曰：大本定矣，大分昭矣，軍政肅矣，倖位杜矣，僭侈抑而禮儀正矣，內則正而法制嚴矣。其經綸之迹乎？讀《大明日曆》而有得焉，曰：功高萬古也，得國之正也，獨秉全智也，敬天勤民也，家法之嚴也，兵政有統也。其致治之本乎？他若宏綱大目備載於《諸司職掌》之中者，其設官分職、體國經野，則又取法乎《周官》，而區畫其輕重，師意不泥其迹，酌古必準以今。故大綱正而法度森然，萬目張而綜理周密，有難以縷述者。凡此皆本於德，原於學，存於心，而致之焉者也。其不與堯舜禹湯文武之時雍、風動、咸和、怙冒者，同一極盛也哉？
translation_en:
…profound attainments in sagely learning. This learning is precisely the learning of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu. What part of it did not take the heart as its foundation and thereby attain rectitude? With this heart he pursued learning; through this learning he perfected his virtue; through this virtue he achieved good government. Thus he could surpass the Two Emperors and Three Kings, making the Han, Tang, and Song seem paltry and unworthy of mention.
Reverently reading the Record of Sagely Government (Shengzheng ji), I gained this understanding: the great foundation was established; the cardinal distinctions of status were made clear; military administration was disciplined; access to office through favoritism was blocked; usurpation of privilege and extravagance were restrained, and ritual observances were rectified; rules for the inner household were set right, and laws and institutions were made strict. Were these not the visible achievements of his ordering of the realm? Reading the Daily Record of the Great Ming (Da Ming rili), I gained this understanding: his achievements surpassed those of all antiquity; he acquired the realm rightfully; he alone possessed consummate wisdom; he revered Heaven and labored for the people; his dynastic household rules were strict; and military administration had a unified direction. Were these not the foundations of his achievement of good government? As for the broad principles and major provisions fully recorded in the Duties of the Various Offices (Zhusi zhizhang), in establishing offices, assigning duties, organizing the capital, and laying out the countryside, he also took the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan) as his model, distinguishing the relative importance of its provisions. He followed their intent without being bound by their outward forms; whenever he drew upon antiquity, he judged it against present circumstances. Thus the principal framework was correctly established, and laws and regulations stood in imposing order; the myriad particulars were put into effect, and their overall administration was thorough and meticulous. These things are difficult to recount in full. All were rooted in virtue, originated in learning, and were held in the heart before being brought to realization. Did this not equal the supreme flourishing under Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu, when the age was harmonious, the people responded as to the wind, all lived in concord, and all found support and protection?

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
列聖相承聿隆化理敬守我
太祖之心學懋昭我
太祖之功德無以復加而獨於敎
太子之道尤切惓惓在
成祖文皇帝則有
文華寶鑑之編焉在
宣宗章皇帝則有
御製帝訓之編焉在
憲宗純皇帝則有
===
文華大訓之編焉皆以衍
祖訓之傳廣昭鑑之類者也是故君德也奉天
也馭外也安內也脩治均平之方於是乎
悉矣進學也養德也厚倫也明治也盛德
大業之本於是乎基矣此其精神內運故
章程立純正之規模涵養中深故典則闡
淵衷之精藴孰謂非心學之妙盛德之積而世
守之耶是德也卽我
聖祖之德也是學也卽我
punctuated: 列聖相承，聿隆化理，敬守我太祖之心學，懋昭我太祖之功德，無以復加，而獨於敎太子之道尤切惓惓。在成祖文皇帝，則有《文華寶鑑》之編焉；在宣宗章皇帝，則有《御製帝訓》之編焉；在憲宗純皇帝，則有《文華大訓》之編焉。皆以衍《祖訓》之傳，廣《昭鑑》之類者也。是故君德也、奉天也、馭外也、安內也，脩治均平之方於是乎悉矣；進學也、養德也、厚倫也、明治也，盛德大業之本於是乎基矣。此其精神內運，故章程立純正之規模；涵養中深，故典則闡淵衷之精藴。孰謂非心學之妙、盛德之積，而世守之耶？是德也，卽我聖祖之德也；是學也，卽我
translation_en:
The successive sage emperors carried on the succession, increasingly perfected moral transformation and governance, reverently preserved our Taizu’s learning of the mind, and splendidly manifested our Taizu’s achievements and virtue. Nothing further could be added; yet they were especially earnest in their concern for the education of the heir apparent. Under Emperor Chengzu Wen, there was the compilation Precious Mirror of Literary Splendor (Wenhua baojian); under Emperor Xuanzong Zhang, the Imperially Composed Instructions for Emperors (Yuzhi dixun); and under Emperor Xianzong Chun, the Great Instructions of Literary Splendor (Wenhua daxun). All served to extend the transmission of the Ancestral Instructions (Zuxun) and expand upon works of the kind exemplified by the Illustrious Mirror (Zhaojian).

Thus, rulerly virtue, serving Heaven, managing relations beyond the realm, and securing peace within it—the methods of cultivating good government and ensuring equity were fully set forth here. Advancing learning, nurturing virtue, strengthening human relationships, and understanding governance—the foundations of abundant virtue and great undertakings were established here. Because their spiritual energies worked within, their regulations established a pattern of purity and rectitude; because their inward cultivation was profound, their guiding norms revealed the subtle riches of their deepest intentions. Who could say that these were not the wonders of learning of the mind and the accumulation of abundant virtue, preserved from generation to generation? This virtue is precisely the virtue of our sagely ancestor; this learning is precisely the learning of our …

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
聖祖之學也是心也卽我
聖祖之心也而皆同符於古帝王焉者也則其
致治之盛固宜無不同者然而昭
列聖維則之孝續精一心學之傳達雍穆熙皞
之治者則又有賴於我
今上也仰惟我
皇上天縱
聖神日新
大德恢弘
===
祖烈深探道原其本之爲德業而發之爲文章
則有敬一箴有心箴解有視聽言動箴解
焉其敘敬一箴曰敬者存其心而不忽之
謂也一者純乎理而不雜之謂也大哉
聖言其萬世心學之綱要乎又曰郊則恭誠廟
嚴孝趨肅於朝廷愼於閒居省躬察咎儆
戒無虞又曰弗貳以三弗貳以二行顧其
言終如其始靜虛無欲日新不已至哉
聖言其主靜立極之根源乎其解范氏心箴曰
punctuated:
聖祖之學也。是心也，卽我聖祖之心也，而皆同符於古帝王焉者也。則其致治之盛，固宜無不同者。然而昭列聖維則之孝，續精一心學之傳，達雍穆熙皞之治者，則又有賴於我今上也。仰惟我皇上天縱聖神，日新大德，恢弘祖烈，深探道原。其本之爲德業而發之爲文章，則有《敬一箴》，有《心箴解》，有《視聽言動箴解》焉。
其敘《敬一箴》曰：「敬者，存其心而不忽之謂也。一者，純乎理而不雜之謂也。」大哉聖言！其萬世心學之綱要乎！又曰：「郊則恭誠，廟嚴孝，趨肅於朝廷，愼於閒居，省躬察咎，儆戒無虞。」又曰：「弗貳以三，弗貳以二，行顧其言，終如其始，靜虛無欲，日新不已。」至哉聖言！其主靜立極之根源乎！其解范氏《心箴》曰：
translation_en:
…the learning of our Sagely Progenitor. This mind is indeed the mind of our Sagely Progenitor; all accord with those of the ancient sage-kings. It is therefore fitting that the splendor of their achievements in government should likewise be the same. Yet manifesting filial devotion by following the standards of the successive sage emperors, continuing the transmission of the learning of the mind through refinement and single-mindedness, and attaining harmonious, reverent, flourishing, and joyous government depend further upon our present sovereign. We reverently consider how our Emperor, endowed by Heaven with sagely wisdom, daily renews his great virtue, magnifies his ancestors’ glorious achievements, and deeply explores the source of the Way. What is rooted in his virtuous accomplishments finds expression in his writings: the Admonition on Reverent Single-mindedness, the Explanation of the Admonition on the Mind, and the Explanations of the Admonitions on Seeing, Hearing, Speaking, and Acting.
In his preface to the Admonition on Reverent Single-mindedness, he says: “Reverence means preserving one’s mind without neglecting it. Single-mindedness means being wholly in accord with principle, without admixture.” Great indeed are these sagely words! Are they not the essential framework for the learning of the mind for all ages? He further says: “At the suburban sacrifices, be respectful and sincere; in the ancestral temple, solemn and filial. Conduct yourself with gravity at court and exercise care in private. Examine yourself and scrutinize your faults; remain vigilant even when no danger threatens.” He also says: “Do not divide it into three; do not divide it into two [?]. Let your conduct heed your words, and end as you began. Be still and empty, free of desire; renew yourself daily without ceasing.” Perfect indeed are these sagely words! Are they not the source of making stillness paramount and establishing the ultimate standard? In his explanation of Master Fan’s Admonition on the Mind, he says: …

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
心爲一身之主吾心克正則四肢百骸莫
不聽其使令使有一毫不正則被聲色所
移物欲所隔便動與理相反斯言也其發
范氏所未發而有功於養心之學者乎其
解程子四箴曰唯中心安之凡視無不明
又曰聽言之際當分別其邪正又曰凡人
所言必求合諸道理準諸經傳又曰凡人
之所動察其當爲與所不當爲精別而行
之斯言也其發程子所未發而默相乎克
===
已之功者乎此皆我
皇上至德淵微
聖學緼與而悉本之以純心發之爲制作寔有
以紹
皇祖
列聖之緒接堯舜禹湯文武之統千聖一心萬
古一道猗歟盛哉然
聖人之學固得於天性而日新之妙尤懋於脩
爲乃若脩爲之方舍敬奚以哉易曰君子
punctuated:
「心爲一身之主，吾心克正，則四肢百骸莫不聽其使令；使有一毫不正，則被聲色所移，物欲所隔，便動與理相反。」斯言也，其發范氏所未發，而有功於養心之學者乎？其解程子四箴曰：「唯中心安之，凡視無不明。」又曰：「聽言之際，當分別其邪正。」又曰：「凡人所言，必求合諸道理，準諸經傳。」又曰：「凡人之所動，察其當爲與所不當爲，精別而行之。」斯言也，其發程子所未發，而默相乎克已之功者乎？

此皆我皇上至德淵微，聖學緼與，而悉本之以純心，發之爲制作，寔有以紹皇祖列聖之緒，接堯舜禹湯文武之統。千聖一心，萬古一道，猗歟盛哉！然聖人之學，固得於天性，而日新之妙，尤懋於脩爲。乃若脩爲之方，舍敬奚以哉？《易》曰：「君子
translation_en:
…“The mind is the master of the whole body. If my mind can be upright, then every limb and bone will obey its commands. If there is the slightest lack of uprightness, however, it will be swayed by sounds and sensual attractions and obstructed by material desires; its actions will then run counter to principle.” Do these words not bring out what Master Fan left unexpressed and contribute to the learning of nurturing the mind? In his explanations of Master Cheng’s Four Admonitions, he says: “Only when the mind within rests at ease in it will everything one looks upon be seen clearly.” He also says: “When listening to words, one should distinguish between the deviant and the correct.” Again: “Whatever a person says must accord with moral principles and be measured against the classics and their commentaries.” Again: “In all that a person does, one should examine what ought and ought not to be done, distinguish carefully, and then act.” Do these words not bring out what Master Cheng left unexpressed and silently assist the work of overcoming the self [?]?

All this arises from the depth and subtlety of our Emperor’s consummate virtue and the richness of his sagely learning [?]. He bases it all upon a pure mind and gives it expression in his writings and institutions. These truly enable him to continue the legacy of the imperial ancestor and the successive sage emperors, and to carry forward the succession of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu. A thousand sages share one mind; through all antiquity there is one Way. Ah, how magnificent! Yet although the sage’s learning is indeed endowed by Heaven in his nature, the wondrous achievement of daily renewal depends especially on diligent self-cultivation. As for the means of self-cultivation, what could serve apart from reverent attentiveness? The Book of Changes says: “The noble man…”

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
敬以直內書曰夙夜惟寅直哉惟清言人
心敬則直直則一聖學之所以成始成終
也故
聖製曰匪敬弗聚匪一弗純敬怠純駁應驗頓
殊徵諸天人如鼓荅桴非所謂萬世不易
之定論也歟我
皇上身體而力行之是以
德極天下之純
學極天下之大而嘉靖無疆之治有明徵矣
===
其所以光
二祖
七宗之烈以開億萬年無疆啓佑之圖者端有
在於是也
聖子
神孫能以我
祖宗之心爲心以我
皇上之心爲心而獨於所謂敬一者加之意焉
則心不患不純學不患不大德不患不脩
punctuated:
敬以直內。《書》曰：「夙夜惟寅，直哉惟清。」言人心敬則直，直則一，聖學之所以成始成終也。故聖製曰：「匪敬弗聚，匪一弗純。敬怠純駁，應驗頓殊。徵諸天人，如鼓荅桴。」非所謂萬世不易之定論也歟？我皇上身體而力行之，是以德極天下之純，學極天下之大，而嘉靖無疆之治有明徵矣。其所以光二祖七宗之烈，以開億萬年無疆啓佑之圖者，端有在於是也。
聖子神孫能以我祖宗之心爲心，以我皇上之心爲心，而獨於所謂敬一者加之意焉，則心不患不純，學不患不大，德不患不脩，
translation_en:
…“Through reverent attentiveness, he makes his inner self upright.” The Book of Documents says: “Morning and night, be reverently attentive; be upright, be pure.” This means that when the human mind is reverently attentive, it becomes upright, and when upright, it becomes single-minded. This is how sagely learning is brought to fulfillment from beginning to end. Thus the imperial composition says: “Without reverent attentiveness, the mind cannot be gathered together; without single-mindedness, it cannot be pure. Reverence and negligence, purity and admixture—their effects differ utterly. Test this against Heaven and humanity: it is like a drum responding to its beater.” Is this not what is called a settled judgment that will remain unchanged for ten thousand generations? Our Emperor embodies this and earnestly puts it into practice. Thus his virtue attains the utmost purity under Heaven, and his learning the utmost greatness under Heaven; there is clear evidence of an enduring reign of auspicious peace. Here indeed lies the means by which he glorifies the achievements of the Two Founding Emperors and the Seven Imperial Ancestors and establishes a plan to guide and sustain his successors without limit for countless millions of years.
If his sagely sons and divine grandsons can take the mind of our imperial ancestors as their own, and the mind of our Emperor as their own, giving particular attention to what is called reverent attentiveness and single-mindedness, then there need be no fear that their minds will lack purity, their learning greatness, or their virtue cultivation…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
治不恚不箴而久安長治之業祈天永命
之休要於敬一中得之矣書曰有典有則
貽厥子孫我
祖宗
皇上以之詩曰不愆不忘率由舊章愚於是又
有望於
聖子
神孫焉謹對
第二問
===
同考試官教諭陳　批〔經史一策正以觀士子淹貫之學此篇以程朱折衷諸子而要歸於道統之傳〕〔若讀其書而尚友者非漫爲勦襲〕
同考試官學正薛　批〔司馬公文中子皆豪傑之士若文正康節又二程之所推尊者其書與六經綱目並行於世子評之各〕〔當如此博洽之學也可敬〕
考試官學正蔡　批〔明道精義之學是如此錄之〕
考試官學正周　批〔經學史才讀此策可見況前二〕
李希洛
punctuated:
治不恚不箴，而久安長治之業、祈天永命之休，要於敬一中得之矣。《書》曰：「有典有則，貽厥子孫。」我祖宗、皇上以之。《詩》曰：「不愆不忘，率由舊章。」愚於是又有望於聖子神孫焉。謹對。

第二問

同考試官教諭陳　批〔經史一策，正以觀士子淹貫之學。此篇以程朱折衷諸子，而要歸於道統之傳〕〔若讀其書而尚友者，非漫爲勦襲。〕

同考試官學正薛　批〔司馬公、文中子皆豪傑之士，若文正、康節，又二程之所推尊者。其書與六經、《綱目》並行於世，子評之各〕〔當。如此博洽之學也，可敬。〕

考試官學正蔡　批〔明道精義之學，是如此。錄之。〕

考試官學正周　批〔經學史才，讀此策可見，況前二〕

李希洛
translation_en:
…governance will neither be resentful nor admonish [?]; the achievement of enduring peace and lasting order, and the blessing of praying to Heaven for an everlasting mandate, will ultimately be attained through reverent single-mindedness. The Book of Documents says: “There are established institutions and rules, handed down to their descendants.” Our imperial ancestors and His Majesty have put these into practice. The Book of Odes says: “Neither erring nor forgetting, follow the old statutes.” In this, I also place my hopes in the sage sons and divine grandsons of the imperial house. Respectfully submitted in reply.

Second Question

Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: 〔A policy essay on the classics and histories serves precisely to reveal a candidate’s comprehensive learning. This essay uses Cheng and Zhu as the standard for assessing the various masters and ultimately grounds its argument in the transmission of the succession of the Way.〕〔It is as though the writer, reading their books, has befriended the ancients; this is no casual exercise in plagiarism.〕

Associate Examiner Xue, Instructor, comments: 〔Master Sima and Wenzhongzi were both outstanding men. Wenzheng and Kangjie, moreover, were esteemed by the two Cheng brothers. Their books circulate in the world alongside the Six Classics and the Outline and Details (Gangmu). Your assessments of them are each〕〔apt. Such broad and comprehensive learning deserves respect.〕

Examiner Cai, Instructor, comments: 〔This is what learning that illuminates the Way and refines the understanding of rightness should be like. Include it in the record.〕

Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: 〔Learning in the classics and talent for history are evident upon reading this policy essay, all the more so in the preceding two…〕

Li Xiluo

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
場文氣雄渾惜不能盡錄也
君子窮經以闡性命之原者深於道者也
作史以定是非之極者精於義者也夫聖
人之道著於經固理學性命之精微而春
秋則因魯史以寓王法筆削之義又萬世
是非之權衡也删述而後窮經者各以其
學著書以希作述之事然見道或有淺深
立言遂有純駁而於聖人精微之藴無所
發明作史者各以其才紀志以著理亂之
===
跡然一時之論議或偏千載之是非莫定
而於春秋之義多所違繆是以雖其用志
之勤而終不免於疵議之及自非大儒者
出因遺經以推性命之原爲綱目以定是
非之極則道以文晦史以文勝學者貿然
莫知取衷而孔孟不傳之緒不幾於遂絕
耶然則程朱二子之功豈其微也哉執事
舉晉之先哲策諸生而肆論其所爲經史
者遂及程朱以遡孔孟蓋欲興景行之思
punctuated:
場文氣雄渾，惜不能盡錄也。
君子窮經以闡性命之原者，深於道者也；作史以定是非之極者，精於義者也。夫聖人之道著於經，固理學性命之精微，而春秋則因魯史以寓王法，筆削之義，又萬世是非之權衡也。删述而後，窮經者各以其學著書，以希作述之事，然見道或有淺深，立言遂有純駁，而於聖人精微之藴無所發明。作史者各以其才紀志，以著理亂之跡，然一時之論議或偏，千載之是非莫定，而於春秋之義多所違繆。是以雖其用志之勤，而終不免於疵議之及。自非大儒者出，因遺經以推性命之原，爲綱目以定是非之極，則道以文晦，史以文勝，學者貿然莫知取衷，而孔孟不傳之緒不幾於遂絕耶？然則程朱二子之功，豈其微也哉！執事舉晉之先哲策諸生，而肆論其所爲經史者，遂及程朱以遡孔孟，蓋欲興景行之思
translation_en:
…the writings from those sessions are vigorous and powerful. It is regrettable that they cannot all be included.

Gentlemen who thoroughly investigate the classics to elucidate the source of human nature and heavenly endowment have a profound understanding of the Way; those who write history to establish the ultimate standard of right and wrong have a precise understanding of righteousness. The Way of the sages is manifest in the classics, which indeed contain the subtleties of the study of principle, human nature, and heavenly endowment. The Spring and Autumn Annals, however, draws upon the historical records of Lu to embody kingly law; the moral judgments expressed through its inclusion and deletion of material are also the balance by which right and wrong are weighed for all ages.

After the sage’s work of editing and transmitting, those who investigated the classics each wrote books according to their learning, aspiring to carry on that work of composition and transmission. Yet their understanding of the Way varied in depth, and their pronouncements consequently varied in purity, leaving the sages’ subtle and profound meanings unilluminated. Those who wrote history each used their talents to compile records and treatises, making manifest the traces of order and disorder. Yet judgments made in a particular age were sometimes partial, leaving questions of right and wrong unsettled for a thousand years and often departing from the principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals. Thus, despite the diligence of their efforts, they ultimately could not escape criticism.

Unless great Confucian scholars emerged to trace the source of human nature and heavenly endowment through the surviving classics, and to compose the Outline and Details (Gangmu) to establish the ultimate standard of right and wrong, the Way would be obscured by literary embellishment, and history would be dominated by it. Students, proceeding blindly, would not know where to seek a balanced judgment. Would not the thread of teaching whose transmission had lapsed after Confucius and Mencius then come close to being severed altogether? How, then, could the achievements of the two masters Cheng and Zhu be considered slight!

You, honored examiners, have cited the earlier worthies of Jin in posing a policy question to us students, inviting a full discussion of their writings on the classics and history, and have proceeded to Cheng and Zhu in order to trace the tradition back to Confucius and Mencius. Your intention, surely, is to inspire the desire to emulate their lofty conduct…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
知就正之道以厲承學甚盛愚也嘗讀其
書矣敢復隱乎夫六籍仲尼之所以垂教
萬世者皆經也而尚書春秋即古左右史
之所紀而刪之筆削之群聖人相傳之道
百王不易之法具於此矣百世之下庶幾
乎有能因其遺文而求其志者然漢儒以
訓詁窮經而不求諸道性命之精微不可
得而聞也以文辭爲史而不揆諸義是非
之淆亂不可得而正也道之托於人者固
===
未嘗亡而士之志於道者則亦有待是故
以經學言之王通之講道河汾嘗有志於
斯矣程子稱其格言粹處非荀楊所及朱
子稱其本領純正論治體處高於仲舒豈
非以粗識聖人之用而無申商之雜乎顧
不求至善之歸而爲好高欲速之計續經
以擬孔子則失之僭中說以方論語則雜
之僞其於道亦何得哉孫復之隱居教授
嘗著春秋發微矣史臣謂其不惑傳註言
punctuated: 知就正之道，以厲承學，甚盛。愚也嘗讀其書矣，敢復隱乎？夫六籍，仲尼之所以垂教萬世者，皆經也。而尚書、春秋，即古左右史之所紀，而刪之、筆削之。群聖人相傳之道，百王不易之法，具於此矣。百世之下，庶幾乎有能因其遺文而求其志者。然漢儒以訓詁窮經，而不求諸道，性命之精微不可得而聞也；以文辭爲史，而不揆諸義，是非之淆亂不可得而正也。道之托於人者，固未嘗亡，而士之志於道者，則亦有待。是故以經學言之，王通之講道河汾，嘗有志於斯矣。程子稱其格言粹處，非荀楊所及；朱子稱其本領純正，論治體處高於仲舒。豈非以粗識聖人之用，而無申商之雜乎？顧不求至善之歸，而爲好高欲速之計，續經以擬孔子，則失之僭；中說以方論語，則雜之僞。其於道亦何得哉？孫復之隱居教授，嘗著春秋發微矣。史臣謂其不惑傳註，言
translation_en:
…to know how to seek correction, thereby encouraging those who carry on the scholarly tradition: this is most generous. I, in my ignorance, have read their books; dare I still conceal my views? The Six Classics, through which Zhongni [Confucius] transmitted his teachings to ten thousand generations, are all canonical works. The Book of Documents and the Spring and Autumn Annals were originally records kept by the ancient Historiographers of the Left and Right, which he abridged and revised. Within them are fully contained the Way transmitted from sage to sage and the standards that remain unchanged through a hundred kings. A hundred generations later, one might hope that someone could seek their intent through the writings they left behind. Yet Han scholars exhausted their efforts on the classics through textual glosses without seeking the Way within them, so the subtle profundities of human nature and Heaven’s mandate could not be learned. They composed histories as literary works without judging them by righteousness, so the confusion of right and wrong could not be corrected. The Way, entrusted to human beings, had certainly never disappeared; yet scholars who set their hearts upon it still had to await someone to come.
Thus, speaking of classical learning, Wang Tong, who taught the Way in the region of the Yellow and Fen rivers, once aspired to this. Master Cheng praised the purest of his maxims as beyond the reach of Xun Qing and Yang Xiong; Master Zhu praised his fundamental grounding as pure and correct, and judged his discussions of the principles of government superior to those of Dong Zhongshu. Was this not because he had some understanding of how the sages’ teachings were put into practice, without admixture from Shen Buhai and Shang Yang? Yet rather than seeking to attain the highest good, he pursued lofty ambitions and quick results. In composing continuations of the classics to emulate Confucius, he erred through presumption; in setting his Discourses on the Mean (Zhongshuo) alongside the Analects, he introduced an admixture of falsity. What, then, did he attain of the Way? Sun Fu, who lived in retirement and taught, wrote Bringing to Light the Subtleties of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu fawei). The official historian said that he was not misled by the commentaries and annotations, and that his language …

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
簡而義詳朱子亦稱之爲得聖人之意豈
非以推言治道不爲權謀之曲說乎然廢
傳從經闇於時措之義先儒詆其用法則
失之刻論禮則失之淺其於經亦何發明
哉若夫康節邵子之學則推先天之易以
窮陰陽消長之數舉天地萬物之理皇帝
王霸之事而著之於皇極經世一書蔡西
山謂命數定象自爲一家秦漢以來所未
有者程子推之曰先生之學純一不雜
===
又曰振古之豪傑内聖外王之道也然程
之學實與邵異蓋程子悼聖學之不傳而
窮理盡性由學庸語孟以達六經如傳易
以明體用之一原傳春秋以明聖人之大
用然後性命之微無不章闡而百代之沉
迷以振孰事所謂上繼孔孟不傳之緒者
誠以其深於道也以史學言之董狐之載
筆於晉甞書趙肴之事而斷之矣孔子蓋
曰是良史也書法不隱春秋之筆削游夏
punctuated:
簡而義詳，朱子亦稱之爲得聖人之意，豈非以推言治道，不爲權謀之曲說乎？然廢傳從經，闇於時措之義，先儒詆其用法則失之刻，論禮則失之淺，其於經亦何發明哉？若夫康節邵子之學，則推先天之易，以窮陰陽消長之數，舉天地萬物之理、皇帝王霸之事，而著之於《皇極經世》一書。蔡西山謂命數定象，自爲一家，秦漢以來所未有者。程子推之曰：「先生之學，純一不雜。」又曰：「振古之豪傑，内聖外王之道也。」然程之學實與邵異，蓋程子悼聖學之不傳，而窮理盡性，由《學》《庸》《語》《孟》以達六經，如傳《易》以明體用之一原，傳《春秋》以明聖人之大用，然後性命之微無不章闡，而百代之沉迷以振。孰事所謂上繼孔孟不傳之緒者，誠以其深於道也。
以史學言之，董狐之載筆於晉，甞書趙肴之事而斷之矣。孔子蓋曰：「是良史也，書法不隱。」《春秋》之筆削，游夏
translation_en:
…concise in wording yet detailed in meaning. Master Zhu likewise praised it for capturing the sage’s intent. Was this not because it expounded the Way of governance without resorting to distorted arguments about expediency and stratagems? Yet by discarding the commentaries and following the classic alone, he failed to understand the principle of acting appropriately to the circumstances. Earlier Confucian scholars criticized him for excessive severity in applying standards and superficiality in discussing ritual. What, then, did he really elucidate in the classic?
As for the learning of Master Shao, known as Kangjie, he developed the a priori approach to the Changes to investigate fully the numerical patterns of yin and yang’s waxing and waning. He brought together the principles governing Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things, along with the affairs of august sovereigns, emperors, kings, and hegemons, and set them down in his Supreme Principles for Ordering the World (Huangji jingshi). Cai Xishan said that his assignment of numbers and determination of images constituted a school of its own, unprecedented since the Qin and Han. Master Cheng commended him, saying, “The Master’s learning is pure, unified, and unmixed.” He also said, “An outstanding man of all antiquity: his is the Way of inward sagehood and outward kingship.”
Yet Cheng’s learning actually differed from Shao’s. Master Cheng lamented the failure to transmit the sages’ learning, and so investigated principle to the utmost and fully realized human nature. Through the Great Learning, the Doctrine of the Mean, the Analects, and the Mencius, he attained an understanding of the Six Classics. Thus, he wrote a commentary on the Changes to illuminate the single source of substance and function, and a commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals to illuminate the sage’s great practical application of the Way. Thereafter, none of the subtleties of human nature and Heaven’s mandate remained unexplained, and the entrenched bewilderment of a hundred generations was dispelled. As for what is called carrying forward the interrupted line of transmission from Confucius and Mencius [?], this was truly because of his profound understanding of the Way.
Speaking of historical learning, Dong Hu, wielding the historian’s brush in Jin, once recorded the affair of Zhao Yao [?] and passed judgment upon it. Confucius said of him, “He was a good historian: his manner of recording concealed nothing.” As for the judgments expressed through inclusion and deletion in the Spring and Autumn Annals, Ziyou and Zixia …

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
所不能贊者乃因而不革歸獄首惡而推
見其情於是乎大義昭而亂臣賊子懼學
者顧以左氏之語而疑焉是信傳而不信
經也可乎司馬遷之世職於漢嘗易編年
之法而爲史記矣創爲義例而工於述作
其文徽而顯質而不俚後之爲史者遵其
制而弗能改才識之高朱子蓋亦稱焉而
班固則譏其先黃老而後六經進姦雄而
祟勢利是知議人而不知議已也可乎至
===
於司馬公之奉詔編集則取左氏之體以
摠歷代之事舉紀傳表志之所載治亂得
失之所由而備著於通鑑一編宋神宗謂
其刪繁舉要足以資治賢於漢之荀悅朱
子亟稱之曰温公之言如桑麻穀粟議論
極純但不爲義例耳故綱目之作稍與公
異蓋朱子懼春秋之大義不明而提要著
統因爲書法以準聖經如書丞相伐魏以
討曹氏之不臣分注周年以明武氏之爲
punctuated:
所不能贊者，乃因而不革，歸獄首惡而推見其情，於是乎大義昭而亂臣賊子懼。學者顧以左氏之語而疑焉，是信傳而不信經也，可乎？
司馬遷之世職於漢，嘗易編年之法而爲史記矣。創爲義例而工於述作，其文徽而顯，質而不俚。後之爲史者遵其制而弗能改，才識之高，朱子蓋亦稱焉。而班固則譏其先黃老而後六經，進姦雄而祟勢利，是知議人而不知議已也，可乎？
至於司馬公之奉詔編集，則取左氏之體以摠歷代之事，舉紀傳表志之所載、治亂得失之所由，而備著於通鑑一編。宋神宗謂其刪繁舉要，足以資治，賢於漢之荀悅。朱子亟稱之曰：「温公之言如桑麻穀粟，議論極純，但不爲義例耳。」故綱目之作稍與公異。蓋朱子懼春秋之大義不明，而提要著統，因爲書法以準聖經，如書丞相伐魏以討曹氏之不臣，分注周年以明武氏之爲
translation_en:
…to which they could contribute nothing. He therefore retained it without alteration, assigning culpability to the chief offender and bringing the circumstances to light. Thus the great moral principles became manifest, and rebellious ministers and treacherous sons were struck with fear. Yet scholars cast doubt upon this on the basis of Master Zuo’s words. This is to trust the commentary but not the Classic. Can that be acceptable?
Sima Qian, who held a hereditary office under the Han, changed the annalistic method when composing the Records of the Historian. He devised principles of arrangement and excelled in historical composition. His writing was subtle [?] yet clear, plain yet not vulgar. Later historians followed his structure and could not improve upon it. Master Zhu also praised the eminence of his talent and judgment. Yet Ban Gu criticized him for placing Huang-Lao teachings before the Six Classics, exalting unscrupulous men of prowess, and venerating [?] power and profit. This is to know how to criticize others but not oneself. Can that be acceptable?
As for Lord Sima’s compilation undertaken by imperial command, he adopted Master Zuo’s form to bring together the affairs of successive dynasties. Drawing upon the records in annals, biographies, tables, and treatises, he fully set forth the causes of order and disorder, success and failure, in a single work, the Comprehensive Mirror. Emperor Shenzong of the Song said that its elimination of excessive detail and presentation of essentials made it sufficient to aid government, and that its author surpassed Xun Yue of the Han. Master Zhu repeatedly praised it, saying: “The words of the Duke of Wen are like mulberry, hemp, grain, and millet. His judgments are entirely sound; he simply did not establish formal interpretive conventions.” Thus the composition of the Outline and Details differed somewhat from Lord Sima’s work. Master Zhu feared that the great moral principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals would remain obscure, so he brought out the essentials and made legitimate succession explicit, establishing conventions of historical wording modeled upon the sage’s Classic. For example, he wrote “the Chancellor attacked Wei” to condemn the Cao house’s failure to act as subjects, and separately annotated the years of Zhou to make clear that Lady Wu was …

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
僞然後是非之極得以考定而千載議論
之同異以析執事所謂上繼獲麟絶筆之
經者誠以其精於義也嗚呼經之所以弗
明者學之偏也史之所以弗精者文之勝
也蓋訓詁詞章之習沉蔽汩沒而道之晦
於天下久矣不有先覺孰開我人故孔子
删述之功賢於堯舜而孟子至以作春秋
比於禹之抑洪水周公之驅戎狄程朱二
子興起斯文而繼其微者功豈出孟子下
===
哉抑文中子生隋之季佛老陷溺之餘而
獨以其學倡明當世太史公當武帝表章
六經之時而退托於史勒成一家之言皆
豪傑特起之士而百世之師也特於聖人
之道春秋之義未有所聞耳是故六經者
學之的也春秋者史之的也學者之志於
道猶射者之志於的程朱二子之所以開
示來學者豈有他哉亦曰反躬實踐掩卷
深思而已明道精義之功於是為至愚也
punctuated: 僞，然後是非之極得以考定，而千載議論之同異以析。執事所謂上繼獲麟絶筆之經者，誠以其精於義也。嗚呼！經之所以弗明者，學之偏也；史之所以弗精者，文之勝也。蓋訓詁詞章之習沉蔽汩沒，而道之晦於天下久矣。不有先覺，孰開我人？故孔子删述之功賢於堯舜，而孟子至以作春秋比於禹之抑洪水、周公之驅戎狄。程朱二子興起斯文而繼其微者，功豈出孟子下哉？抑文中子生隋之季，佛老陷溺之餘，而獨以其學倡明當世；太史公當武帝表章六經之時，而退托於史，勒成一家之言。皆豪傑特起之士，而百世之師也。特於聖人之道、春秋之義，未有所聞耳。是故六經者，學之的也；春秋者，史之的也。學者之志於道，猶射者之志於的。程朱二子之所以開示來學者，豈有他哉？亦曰反躬實踐，掩卷深思而已。明道精義之功，於是為至。愚也，
translation_en:
…as illegitimate. Only then could the ultimate standards of right and wrong be examined and settled, and the agreements and disagreements in a thousand years of discussion be distinguished. What you, honored examiners, describe as carrying forward the classic whose writing ended with the capture of the qilin is indeed so described because of its exact understanding of moral principles. Alas! That the classics remain obscure results from one-sided learning; that historical writing lacks precision results from the predominance of literary embellishment. Habits of textual glossing and literary composition have submerged and obscured understanding, and the Way has long been hidden in the world. Without those who awaken first, who would enlighten us? Thus Confucius’s achievement in editing and transmitting surpassed that of Yao and Shun, and Mencius went so far as to compare the composition of the Spring and Autumn Annals to Yu’s stemming the floods and the Duke of Zhou’s driving out the Rong and Di. Could the achievement of the two masters Cheng and Zhu, who revived this cultural tradition and carried forward its waning transmission, rank below that of Mencius?

Moreover, Wenzhongzi lived at the end of the Sui, amid the aftermath of immersion in Buddhist and Daoist teachings, yet through his learning he alone took the lead in bringing enlightenment to his age. The Grand Astrologer, living when Emperor Wu honored and promoted the Six Classics, withdrew to entrust his aspirations to historical writing and fashioned the teachings of a distinctive school. Both were outstanding men who rose independently, and teachers for a hundred generations. It was only that they had not gained an understanding of the Way of the sages and the principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals.

Therefore the Six Classics are the target of learning, and the Spring and Autumn Annals is the target of historical writing. A learner’s resolve upon the Way resembles an archer’s resolve upon the target. Could the guidance that the two masters Cheng and Zhu offered later learners consist in anything else? It amounts simply to examining oneself and putting learning into practice, closing the book and thinking deeply. Here the work of illuminating the Way and refining one’s understanding of moral principles reaches its utmost. As for my ignorant self, …

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
佔俾之士竊嘗從事於斯而不知所裁惟
執事之教之也
第三問
馬出圖
考試官學正蔡　批〔禮法防民古今不易之論是篇鋪敘明悉歸重風化見有本〕〔是必留心於移風易俗者取之不徒以文也〕
考試官學正周　批〔以禮法救風俗之敝甚爲切當〕
〔言明禮正法處真可舉而行之謂治世之良策非與錄之以告長民者〕
君子之爲治也其節民欲也定其志其合
===
民散也制其情夫民生有欲各逞則亂是
故必定其志而後欲可節人心本屬義失
則乖是故必制其情而後散可合定志者
其惟禮乎制情者其惟法乎古之風淳俗
美也禮行而相安法具而不施者也百姓
日用而不知而長民者亦無所見其能今
之風靡俗敝也禮具而或未明法行而或
未允者也百姓日非而不知而長民者不
可不加之意矣執事以三晉古今風俗下
punctuated:
佔俾之士，竊嘗從事於斯，而不知所裁，惟執事之教之也。

第三問
馬出圖
考試官學正蔡，批〔禮法防民，古今不易之論。是篇鋪敘明悉，歸重風化，見有本〕〔是必留心於移風易俗者，取之不徒以文也〕
考試官學正周，批〔以禮法救風俗之敝，甚爲切當〕〔言明禮正法處，真可舉而行之，謂治世之良策，非與？錄之以告長民者〕

君子之爲治也，其節民欲也，定其志；其合民散也，制其情。夫民生有欲，各逞則亂，是故必定其志而後欲可節。人心本屬，義失則乖，是故必制其情而後散可合。定志者，其惟禮乎？制情者，其惟法乎？古之風淳俗美也，禮行而相安，法具而不施者也。百姓日用而不知，而長民者亦無所見其能。今之風靡俗敝也，禮具而或未明，法行而或未允者也。百姓日非而不知，而長民者不可不加之意矣。執事以三晉古今風俗下
translation_en:
…a student devoted to textual study [?], I have humbly attempted to pursue this, yet do not know how to judge it. I look solely to you, sir, for instruction.

Third Policy Question
Ma Chutu
Examiner Cai, Instructor, comments: 〔That ritual and law restrain the people is an argument valid alike in antiquity and today. This essay develops its exposition clearly and fully, placing its chief emphasis on moral transformation and demonstrating a firm foundation.〕〔Its author must be someone attentive to transforming prevailing customs. It is selected for more than literary merit alone.〕
Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: 〔Using ritual and law to remedy the corruption of customs is most appropriate.〕〔The passages discussing the clarification of ritual and rectification of law can truly be put into practice. Is this not an excellent policy for governing the age? It is recorded here to instruct those who govern the people.〕

When the gentleman governs, he stabilizes the people’s aspirations in order to moderate their desires; he regulates their feelings in order to unite them when they are scattered. People are born with desires, and if each indulges them freely, disorder follows. Thus their aspirations must first be stabilized before their desires can be moderated. Human hearts are originally joined together; when righteousness is lost, they become estranged. Thus their feelings must first be regulated before those who are scattered can be united. Is it not ritual that stabilizes aspirations? Is it not law that regulates feelings? In antiquity, when prevailing habits were sincere and customs admirable, ritual was practiced and people lived together peacefully; laws were in place but did not need to be applied. The common people followed these principles daily without being conscious of them, and those who governed them likewise had no occasion to display their abilities. Today, when prevailing habits are decadent and customs corrupt, ritual is established but sometimes remains unclear, while laws are enforced but sometimes lack fairness. The common people do wrong daily without realizing it, and those who govern them cannot fail to give this their attention. You, sir, concerning the customs of the Three Jin region, past and present, have condescended to…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
詢承學誠欲求轉移之機愚生也晚有慙
衷正何足以知之雖然亦嘗有槩於衷矣
願因明問而陳其鄙焉若稽古帝堯有此
冀方舜禹因之相守一道其於變時雍之
民稱之者以爲比屋可封非虛語也當時
熈熈皞皞之氣象與後世赫赫奕奕之遺
休不暇悉言矣奢儉之風古今異道固以
動執事之問也請遂言之且土階如舊惡
衣爲衰漆器重始堯舜禹之德也於宮室
===
衣服器用之間自奉約矣太朴不雕可以
想見且恐民之惑於淫祀乃命重黎絶地
天通唐民之化於其德職思其居好樂無
荒雖至於春秋之世有功如仲叔于奚猶
不得以邑請纓節儉有制何其流澤之遠
也今去春秋不遠於春秋之去虞夏也乃
民間屋宇窮麗衣服鮮異娛目有珍奇從
馬有繁飾其他縱淫愽而蕩家侈賽會以
徼福逞心之事未易枚舉奢靡誠不可長
punctuated: 詢承學，誠欲求轉移之機。愚生也晚，有慙衷正，何足以知之？雖然，亦嘗有槩於衷矣，願因明問而陳其鄙焉。若稽古帝堯有此冀方，舜禹因之，相守一道。其於變時雍之民，稱之者以爲比屋可封，非虛語也。當時熈熈皞皞之氣象，與後世赫赫奕奕之遺休，不暇悉言矣。奢儉之風，古今異道，固以動執事之問也，請遂言之。且土階如舊，惡衣爲衰，漆器重始，堯舜禹之德也。於宮室、衣服、器用之間，自奉約矣，太朴不雕，可以想見。且恐民之惑於淫祀，乃命重黎絶地天通。唐民之化於其德，職思其居，好樂無荒。雖至於春秋之世，有功如仲叔于奚，猶不得以邑請纓。節儉有制，何其流澤之遠也！今去春秋，不遠於春秋之去虞夏也。乃民間屋宇窮麗，衣服鮮異，娛目有珍奇，從馬有繁飾。其他縱淫愽而蕩家，侈賽會以徼福，逞心之事，未易枚舉。奢靡誠不可長
translation_en: …inquire of us students, sincerely seeking the means to bring about change. I, an ignorant student born late, am ashamed of my inward rectitude [?]; how could I know enough to answer? Nevertheless, I have felt concern about this in my heart, and would take your discerning question as an opportunity to present my humble views. Examining antiquity, we find that Emperor Yao possessed this region of Ji. Shun and Yu succeeded him, each preserving the same Way. Of their people, transformed and brought into harmony, it was said that every household contained someone worthy of enfeoffment. These were no empty words. There is no time to describe fully the atmosphere of joyful simplicity then, or the splendid legacy of blessings left to later generations. That customs of extravagance and frugality differ between antiquity and the present has indeed prompted your question. Allow me, then, to discuss it. Earthen steps remained as before; poor clothing served as mourning dress [?]; and the introduction of lacquer vessels was treated as a matter of grave consequence. Such was the virtue of Yao, Shun, and Yu. In their palaces, clothing, and utensils, they provided sparingly for themselves. We can imagine their unadorned simplicity. Moreover, fearing that the people would be deluded by improper sacrifices, they commanded Chong and Li to sever communication between earth and heaven. Transformed by this virtue, the people of Tang attended to their proper stations and enjoyed pleasure without excess. Even as late as the Spring and Autumn period, a man with achievements such as Zhongshu Yuxi could not exchange a grant of a fief for permission to wear tassels of rank. Frugality was governed by established rules: how far into the future their beneficial influence extended! Our own time is no more distant from the Spring and Autumn period than that period was from the ages of Shun and the Xia. Yet now the houses of ordinary people are lavishly beautiful, their clothing brilliant and unusual; rare treasures delight their eyes, and their accompanying horses bear elaborate ornaments. As for other practices—indulging in licentiousness and gambling until households are ruined, or holding extravagant festivals to repay the gods and solicit blessings—such acts of gratifying every desire are too numerous to enumerate readily. Extravagance truly must not be allowed to grow…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
矣是雖民之僭擬無涯是亦禮制未明之
咎也不知其不得爲何憚不爲乎抑欲民
之去奢非朿之以禮不可也傳曰民之趨
欲如水不以教化隄防之不止也是以先
王嘗以五禮防民之僞而
大明會典所載班班可考不可以毫髮僭差也
故必於宮室衣服之制車輿器數之度詔
神游手之戒三令五申家喻戶曉而又歲
時會民以考度之家塾設教以童習之俾
===
公卿大夫既得以分安位而農工商賈雖
富無所紛華禮制既明民自可守易曰君
子以辯上下定民志言嚴之不疚節民欲
之方也子産之爲鄭國都鄙有章上下有
服用是道爾其有不褚衣服不減騶從者
是豈理之然乎淳澆之氣古今異習又以
勤執事之念矣敢卒言之望雲思舍饁敬
如賓七葉同居狄仁傑冀缺郭雋之事也
於父子兄弟夫婦之間大倫厚矣天性不
punctuated:
矣。是雖民之僭擬無涯，是亦禮制未明之咎也。不知其不得爲，何憚不爲乎？抑欲民之去奢，非朿之以禮不可也。傳曰：「民之趨欲如水，不以教化隄防之，不止也。」是以先王嘗以五禮防民之僞，而《大明會典》所載，班班可考，不可以毫髮僭差也。故必於宮室衣服之制、車輿器數之度、詔神游手之戒，三令五申，家喻戶曉，而又歲時會民以考度之，家塾設教以童習之，俾公卿大夫既得以分安位，而農工商賈雖富，無所紛華。禮制既明，民自可守。《易》曰：「君子以辯上下，定民志。」言嚴之不疚，節民欲之方也。子産之爲鄭，國都鄙有章，上下有服，用是道爾。其有不褚衣服、不減騶從者，是豈理之然乎？淳澆之氣，古今異習，又以勤執事之念矣。
敢卒言之：望雲思舍，饁敬如賓，七葉同居，狄仁傑、冀缺、郭雋之事也。於父子兄弟夫婦之間，大倫厚矣。天性不
translation_en:
…indeed. Although this reflects the people's boundless presumption in imitating their superiors, it is also the fault of failing to make ritual regulations clear. If they do not know that something is forbidden, what would deter them from doing it? To make the people abandon extravagance, one must restrain them through ritual. The commentary says: “The people's pursuit of desires is like water: unless instruction and moral transformation form dikes against it, it will not stop.” Thus the former kings used the five categories of rites to guard against deceit among the people. The provisions recorded in the Collected Statutes of the Great Ming (Da Ming huidian) are clearly available for consultation; not the slightest presumptuous departure from them is permissible. Therefore, the regulations governing residences and clothing, the standards for carriages and the prescribed quantities of implements, and the prohibitions concerning invoking spirits [?] and idleness must be proclaimed repeatedly, so that every household understands them. Moreover, the people should be assembled at the appointed seasons to examine their compliance with these standards, and instruction should be established in household schools so that children become familiar with them. In this way, dukes, ministers, and grand masters can rest secure in their stations according to their allotted ranks, while farmers, artisans, and merchants, however wealthy, will have no scope for ostentatious display. Once ritual regulations are clear, the people can naturally abide by them. The Book of Changes says: “The gentleman distinguishes those above from those below and settles the people's aspirations.” This means enforcing distinctions strictly without ill effect [?]; it is a method for moderating the people's desires. When Zichan governed Zheng, there were established rules for the capital and the outlying settlements, and prescribed dress for superiors and inferiors. He simply applied this principle. If some still fail to put away their clothing [?] or reduce their mounted attendants, can this accord with proper principle? The temper of simplicity or decadence, and the differing customs of antiquity and the present, further call for your diligent consideration.
I venture to conclude: gazing at clouds and thinking of home, bringing food to one's husband in the fields with the respect due a guest, and seven generations living together—these are the deeds of Di Renjie, Ji Que, and Guo Jun. In the relations between fathers and sons, brothers, and husbands and wives, they gave substance to the great human bonds. So long as one's natural affections have not…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
泯孰非可師其他如虞芮質成閩岐民讓
畔而棄田爲閒劉永一持廉因鄉人負債
而立焚其劵以至衡茅之下有賢如王烈
者又能以德止訟信讓不匱何慚堯舜之
民乎今視諸賢無異於諸賢之視堯舜也
乃民間父訟子逆婦苦夫殘鄉隣狠於鬬
兄弟鬩於牆其他立僞劵而奪人田駕誣
詞而騁巳辯犯義之事靡所不爲澆薄誠
所當戒矣是雖民之情義乖離或亦刑罰
===
未中之由也知其可以幸免誰將遠罪乎
抑欲民之止惡非正之以法不可也傳曰
小人之德惟草草尚之風必偃是以先王
嘗以五刑防民之淫而
大明律令所載炳炳爲烈不可以毫髮出入也
故必於孝友睦婣恤之違貪婪淫酗亂之
犯過失謀故終之別多方雜訊虛巳盡人
而又歲時讀法以告戒之家藏律誥以實
減之俾懷刑君子旣得以善安業而殘賊
punctuated: 泯，孰非可師？其他如虞芮質成，閩岐民讓畔而棄田爲閒；劉永一持廉，因鄉人負債而立焚其劵；以至衡茅之下，有賢如王烈者，又能以德止訟。信讓不匱，何慚堯舜之民乎？今視諸賢，無異於諸賢之視堯舜也。乃民間父訟子逆，婦苦夫殘，鄉隣狠於鬬，兄弟鬩於牆。其他立僞劵而奪人田，駕誣詞而騁巳辯，犯義之事，靡所不爲。澆薄誠所當戒矣。是雖民之情義乖離，或亦刑罰未中之由也。知其可以幸免，誰將遠罪乎？抑欲民之止惡，非正之以法不可也。傳曰：「小人之德惟草，草尚之風必偃。」是以先王嘗以五刑防民之淫，而《大明律令》所載，炳炳爲烈，不可以毫髮出入也。故必於孝友睦婣恤之違，貪婪淫酗亂之犯，過失謀故終之別，多方雜訊，虛巳盡人。而又歲時讀法以告戒之，家藏律誥以實減之，俾懷刑。君子旣得以善安業，而殘賊
translation_en:
…has not been extinguished: which of them cannot serve as a model? Other examples include the rulers of Yu and Rui seeking an adjudication: the people of Min and Qi [?] yielded their field boundaries and left land unused. Liu Yong steadfastly maintained his integrity; when a fellow villager owed him a debt, he immediately burned the bond. Even beneath humble thatched roofs were worthy men such as Wang Lie, who likewise could end litigation through virtue. With trustworthiness and deference inexhaustible, how could they feel ashamed before the people of Yao and Shun? Our regard for these worthy men today is no different from their regard for Yao and Shun.

Yet among the people, fathers bring suits over their sons’ disobedience, wives suffer their husbands’ cruelty, neighbors fight savagely, and brothers quarrel within their own walls. Others fabricate deeds to seize people’s fields or concoct false allegations to display their own argumentative skill. There is no act contrary to righteousness that they will not commit. Such moral shallowness is indeed something against which we must guard. Although this reflects the estrangement of the people’s affections and moral obligations, it may also result from punishments not being properly applied. If people know they may escape punishment through good fortune, who will keep clear of crime? To make the people cease doing evil, one must correct them through law.

The transmitted teaching says: “The virtue of the petty person is grass; when the wind passes over grass, it must bend.” Thus the former kings used the five punishments to restrain the people’s excesses. The provisions recorded in the Laws and Ordinances of the Great Ming are luminously clear and authoritative; one must not deviate from them by so much as a hair’s breadth. Accordingly, in cases involving violations of filial devotion, brotherly affection, harmony among kin, amity among relations by marriage, and compassion for the needy; offenses of greed, avarice, sexual misconduct, drunken violence, and disorder; and distinctions among inadvertent, negligent, premeditated, deliberate, and persistent wrongdoing, one must question widely and from many angles, empty oneself of preconceptions, and let others fully state their cases. Moreover, at regular times the laws should be read aloud to instruct and admonish the people, and every household should keep the laws and imperial admonitions so as actually to diminish such wrongdoing [?], leading people to bear punishment in mind. Once upright people can peacefully pursue their livelihoods through good conduct, the cruel and vicious…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
不道雖兇無敢縱恣法理旣當人自避辠
易曰先王以明罰勑法言噬嗑之亨合民
散之道也曹劌之論治軍曰小大之獄必
以其情知是義爾其有望火不畏易測而
投者是豈理之有乎雖然此就事而言之
爾要之禮所以防民僞然敎之而不從則
禮有所不及可無輔之以法乎刑所以防
民淫然陷之而不知則刑有所不忍可無
先之以禮乎故賈生曰禮者禁於未然之
===
前法者施於已然之後偏廢不可也雖然
又有說也上所不爲而民或爲之是以敎
則易從威則易行苟下之所爲上亦或爲
之則民從率而不從令爲之固其所也禮
何爲乎法何爲乎是必本之以德可也孔
子曰道之以政齊之以刑民免而無恥道
之以德齊之以禮有恥且格治道之備也
執事患三晉之風俗不古思移易之且曰
責在有位是導之使言也故愚生敢肆其
punctuated:
不道，雖兇無敢縱恣。法理旣當，人自避辠。《易》曰：「先王以明罰勑法。」言噬嗑之亨，合民散之道也。曹劌之論治軍曰：「小大之獄，必以其情。」知是義爾。其有望火不畏，易測而投者，是豈理之有乎？雖然，此就事而言之爾。要之，禮所以防民僞，然敎之而不從，則禮有所不及，可無輔之以法乎？刑所以防民淫，然陷之而不知，則刑有所不忍，可無先之以禮乎？故賈生曰：「禮者禁於未然之前，法者施於已然之後。」偏廢不可也。

雖然，又有說也。上所不爲而民或爲之，是以敎則易從，威則易行。苟下之所爲，上亦或爲之，則民從率而不從令，爲之固其所也。禮何爲乎？法何爲乎？是必本之以德可也。孔子曰：「道之以政，齊之以刑，民免而無恥；道之以德，齊之以禮，有恥且格。」治道之備也。執事患三晉之風俗不古，思移易之，且曰：「責在有位。」是導之使言也。故愚生敢肆其
translation_en:
…the unrighteous, however fierce, will not dare act without restraint. Once the application of law is appropriate, people will naturally avoid crime. The Book of Changes says: “The former kings made punishments clear and put the laws in order.” This explains the success signified by the hexagram Shihe, Biting Through: it is the way to unite a scattered people. In discussing the conduct of military affairs, Cao Gui said: “In legal cases, great or small, one must proceed according to the actual circumstances.” He understood this principle. Could there be anyone who sees fire without fearing it, lightly gauges it and throws himself into it [?]? How could that accord with reason? Yet this discusses only particular circumstances. In essence, ritual serves to guard against deceit among the people. But if they are taught and do not obey, ritual has limits to its reach: can it go without the support of law? Punishment serves to guard against excess among the people. But if they fall into wrongdoing without knowing it, there are cases in which one cannot bear to punish them: can punishment fail to be preceded by ritual instruction? Thus Master Jia said: “Ritual prohibits wrongdoing before it occurs; law is applied after it has occurred.” Neither may be neglected.

Yet there is a further point. When the people sometimes do what their superiors refrain from doing, instruction is readily followed and authority readily exercised. If, however, superiors also sometimes do what their subordinates do, the people will follow their example rather than their commands; it is only to be expected that they will act so. What use would ritual be? What use would law be? These must therefore be rooted in virtue. Confucius said: “Guide them through governmental measures and bring them into line through punishments, and the people will evade punishment but have no shame. Guide them through virtue and bring them into line through ritual, and they will have shame and moreover reform themselves.” Here is the full way of government. You, sir, are troubled that the customs of the Three Jin no longer resemble those of antiquity and wish to transform them. You further say: “The responsibility rests with those in office.” This invites us to speak. Thus this humble student ventures to set forth his …

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
說雖然折中效郭動物有徵林宗亦愚鄉
人也是又不可專謂有位之責也
第四問
路王道
同考試官教諭彭　批〔今日之務莫大于禦戎于之敦對詳明方略素定宜錄以資邊臣採焉〕
同考試官教諭崔　批〔九邊之險要可據諸鎮之調遣無策非書生所能悉者且攻守得失雖老將不知子能言之可以觀志矣〕
===
考試官學正蔡　批〔其詞壯其氣昌有用之才也〕
考試官學正周　批〔議論源源不竭足以占抱負不群〕
帝王制禦戎狄之道有不可失之勢有不
可逆之機有不可忽之本地利大勢也人
心大機也內修大本也是故設險守國以
嚴內外之防而使窺伺者無以乘其間則
天下之大勢在我守而不失矣惠德字民
以和天下之志而使效用者罔不輸其忠
則天下之大機在我萃而不渙矣先本後
punctuated:
說。雖然，折中效郭，動物有徵，林宗亦愚鄉人也，是又不可專謂有位之責也。

第四問
路王道
同考試官教諭彭批〔今日之務莫大于禦戎，于之敦對詳明，方略素定，宜錄以資邊臣採焉。〕
同考試官教諭崔批〔九邊之險要可據，諸鎮之調遣無策，非書生所能悉者。且攻守得失，雖老將不知，子能言之，可以觀志矣。〕
考試官學正蔡批〔其詞壯，其氣昌，有用之才也。〕
考試官學正周批〔議論源源不竭，足以占抱負不群。〕
帝王制禦戎狄之道，有不可失之勢，有不可逆之機，有不可忽之本。地利，大勢也；人心，大機也；內修，大本也。是故設險守國，以嚴內外之防，而使窺伺者無以乘其間，則天下之大勢在我，守而不失矣。惠德字民，以和天下之志，而使效用者罔不輸其忠，則天下之大機在我，萃而不渙矣。先本後
translation_en:
…argument. Nevertheless, taking Guo as a model in finding the proper balance, there is evidence of the power to influence others [?]. Linzong, too, was a native of my home region; thus this cannot be called exclusively the responsibility of those holding office.

Fourth Policy Question
Lu Wangdao

Associate Examiner Peng, Instructor, comments: 〔Among today's urgent tasks, none is greater than defending against the Rong. Your earnest response [?] is detailed and clear, and your strategic plans have long been settled. It should be recorded so that frontier officials may draw upon it.〕

Associate Examiner Cui, Instructor, comments: 〔The strategic terrain of the Nine Frontier Garrisons can be occupied for defense; the deployment of troops among the garrisons has no plan [?]. These are matters that a scholar cannot know in full. Moreover, even veteran generals do not know all the gains and losses involved in attack and defense. Your ability to discuss them reveals your aspirations.〕

Examiner Cai, Instructor, comments: 〔His language is vigorous and his spirit flourishing: he is a man of useful talent.〕

Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: 〔His arguments flow without exhaustion, sufficiently revealing his exceptional aspirations.〕

In the way emperors and kings control and defend against the Rong and Di, there is a strategic advantage that must not be lost, a critical dynamic that must not be opposed, and a foundation that must not be neglected. Favorable terrain is the great strategic advantage; the people's hearts are the great critical dynamic; internal cultivation is the great foundation. Thus, by establishing defenses at strategic points and guarding the state, one makes the boundary between inside and outside secure and prevents those watching for opportunities from exploiting any gap. Then the great strategic advantage of the realm rests with us, preserved without loss. By nurturing the people with kindness and virtue, one brings the aspirations of the realm into harmony and ensures that all who offer their service give their utmost loyalty. Then the great critical dynamic of the realm rests with us, concentrated rather than dispersed. Put the foundation first and afterward…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
未以立修攘之基使在我者所有恃以無
虞而在外者舉不得加之我則天下之大
本在我慎而不忽矣尚何戎夷之不可制
而有彊圉不靖之慮哉執事發策以禦戎
之道下詢蓋慨然有安邊之志而且以先
憂望承學也雖非其人敢不掇拾以對聞
之陸贄曰夷狄爲患自古有之蓋中國之
有夷狄猶造化之有陰陽晝夜人類之有
君子小人要之雖有內外華夷之辨亦天
===
地並育之不能絕焉者也是故有苗之征
在四方風動之域鬼方之伐當萬邦作乂
之時自有虞氏以來已不能無玆患矣而
感格道化之術征討制禦之方則有不可
以一致齊者焉書曰無怠無荒四夷來王
又曰明王慎德四夷咸賓此言化之也而
未始征之也然荒服之外聲教所不逮聖
王所不臣而犬羊之性其去來無定其出
沒無常雖聖王亦豈能保其不爲我患而
punctuated: 未，以立修攘之基，使在我者所有恃以無虞，而在外者舉不得加之我，則天下之大本在我慎而不忽矣。尚何戎夷之不可制，而有彊圉不靖之慮哉？執事發策，以禦戎之道下詢，蓋慨然有安邊之志，而且以先憂望承學也。雖非其人，敢不掇拾以對？聞之陸贄曰：「夷狄爲患，自古有之。」蓋中國之有夷狄，猶造化之有陰陽晝夜，人類之有君子小人。要之，雖有內外華夷之辨，亦天地並育之不能絕焉者也。是故有苗之征，在四方風動之域；鬼方之伐，當萬邦作乂之時。自有虞氏以來，已不能無玆患矣。而感格道化之術、征討制禦之方，則有不可以一致齊者焉。《書》曰：「無怠無荒，四夷來王。」又曰：「明王慎德，四夷咸賓。」此言化之也，而未始征之也。然荒服之外，聲教所不逮，聖王所不臣，而犬羊之性，其去來無定，其出沒無常，雖聖王亦豈能保其不爲我患而
translation_en:
…secondary matters [?], thereby establishing the foundation for internal cultivation and resistance to external threats. If those within our realm all have something upon which to rely and are free from anxiety, while those outside can inflict nothing upon us, then the great foundation of the realm will be in our keeping, carefully maintained and never neglected. What Rong and Yi could then remain beyond our control, and what cause would there be to fear unrest along the frontiers? You, honored examiners, have set a policy question asking about the way to resist the Rong. Surely you are deeply resolved to secure the borders, and expect us students likewise to put concern for the realm before our own comfort. Though I am unequal to the task, how could I fail to gather what I can and offer a reply?

I have heard these words of Lu Zhi: “The Yi and Di have caused trouble since antiquity.” The presence of Yi and Di alongside the Central States is like the presence of yin and yang, day and night, in the workings of creation, or of gentlemen and petty men among humankind.
