In essence, although there are distinctions between inner and outer, Hua and Yi, they too are nurtured together by Heaven and Earth and cannot be eliminated. Thus, the campaign against the Youmiao took place within a realm where the four quarters responded like grass bending before the wind; the attack on Guifang occurred when the myriad states were well governed. Ever since the time of the ruler of Youyu, Shun, such troubles have been unavoidable. Yet the arts of moving them to submission and transforming them through the Way, and the methods of campaigning against and restraining them, cannot all be reduced to one uniform approach.

The Book of Documents says: “Be neither idle nor neglectful, and the Yi of the four quarters will come to acknowledge your kingship.” It also says: “When an enlightened king attends carefully to his virtue, the Yi of the four quarters all come as guests.” These passages speak of transforming them, without undertaking campaigns against them. Yet beyond the outermost zone of allegiance lie places that moral instruction does not reach and peoples whom even sage kings do not make their subjects. With their nature like that of dogs and sheep, their coming and going is unsettled, their appearances and disappearances unpredictable. Could even a sage king guarantee that they would never cause us trouble and…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
無以爲征討制禦之方也哉周宣王時玁
狁內侵至于涇陽命將征之盡境而還是
來則禦之去不窮追所謂治之以不治而
不臣其所不可臣禦戎之策莫加矣自是
而秦始皇有長城之築焉自是而漢武帝
有攻討之威焉夫疲民力以幸邊功竭中
國而樹垣守秦之爲役誠勞矣然居中制
外尚足以備禦戎馬之衝而一勞永逸有
得夫設險守國之義較之漢武深入遠戍
===
徒耀武於目前克獲成功罔貽謀於日後
者其得失豈不昭然也乎劉貺故曰周得
上策秦得其中漢無策而嚴尤三策要之
非至當之論也洪惟我
國家自
皇祖開基
列聖嗣統臣妾萬國鞭撻四夷百七八十年來
以及我
皇上盛德大業神武聖文道化窮荒威行海外
punctuated:
無以爲征討制禦之方也哉？周宣王時，玁狁內侵，至于涇陽，命將征之，盡境而還。是來則禦之，去不窮追，所謂治之以不治，而不臣其所不可臣，禦戎之策莫加矣。自是而秦始皇有長城之築焉，自是而漢武帝有攻討之威焉。夫疲民力以幸邊功，竭中國而樹垣守，秦之爲役誠勞矣。然居中制外，尚足以備禦戎馬之衝，而一勞永逸，有得夫設險守國之義。較之漢武深入遠戍，徒耀武於目前，克獲成功，罔貽謀於日後者，其得失豈不昭然也乎？劉貺故曰：「周得上策，秦得其中，漢無策。」而嚴尤三策，要之非至當之論也。
洪惟我國家，自皇祖開基，列聖嗣統，臣妾萬國，鞭撻四夷，百七八十年來，以及我皇上，盛德大業，神武聖文，道化窮荒，威行海外。
translation_en:
…and yet have no means of conducting punitive expeditions and keeping them in check? In the time of King Xuan of Zhou, the Xianyun invaded the interior, reaching Jingyang. He ordered his generals to campaign against them; they went as far as the frontier and returned. Thus, when the enemy came, they resisted them; when the enemy withdrew, they did not pursue them to exhaustion. This was what is meant by governing them through noninterference and declining to make subjects of those who could not be made subjects. No strategy for resisting the Rong could surpass it. Thereafter, the First Emperor of Qin undertook the construction of the Great Wall; thereafter, Emperor Wu of Han displayed his might in offensive campaigns. To exhaust the people's strength in the hope of achievements on the frontier, and to drain the central realm to erect defensive walls—Qin's undertaking was indeed burdensome. Yet, by remaining within and controlling those outside, it could still guard against the onslaught of enemy cavalry. Through one exertion it secured lasting repose, grasping something of the principle of establishing defensive barriers to protect the state. Compare this with Emperor Wu of Han, who penetrated deeply into distant territory and stationed garrisons far away, merely displaying military might in the present and winning victories, without leaving plans for the future: are their respective merits and failings not perfectly clear? Liu Kuang therefore said: “Zhou obtained the best strategy; Qin obtained the middling one; Han had no strategy.” As for Yan You's three strategies, taken as a whole, his assessment was not entirely sound.
We reverently reflect that, since our imperial ancestor laid the foundations of our dynasty and successive sage sovereigns inherited the throne, our state has reduced the myriad countries to subjection and chastised the barbarians of the four quarters. Over these hundred and seventy or eighty years, down to our present Emperor, sublime virtue and great achievements, divine military prowess and sagely civil accomplishment have prevailed. His moral influence transforms the remotest wilderness, and his might extends beyond the seas…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
至治之盛媲美虞周夫何邇年以來黠虜
無知敢於犯順故往歲嘗寇宣大矣又寇
延綏矣又屢犯遼東矣又長驅太原矣致
諸鎮虜掠之苦貽三晉屠戮之災我
皇上宵旰圖謀撥策群力並宜
雖咸賓之化可期而干襄之績未奏則執
事所謂守備之失宜修復之未講者要之
誠有見之說而愚不敢謂其必無也伍文
莊曰
===
國初之盛所守不過數處然皆據其總會扼
其要害人聚力全而虜之來有以待之得
以全力制勝而正統以後則有不然者焉
夷考其地則曰宣府曰大同曰甘肅曰遼
東曰大寧永樂初革去大寧惟存四鎮凡
此皆西北邊城立爲重鎮而統之以重兵
則所謂總會要害之區莫大於此乃後寧
夏守鎮肇於永樂之時榆林控制始於正
統之世其餘花馬池等堡又創置於邊境
punctuated:
至治之盛，媲美虞周。夫何邇年以來，黠虜無知，敢於犯順？故往歲嘗寇宣大矣，又寇延綏矣，又屢犯遼東矣，又長驅太原矣，致諸鎮虜掠之苦，貽三晉屠戮之災。我皇上宵旰圖謀，撥策群力並宜。雖咸賓之化可期，而干襄之績未奏，則執事所謂守備之失宜、修復之未講者，要之誠有見之說，而愚不敢謂其必無也。
伍文莊曰：「國初之盛，所守不過數處，然皆據其總會，扼其要害，人聚力全，而虜之來有以待之，得以全力制勝。而正統以後，則有不然者焉。」夷考其地，則曰宣府，曰大同，曰甘肅，曰遼東，曰大寧。永樂初革去大寧，惟存四鎮。凡此皆西北邊城，立爲重鎮，而統之以重兵，則所謂總會要害之區，莫大於此。乃後寧夏守鎮肇於永樂之時，榆林控制始於正統之世，其餘花馬池等堡，又創置於邊境
translation_en:
…the splendor of consummate government rivals that of Yu and Zhou. Why, then, have the cunning barbarians in recent years been so ignorant as to dare attack those who uphold the proper order? In past years they raided Xuanfu and Datong, then Yansui; they repeatedly invaded Liaodong and drove deep into Taiyuan. They subjected the frontier garrisons to the suffering of plunder and brought the calamity of slaughter upon the Three Jin regions of Shanxi. Our Emperor rises before dawn and eats late, deliberating on plans, devising strategies and suitably coordinating collective efforts [?]. Although we may hope for the transforming influence that brings all into submission, the achievement of military pacification [?] has yet to be reported. Thus, what you, honored examiners, have described as deficiencies in defensive preparations and a failure to consider their restoration is, in essence, a perceptive judgment. I would not venture to claim that such failings certainly do not exist.
Wu Wenzhuang said: “At the height of the dynasty’s early prosperity, only a few places were defended. Yet all occupied strategic junctions and commanded vital points. Men were concentrated and strength kept intact, so that when the barbarians came, preparations were in place to meet them, and victory could be secured with the full force available. After the Zhengtong reign, however, this was no longer the case.” On examining these locations, we find Xuanfu, Datong, Gansu, Liaodong, and Daning. Early in the Yongle reign, Daning was abolished, leaving only four garrisons. These were all frontier cities in the northwest, established as major garrisons and held by substantial forces. No places were more important as strategic junctions and vital points. Subsequently, the defensive garrison at Ningxia originated during the Yongle reign, while military control from Yulin began in the Zhengtong reign. The other forts, including Huamachi, were also newly established on the frontier…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
多事之秋制已備矣其後堡寨日多分戍
日衆然軍卒之數則固不異於前日而兵
分力輕誠有如文莊所慮者然則今日防
邊之計無亦於此焉是講可乎且夫兩敵
相爭恒苦於强弱之相懸而懼夫衆寡之
不敵然以堂堂中國百萬之師豈不足以
當蕞爾犬羊烏合之衆而顧致疑於强弱
衆寡之間者何哉蓋彼之寇我也常舉國
而來而我之禦彼也則無地非守歐陽脩
===
曰吾兵雖多分之而寡彼衆雖寡聚而爲
多夫以分合聚散之間而衆寡强弱之勢
自較若矣以我散處之卒而禦彼團結之
兵則惡可以制勝以彼合衆之多而寇我
分備之寡則又惡得以無患也哉此實兵
家之大忌而勞逸利害有成筭也誠致審
於斯而必使逸常在我勞常在夷利常在
我害常在夷則執事所謂復
國初分守之地據總會要害之區而九邊重
punctuated: 多事之秋，制已備矣。其後堡寨日多，分戍日衆，然軍卒之數則固不異於前日，而兵分力輕，誠有如文莊所慮者。然則今日防邊之計，無亦於此焉是講可乎？且夫兩敵相爭，恒苦於强弱之相懸，而懼夫衆寡之不敵。然以堂堂中國百萬之師，豈不足以當蕞爾犬羊烏合之衆，而顧致疑於强弱衆寡之間者，何哉？蓋彼之寇我也，常舉國而來，而我之禦彼也，則無地非守。歐陽脩曰：「吾兵雖多，分之而寡；彼衆雖寡，聚而爲多。」夫以分合聚散之間，而衆寡强弱之勢自較若矣。以我散處之卒而禦彼團結之兵，則惡可以制勝？以彼合衆之多而寇我分備之寡，則又惡得以無患也哉？此實兵家之大忌，而勞逸利害有成筭也。誠致審於斯，而必使逸常在我，勞常在夷，利常在我，害常在夷，則執事所謂復國初分守之地，據總會要害之區，而九邊重
translation_en: …in a time of troubles, the arrangements were already complete. Thereafter, forts and stockades increased daily, and troops were divided among ever more garrisons. Yet the number of soldiers remained no different from before; dispersing the troops weakened their strength, just as Wenzhuang had feared. Should not present plans for defending the frontier therefore give consideration to this very matter? When two enemies contend, they are constantly troubled by disparities in strength and fear that the smaller force cannot match the larger. Yet surely the imposing Central Kingdom, with its million-strong army, is sufficient to withstand that paltry rabble of dogs and sheep. Why, then, should there still be doubts about relative strength and numbers? It is because, when they raid us, they regularly come with their entire nation's forces, whereas, when we defend against them, we guard every place. Ouyang Xiu said: “Though our troops are numerous, division makes them few; though their forces are few, concentration makes them many.” Thus division and combination, concentration and dispersal, make the relative balance of numbers and strength perfectly clear. How can our scattered soldiers secure victory against their concentrated troops? And when their large, combined force raids our small detachments dispersed for defense, how can we escape trouble? This is indeed a cardinal error in warfare, and the resulting exhaustion or ease, advantage or harm, can be calculated in advance. If we truly examine this carefully and ensure that ease always falls to us and exhaustion to the barbarians, advantage always to us and harm to the barbarians, then, as you have proposed, restoring the areas of divided defense established at the beginning of the dynasty and occupying the strategic points where routes converge, while the major garrisons of the Nine Frontiers…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
鎮守備之所當先者可弗加之意乎愚請
自今遣一知邊事大臣躬臨邊境察山川
之險易相地里之遠近曰某城與某城相
接某寨與某寨相連某爲總會某爲要害某
處爲夷虜出沒之墟某險爲我兵應援之
地某塞堡之設去遠門戶而緩急不足以
爲虞某寨堡之立適當險要而兵寡不足
以致守如是則識其稍緩之處而併歸重
於要害如遼東如薊州如宣大偏關以至
===
榆林固原甘肅寧夏九邊重鎮者則城守
不可不嚴備峙不可不富帥領不可不擇
兵卒不可不多斥堠不可不修謀慮不可
不審毋恃其不來恃吾有以待之毋恃其
不攻恃吾有所不可攻使虜雖欲來也而
無可通行之徑虜雖欲攻也而無可容足
之地虜雖欲窺伺也而無可乘入之機則
守備之道周而禦戎之策備矣或曰復故
地以列分守是也而河套非中國之沃土
punctuated:
鎮守備之所當先者，可弗加之意乎？愚請自今遣一知邊事大臣，躬臨邊境，察山川之險易，相地里之遠近，曰：某城與某城相接，某寨與某寨相連，某爲總會，某爲要害，某處爲夷虜出沒之墟，某險爲我兵應援之地，某塞堡之設去遠門戶而緩急不足以爲虞，某寨堡之立適當險要而兵寡不足以致守。如是，則識其稍緩之處，而併歸重於要害。如遼東，如薊州，如宣大偏關，以至榆林、固原、甘肅、寧夏九邊重鎮者，則城守不可不嚴，備峙不可不富，帥領不可不擇，兵卒不可不多，斥堠不可不修，謀慮不可不審。毋恃其不來，恃吾有以待之；毋恃其不攻，恃吾有所不可攻。使虜雖欲來也，而無可通行之徑；虜雖欲攻也，而無可容足之地；虜雖欲窺伺也，而無可乘入之機，則守備之道周，而禦戎之策備矣。
或曰：「復故地以列分守，是也，而河套非中國之沃土
translation_en:
…the priorities for defending the major frontier garrisons: can we fail to give them our attention? I humbly propose that henceforth a high official versed in frontier affairs be dispatched to visit the borderlands in person, examine the difficulty or ease of the mountain and river terrain, and assess the distances between places. He should determine that this city adjoins that city, this fortified camp connects with that camp, this place is a central assembly point, and that place a strategic position; that one locality is where the barbarian enemy comes and goes, and another defensible position is where our troops can provide support and relief; that one frontier fort stands far from the gateways and cannot adequately meet an emergency [?], while another fortified camp occupies precisely a strategic position, but has too few soldiers to hold it. In this way, the places of somewhat lesser urgency can be identified, and resources consolidated at strategic positions. At the major garrisons of the Nine Frontiers—Liaodong, Jizhou, Xuanfu, Datong, Pianguan, and onward to Yulin, Guyuan, Gansu, and Ningxia—city defenses must be strict, stockpiled supplies abundant, commanders carefully selected, soldiers numerous, scouting and lookout arrangements maintained, and plans carefully considered. Do not rely on the enemy’s not coming; rely on our having the means to meet him. Do not rely on his not attacking; rely on our possessing a position he cannot attack. Let the enemy, though wishing to come, find no route through; though wishing to attack, find no foothold; and though wishing to spy out an opportunity, find no opening through which to enter. Then our defensive arrangements will be comprehensive, and our plans for resisting the barbarians complete.
Someone may say: “It is right to restore the former territories and station separate defensive forces throughout them. But is Hetao not fertile land belonging to China…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
乎自河套不復則虜居其內我守其外而
內外之制與虜一矣是得爲久安長治之
策也哉執險阻以爲要害固也而大寧非
中國之藩籬乎自大寧棄則遼東折右臂
宣府折左臂而山川形勝與虜共矣是得
爲久安長治之策也哉愚竊以爲二地信
不可棄也然必欲復之以爲我有顧有利
害交於中大勢阻於外而有難以成功者
則未可輕議焉借曰天下無不可爲之事
===
亦無不可變之勢二地在所必取也取之
在所必得也愚又以爲今非其時焉何也
王制一年耕而有三年之積三年耕而有
九年之積語曰千里饋糧士有饑色樵蘇
後爨師不宿飽言財貴以給用也今邊方
財貨果有三年九年之積而可以給用否
乎陸贄曰尅敵之要在乎將得其人將非
其人者兵雖衆不足恃故必有李齊而後
成鉅鹿之功必有李牧而後固鴈門之守
punctuated:
乎？自河套不復，則虜居其內，我守其外，而內外之制與虜一矣。是得爲久安長治之策也哉？執險阻以爲要害，固也，而大寧非中國之藩籬乎？自大寧棄，則遼東折右臂，宣府折左臂，而山川形勝與虜共矣。是得爲久安長治之策也哉？愚竊以爲二地信不可棄也，然必欲復之以爲我有，顧有利害交於中、大勢阻於外，而有難以成功者，則未可輕議焉。
借曰天下無不可爲之事，亦無不可變之勢，二地在所必取也，取之在所必得也，愚又以爲今非其時焉。何也？《王制》：一年耕而有三年之積，三年耕而有九年之積。語曰：「千里饋糧，士有饑色；樵蘇後爨，師不宿飽。」言財貴以給用也。今邊方財貨果有三年九年之積，而可以給用否乎？陸贄曰：「尅敵之要，在乎將得其人。將非其人者，兵雖衆，不足恃。」故必有李齊而後成鉅鹿之功，必有李牧而後固鴈門之守。
translation_en:
…is it not? Since Hetao has not been recovered, the enemy occupies its interior while we defend its exterior, and control of the interior and exterior is now divided equally between us and the enemy. Can this be a strategy for lasting peace and enduring order? Holding difficult terrain as strategic strongpoints is certainly sound; yet is Daning not a protective barrier for China? Since Daning was abandoned, Liaodong has lost its right arm and Xuanfu its left, and the strategic advantages of mountains and rivers are now shared with the enemy. Can this be a strategy for lasting peace and enduring order? In my humble opinion, these two territories certainly must not be abandoned. Yet if we insist on recovering them as our own, we must consider that benefits and harms are intertwined within, while the overall strategic situation presents obstacles without, making success difficult. We should therefore not lightly propose such an undertaking.
Even supposing that nothing in the world is impossible to accomplish and no situation impossible to change, that these two territories must be taken and that taking them must succeed, I still believe that now is not the time. Why? The “Royal Regulations” states that one year of cultivation yields reserves for three years, and three years of cultivation yields reserves for nine years [?]. A saying goes: “When provisions are transported a thousand li, the soldiers look hungry; when firewood and fodder must be gathered before cooking, the army cannot remain well fed overnight.” This means that resources are valued for their ability to meet needs. Do the frontier regions now actually possess reserves of wealth and goods sufficient for three or nine years, capable of meeting their needs? Lu Zhi said: “The key to defeating the enemy lies in securing the right men as commanders. If the commanders are not the right men, even numerous troops cannot be relied upon.” Thus only with a Li Qi [?] could victory at Julu be achieved, and only with a Li Mu could the defenses of Yanmen be secured…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
必有周亞夫而後著細柳之聲言將貴於
得人也今邊方將領果有頗牧亞夫之賢
而可以任大事否乎必二者之無備則毋
事不足爲矣倘二者有一之未至則復地
之謀未可以輕動也而况有所謂難以成
功者哉蓋不得不復者圖久安長治之策
也不能遽復者審一時利害之勢也必欲
圖久安之策而免後患之貽則實邊選將
以圖夫執險修復之利者誠不可不講也
===
况舉大事者存乎豫不蓄則不得二者之
議愚請自今曰豫而蓄之可也抑又聞之
禦戎無上策守備爲良圖以是知古帝王
制禦戎夷未嘗不貴守而賤戰也乃若選
將練兵之法討逆制勝之師則亦有不可
盡廢者焉要之可攻可守之勢不在於夷
而必攻必守之具則存乎我使能擇要害
以據天下之大勢和人心以順天下之大
機嚴內治以立天下之大本則其具在我
punctuated:
必有周亞夫而後著細柳之聲，言將貴於得人也。今邊方將領果有頗、牧、亞夫之賢，而可以任大事否乎？必二者之無備，則毋事不足爲矣；倘二者有一之未至，則復地之謀未可以輕動也，而况有所謂難以成功者哉！蓋不得不復者，圖久安長治之策也；不能遽復者，審一時利害之勢也。必欲圖久安之策，而免後患之貽，則實邊選將，以圖夫執險修復之利者，誠不可不講也。
况舉大事者存乎豫，不蓄則不得。二者之議，愚請自今曰豫而蓄之可也。抑又聞之：「禦戎無上策，守備爲良圖。」以是知古帝王制禦戎夷，未嘗不貴守而賤戰也。乃若選將練兵之法、討逆制勝之師，則亦有不可盡廢者焉。要之，可攻可守之勢，不在於夷；而必攻必守之具，則存乎我。使能擇要害以據天下之大勢，和人心以順天下之大機，嚴內治以立天下之大本，則其具在我
translation_en:
…Only with Zhou Yafu could the renown of Xiliu be established: this means that, in appointing generals, what matters is obtaining the right men. Do the commanders now serving on the frontier truly possess the worthiness of Lian Po, Li Mu, and Zhou Yafu, such that they can be entrusted with great affairs? If both requirements are fully provided for, nothing will be beyond our power [?; the transcription here reads “both lack preparation”]. But if either remains unfulfilled, plans to recover the territory must not be put into action lightly. How much more so when there are also the aforementioned obstacles to success! The necessity of recovering it arises from a plan for lasting peace and enduring order; the inability to recover it immediately arises from weighing the advantages and dangers of the present circumstances. If we are determined to secure lasting peace and avoid bequeathing future troubles, we must indeed give careful consideration to strengthening the frontier and selecting generals, thereby seeking the advantages of holding strategic terrain and restoring the lost territory.
Moreover, undertaking great affairs depends on preparation; without accumulating resources, success cannot be attained. As to these two requirements, I humbly propose that, from this day forward, we prepare and build up our resources [?]. I have also heard it said: “There is no supreme strategy for resisting the Rong; defensive preparations are the sound plan.” From this we know that the ancient emperors and kings, in controlling the Rong and Yi, invariably valued defense above warfare. Yet methods of selecting generals and training troops, and forces for suppressing rebels and securing victory, cannot be wholly abandoned either. In essence, the circumstances that permit attack or defense do not rest with the Yi, while the means required to attack or defend lie with us. If we can choose strategic points and thereby command the overall disposition of the realm, bring the people's hearts into harmony and thereby accord with the great workings of the realm, and make internal governance rigorous and thereby establish the realm's great foundation, then the means will lie with us…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
而舉動自無不宜是故守可也攻亦可也
攻則克而夷技無以恃其長守則固而虜
黠無以乘其間事無不集而功無不成
中國常尊而四夷遠遁矣尚何外患不寧之
足患哉蘇洵曰中國內也四夷外也憂在
內者本也憂在外者末也聖人先本而後
末非顓用心於內而忘有事於外也蓋內
寧而外不治者未之有也噫此執事事也
執事責也於愚生何有焉
===
第五問　　　　王銳
同考試官教諭何　批〔兵食二字莫弊于無經久之規〕
〔子之反覆辯論皆至要良圖胸中有數萬甲兵于此可驗他日于誠〕
〔之選舍子其誰〕
考試官學正蔡　批〔謀國要言僅見此篇〕
考試官學正周　批〔子之經學經世務如此真有先〕
〔憂之志者當留心以需〕
□□□之對
punctuated:
而舉動自無不宜。是故守可也，攻亦可也。攻則克，而夷技無以恃其長；守則固，而虜黠無以乘其間。事無不集，而功無不成，中國常尊，而四夷遠遁矣。尚何外患不寧之足患哉？蘇洵曰：「中國，內也；四夷，外也。憂在內者，本也；憂在外者，末也。聖人先本而後末，非顓用心於內而忘有事於外也。蓋內寧而外不治者，未之有也。」噫！此執事事也，執事責也，於愚生何有焉？

第五問　王銳
同考試官教諭何　批〔兵食二字，莫弊于無經久之規。〕〔子之反覆辯論，皆至要良圖，胸中有數萬甲兵，于此可驗。他日于誠〕〔之選，舍子其誰？〕
考試官學正蔡　批〔謀國要言，僅見此篇。〕
考試官學正周　批〔子之經學，經世務如此，真有先〕〔憂之志者，當留心以需。〕

□□□之對
translation_en:
…and every action will naturally be appropriate. Thus, defense is feasible, and so too is attack. When we attack, we will prevail, and the barbarians will have no superior skills on which to rely; when we defend, we will stand firm, and the enemy’s cunning will find no opening to exploit. Every undertaking will succeed and every objective will be achieved. The Central Kingdom will remain honored, and the barbarians of the four quarters will flee far away. What further cause would there be to fear unrest from external threats? Su Xun said: “The Central Kingdom is the interior; the barbarians of the four quarters are the exterior. Troubles within concern the root; troubles outside concern the branches. The sage attends first to the root and then to the branches. This does not mean concentrating exclusively on the interior and forgetting affairs outside. For there has never been a case in which the interior was at peace but external affairs could not be brought under control.” Ah! This is your undertaking, honored sirs, and your responsibility. What part could a foolish student like me have in it?

Fifth Question — Wang Rui

Associate Examiner He, Instructor, comments: “In the two matters of troops and provisions, nothing is more harmful than the absence of enduring plans. Your repeated examination and argument offer essential points and sound plans throughout. Here one can see that you have tens of thousands of armored soldiers in your mind. When the time comes to select a Yu Cheng [?], who but you could be chosen?”

Examiner Cai, Instructor, comments: “Only in this essay have I seen such essential counsel for planning the affairs of state.”

Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: “Your learning in the Classics equips you to manage the affairs of the world in this way. You truly aspire to be the first to take on the burden of concern. You should keep these matters in mind and await the time when you are needed.”

The response of □□□…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
善謀國者與其妙權宜以濟一時之變孰
若定經制以立萬世之規蓋經者法之一
定而不可易者也權者所以趨天下之急
而輔法之所不及爲者也隨時應變君子
固不能無行權之術而法立可守尤貴於
有經久之規圖萬世之治安者苟不立經
久不易之規而但爲達權濟變之術遂執
其術以定國是襲其故以經大猷狃其近
利以爲不可復易其不至於滋天下之弊
而誤國家之事者幾希是故弊而知其利
===
者然後可與論經也利而知其害者然後
可與論權也即利害之兩端而劑量其輕
重有所謀也有所爲也必使有利無害可
行之萬世而無弊然後爲經久不易之法
也噫知此則所以爲足食足兵之道而其
施爲措置之宜有勝筭矣夫非食無以聚
人非兵無以禦敵夫子之告子貢者雖從
政之大端要之體國經世之方安内攘外
punctuated:
善謀國者，與其妙權宜以濟一時之變，孰若定經制以立萬世之規？蓋經者，法之一定而不可易者也；權者，所以趨天下之急而輔法之所不及爲者也。隨時應變，君子固不能無行權之術；而法立可守，尤貴於有經久之規。圖萬世之治安者，苟不立經久不易之規，而但爲達權濟變之術，遂執其術以定國是，襲其故以經大猷，狃其近利以爲不可復易，其不至於滋天下之弊而誤國家之事者，幾希。是故弊而知其利者，然後可與論經也；利而知其害者，然後可與論權也。即利害之兩端而劑量其輕重，有所謀也，有所爲也，必使有利無害，可行之萬世而無弊，然後爲經久不易之法也。
噫！知此，則所以爲足食足兵之道，而其施爲措置之宜，有勝筭矣。夫非食無以聚人，非兵無以禦敵。夫子之告子貢者，雖從政之大端，要之，體國經世之方，安内攘外
translation_en:
For those skilled in planning the affairs of state, how could ingenious expedients that meet the crises of a single moment compare with establishing enduring institutions to provide rules for all ages? Constancy means what is fixed in the law and cannot be altered; expediency is the means of responding to urgent needs in the realm and supplementing what the law cannot accomplish. In adapting to the times and responding to change, the gentleman certainly cannot dispense with the art of exercising discretion. Yet, if laws are to be established and upheld, enduring rules are especially valuable. Those who plan for peace and good order through all ages, if they fail to establish lasting, unchanging rules and merely devise expedients to meet changing circumstances, may then seize upon these methods to determine state policy, perpetuate their precedents in directing great affairs, and grow so accustomed to their immediate benefits that they consider them unalterable. Rarely will they avoid multiplying abuses throughout the realm and mishandling the affairs of state. Thus, only with those who recognize the benefits amid defects can one discuss constancy; only with those who recognize the harm amid benefits can one discuss expediency. One must weigh the relative importance of benefit and harm. Whatever one plans or undertakes must bring benefit without harm and be practicable for all ages without producing abuses; only then can it constitute an enduring, unchanging law.
Ah! Understanding this provides a sound calculation for the appropriate measures and arrangements by which to ensure sufficient food and sufficient military strength. Without food, one cannot bring the people together; without troops, one cannot repel the enemy. What the Master told Zigong concerned the principal elements of government; ultimately, as methods of organizing the state and ordering the world, of securing peace within and repelling threats from without…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
之績莫能或之先也周禮以鄉遂出兵以
九法制兵而復以六卿將其兵制則易矣
然民不廢業而兵益强以九職貢民以九
賦歛民而復以九式節其財制則簡矣然
財不告乏而用益富揆厥所自無亦以用
之有節而不耗之以冗食之徒選之有要
而不縱之以驕惰之習故能致强富之盛
也如是哉我
國家承平日久法制漸更理治之端殆有不
===
容於不講者向因北虜寇邊山西告警以
戰則未足收全勝之功以守則未見有籓
籬之固其籌邊諸臣每議之兵食不足而
所以計畫區處之者已無所不用其謀矣
然卒之議論多而成功少者無他大率所
以爲足食足兵之道皆一時達權濟變之
術而非所謂萬世經久不易之規欲要其
成功也不亦難矣哉自兵言之翼翼
天朝雄據上游之地沿邊有定守而武備以實
punctuated:
之績，莫能或之先也。《周禮》以鄉遂出兵，以九法制兵，而復以六卿將其兵，制則易矣，然民不廢業而兵益强；以九職貢民，以九賦歛民，而復以九式節其財，制則簡矣，然財不告乏而用益富。揆厥所自，無亦以用之有節，而不耗之以冗食之徒；選之有要，而不縱之以驕惰之習，故能致强富之盛也如是哉！我國家承平日久，法制漸更，理治之端，殆有不容於不講者。
向因北虜寇邊，山西告警，以戰則未足收全勝之功，以守則未見有籓籬之固。其籌邊諸臣，每議之兵食不足，而所以計畫區處之者，已無所不用其謀矣。然卒之議論多而成功少者，無他，大率所以爲足食足兵之道，皆一時達權濟變之術，而非所謂萬世經久不易之規。欲要其成功也，不亦難矣哉！自兵言之，翼翼天朝，雄據上游之地，沿邊有定守，而武備以實，
translation_en:
…in their achievements, nothing can take precedence over these. In the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli), troops were raised from the townships and outlying districts, regulated through the nine methods [?], and further placed under the command of the Six Ministers. The system was straightforward, yet the people did not abandon their occupations and the army grew stronger. Contributions were required of the people according to the nine occupations, levies were collected through the nine categories of taxation, and expenditure was further regulated by the nine standards. The system was simple, yet resources did not run short and funds for use grew more abundant. Considering how this came about, was it not because expenditure was measured, without resources being squandered on superfluous mouths, and recruitment followed essential principles, without allowing habits of arrogance and idleness to develop, that such great strength and wealth could be achieved? Our state has long enjoyed peace, and its laws and institutions have gradually changed. There are surely matters of governance that cannot be left unexamined.
Previously, when the northern barbarians raided the frontier and Shanxi reported an emergency, we could neither achieve complete victory in battle nor demonstrate the security of a firm defensive barrier. The ministers responsible for frontier strategy invariably spoke of insufficient troops and provisions, and in planning and arranging responses they had already exhausted every device at their disposal. Yet in the end there was much discussion and little achievement. The reason was simply that their methods of securing sufficient provisions and troops were mostly expedients for meeting the exigencies of the moment, rather than enduring rules that could remain unchanged for ten thousand generations. Was it not difficult to expect success from them? Speaking of the troops: our august imperial court commands the strategically dominant upper reaches; fixed defensive posts stand along the frontier, and military preparations are thereby made substantial…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
編發有定籍而行伍以充夫固無兵不足
之說也乃今邊鎮疲羸不當一面而姦詭
逃亡之弊老幼單弱之形始大有可憂者
焉於是憂兵不足者則議招募民兵與調
遣分布以足其所不足矣此一時應變之
機夫固未嘗有不可者然不知歲調皆重
鎮之兵顧此有失彼之慮况民兵之招募
未必得勇敢之夫而皆濫充以游手之輩
夫強弩之末不能穿魯縞衝風之衰不能
===
振羽毛况以不習之兵當方張之虜而望
制勝以成功也可得哉愚竊以為足兵之
方當自守要者始昔人有言曰兵分備寡
兵家之大害言濫守則兵分也又曰以逸
待勞兵家之大利言擇險以坐守也今日
之事曷亦致審於斯乎夫三關堂奥之區
也宣大門户之地也入堂奥者必自門户
以發軔今不固守於門户之外而徒過防
於堂奥之間則吾之戍衆兵分而調布日
punctuated: 編發有定籍，而行伍以充，夫固無兵不足之說也。乃今邊鎮疲羸，不當一面，而姦詭逃亡之弊、老幼單弱之形，始大有可憂者焉。於是憂兵不足者，則議招募民兵與調遣分布，以足其所不足矣。此一時應變之機，夫固未嘗有不可者。然不知歲調皆重鎮之兵，顧此有失彼之慮。况民兵之招募，未必得勇敢之夫，而皆濫充以游手之輩。夫強弩之末，不能穿魯縞；衝風之衰，不能振羽毛。况以不習之兵，當方張之虜，而望制勝以成功也，可得哉？愚竊以為足兵之方，當自守要者始。昔人有言曰：「兵分備寡，兵家之大害。」言濫守則兵分也。又曰：「以逸待勞，兵家之大利。」言擇險以坐守也。今日之事，曷亦致審於斯乎？夫三關，堂奥之區也；宣大，門户之地也。入堂奥者，必自門户以發軔。今不固守於門户之外，而徒過防於堂奥之間，則吾之戍衆兵分，而調布日
translation_en:
…There are fixed registers for mustering and dispatching troops, and the ranks are thereby filled. Surely there should be no question of insufficient troops. Yet now the frontier garrisons are exhausted and weak, unable to hold even a single sector. Fraud and desertion, and the presence of old, young, isolated, and feeble soldiers, have become causes for grave concern. Those concerned about insufficient troops therefore propose recruiting militia and transferring and distributing forces to make up the shortfall. As an expedient for responding to an immediate crisis, this is certainly not inherently unacceptable. Yet they fail to recognize that the troops transferred each year all come from major garrisons: attending to one place risks losing another. Moreover, recruiting militia does not necessarily secure brave men; the ranks are instead indiscriminately filled with idlers. A bolt from a powerful crossbow, at the end of its flight, cannot pierce fine silk from Lu; a violent wind, once spent, cannot stir a feather. How much less could one expect untrained troops to achieve victory against an enemy whose strength is still rising?

In my humble view, the way to secure sufficient troops must begin with defending strategic points. An ancient saying runs: “Dividing the troops leaves defenses thin: this is a great bane of warfare.” This means that attempting to defend too many places disperses one's forces. Another says: “Awaiting the weary with rested troops is a great advantage in warfare.” This means choosing defensible terrain and holding one's position there. Should we not carefully consider these principles in dealing with affairs today? Sanguan, the Three Passes, is like the innermost chambers of a house; Xuanfu and Datong are like its gateway. Anyone entering the inner chambers must begin at the gateway. If we now fail to hold firm outside the gateway and merely concentrate excessive defenses within the inner chambers, our garrison forces will be dispersed, and their allocation will daily…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
見其不足矣焉得無缺兵之慮耶爲今之
計莫若增大邊之築以固藩籬併三關之
兵以守宣大補逃亡之軍以復故數汰老
幼之卒以易精健一遇行伍缺人卽於邊
地選補蓋其生長邊陲通曉地利習經戰
陣夙知虜情非若內地之兵但可以爲聲
援而不可驅以克敵者比一遇黠虜內侵
卽能捐軀捍患務使我之門戶肅嚴而堂
奥鎮定則執樞據險戍守不分於堡寨之
===
多健卒精兵軍威益張於卒合之後而又
嚴清勾之法申鬻放之律罷貪鄙之將重
賞罰之科則兵不求足而自足諸鎮之兵
可不必調而遊食之民可不必招也此非
經常之慮乎自食言之堂堂中國坐享萬
方之供田糧有定則而輓輸以時年例有
定額而接濟有度夫固無食不足之說也
乃今邊儲虛耗支給不敷而豪强兼併之
私歲事告凶之歉又有大可議者焉於是
punctuated:
見其不足矣，焉得無缺兵之慮耶？爲今之計，莫若增大邊之築以固藩籬，併三關之兵以守宣大，補逃亡之軍以復故數，汰老幼之卒以易精健。一遇行伍缺人，卽於邊地選補，蓋其生長邊陲，通曉地利，習經戰陣，夙知虜情，非若內地之兵但可以爲聲援而不可驅以克敵者比。一遇黠虜內侵，卽能捐軀捍患，務使我之門戶肅嚴而堂奥鎮定，則執樞據險，戍守不分於堡寨之多；健卒精兵，軍威益張於卒合之後。而又嚴清勾之法，申鬻放之律，罷貪鄙之將，重賞罰之科，則兵不求足而自足，諸鎮之兵可不必調，而遊食之民可不必招也。此非經常之慮乎？
自食言之，堂堂中國，坐享萬方之供，田糧有定則而輓輸以時，年例有定額而接濟有度，夫固無食不足之說也。乃今邊儲虛耗，支給不敷，而豪强兼併之私、歲事告凶之歉，又有大可議者焉。於是
translation_en:
… their insufficiency becomes apparent. How, then, could there be no concern about a shortage of troops? The best plan now would be to enlarge the fortifications along the outer frontier to strengthen our protective barrier; consolidate the troops of the Three Passes to defend Xuanfu and Datong; replace deserters to restore the former troop strength; and discharge the old and young soldiers, replacing them with vigorous, able-bodied men. Whenever vacancies occur in the ranks, replacements should be selected locally along the frontier. Having grown up in the borderlands, these men understand the terrain thoroughly, have experience in battle, and have long known the enemy’s circumstances. They cannot be compared with troops from the interior, who can lend support but cannot be driven forward to defeat the enemy. Whenever the crafty enemy invades, they will be able to risk their lives to ward off disaster. We must ensure that our gateways are strictly guarded and our inner chambers secure. Then, holding the strategic pivots and occupying defensible terrain, our garrison forces will no longer be scattered among numerous forts and stockades; with vigorous soldiers and seasoned troops, our military might will increase further once the troops are concentrated [?]. Moreover, if we strictly enforce the procedures for checking military registers and pursuing men liable for service, reaffirm the laws against selling exemptions from service, dismiss corrupt and base commanders, and give greater weight to the provisions for rewards and punishments, troop strength will become sufficient without our having to seek additional men. There will be no need to transfer troops from the various defense commands or recruit people who wander about seeking a livelihood. Is this not a plan for enduring, regular administration?
As for provisions, our imposing Central Realm enjoys supplies from every quarter. Land-tax grain is assessed at fixed rates and transported at the proper times; annual appropriations have fixed quotas, and supplementary assistance is duly regulated. There should certainly be no question of insufficient provisions. Yet frontier reserves are now depleted, and disbursements fall short of requirements. The selfish engrossment of holdings by the powerful, and the shortages caused by years of poor harvests, also present substantial matters for deliberation. Thus …

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
議食不足者則請須給
內帑挖運通倉以足其所不足矣此一時權
宜之術夫固未嘗有不是者然不思帑藏
係
國儲之本通倉亦有待之需况民兵與調遣
奚直數十萬之徒而動經夫不貲之費夫
山林之材不能供野火江海之派不能實
漏巵况以有限之積給無窮之用而欲淵
源之不竭也可得哉愚竊以爲足食之方
===
當自去兵者始昔人有言養軍十萬五萬
可去言冗兵之糜財也又曰屯兵十年五
年無益言玩愒之蠹國也近時之弊無亦
坐此之故乎夫額辦主兵之費也客兵掎
角之資也固主守者雖藉掎角以張勢然
以主兵之坐派而分給於客兵之浩繁則
吾之人多食寡而餽餉益見其不敷矣焉
得無缺食之患耶爲今之計莫若增外邊
之守以執險阻萃散處之卒以壯軍威罷
punctuated:
議食不足者，則請須給內帑、挖運通倉，以足其所不足矣。此一時權宜之術，夫固未嘗有不是者。然不思帑藏係國儲之本，通倉亦有待之需。况民兵與調遣，奚直數十萬之徒，而動經夫不貲之費！夫山林之材不能供野火，江海之派不能實漏巵，况以有限之積給無窮之用，而欲淵源之不竭也，可得哉？愚竊以爲足食之方，當自去兵者始。
昔人有言：「養軍十萬，五萬可去。」言冗兵之糜財也。又曰：「屯兵十年，五年無益。」言玩愒之蠹國也。近時之弊，無亦坐此之故乎？夫額辦，主兵之費也；客兵，掎角之資也。固主守者雖藉掎角以張勢，然以主兵之坐派而分給於客兵之浩繁，則吾之人多食寡，而餽餉益見其不敷矣，焉得無缺食之患耶？爲今之計，莫若增外邊之守，以執險阻；萃散處之卒，以壯軍威；罷
translation_en:
…those who discuss the shortage of provisions request disbursements from the palace treasury [?] and the withdrawal and shipment of grain from the granaries at Tongzhou to make up the deficit. These are expedients for the moment, and certainly they are not without merit. Yet such proposals fail to consider that the treasury holdings are the foundation of the state's reserves, and that the Tongzhou granaries likewise have demands awaiting them. Moreover, the militia and the troops dispatched [?] number far more than several hundred thousand, and every mobilization entails enormous expenditure! Timber from the mountains and forests cannot keep a wildfire supplied; the tributaries of rivers and seas cannot fill a leaking cup. How much less can one meet limitless expenditure from finite stores and still expect the source never to run dry? In my humble judgment, the way to secure sufficient provisions must begin with reducing the troops.
Someone of old said: “Of a hundred thousand troops maintained, fifty thousand could be dispensed with.” This speaks of the wealth squandered on superfluous troops. It was also said: “Of ten years spent stationing troops, five yield no benefit.” This speaks of the harm that idle delay does to the state. Might not recent abuses arise precisely from this? The prescribed levies meet the expenses of the local garrison troops; troops brought in from elsewhere provide mutually supporting assistance. Although those responsible for defense rely on such support to strengthen their position, when the fixed allocations for the local garrisons are divided among the vast numbers of outside troops, we have many men and little food, and the inadequacy of our military supplies becomes still more apparent. How could we avoid the danger of food shortages? For present purposes, nothing would be better than to strengthen the defenses of the outer frontier so as to hold the strategic terrain; concentrate the scattered troops so as to enhance military strength; and abolish…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
內地之恭遊以省芻糧斆四方之招募以
去無用獨以精練之兵充實要害之地其
餘各路軍騎非大舉不得調援近邊土兵
團操各處姑令分番代守凡權豪影射不
閑弓馬之夫舉不得蠹吾之財而食吾之
粟務使我之行伍既充而邊儲亦裕則兵
皆精壯輓輸不養夫無用之人用有常經
度支不給乎無名之費而又責逋負之償
嚴掊尅之罪修屯田之制禁無益之作則
===
食不求足而自足帑藏之財可不必請通
倉之粟可不必輸也此非久大之謀乎或
曰併守禦以合兵於兵足矣而三關非我
地之險要耶置而不守未見爲完策也愚
則以爲不然夫自古守封疆者必據險阻
然不守其險之險而必守乎險之外是以
古人之守江也必守淮而唐人之禦突厥
也始以河爲界其後張仁愿建三城于河
外以扼其吭而折其脅自是朔方不敢踰
punctuated:
內地之恭遊，以省芻糧；斆四方之招募，以去無用。獨以精練之兵充實要害之地，其餘各路軍騎，非大舉不得調援。近邊土兵團操各處，姑令分番代守。凡權豪影射、不閑弓馬之夫，舉不得蠹吾之財而食吾之粟。務使我之行伍既充，而邊儲亦裕，則兵皆精壯，輓輸不養夫無用之人；用有常經，度支不給乎無名之費。而又責逋負之償，嚴掊尅之罪，修屯田之制，禁無益之作，則食不求足而自足，帑藏之財可不必請，通倉之粟可不必輸也。此非久大之謀乎？
或曰：「併守禦以合兵，於兵足矣，而三關非我地之險要耶？置而不守，未見爲完策也。」愚則以爲不然。夫自古守封疆者必據險阻，然不守其險之險，而必守乎險之外。是以古人之守江也必守淮，而唐人之禦突厥也，始以河爲界，其後張仁愿建三城于河外，以扼其吭而折其脅，自是朔方不敢踰
translation_en:
…the interior’s patrol forces [?], to save fodder and grain; emulate recruitment practices throughout the realm [?], to eliminate the useless. Station only well-trained troops in strategically vital places. Cavalry units from the remaining circuits should not be mobilized as reinforcements except for major operations. For the time being, have local troops near the frontier, organized and drilled at their respective locations, take turns on garrison duty. All those sheltered by powerful families and falsely registered, who lack proficiency in archery and horsemanship, must be prevented from draining our funds and consuming our grain. Ensure that our ranks are fully manned and our frontier reserves abundant. Then all the soldiers will be picked, sturdy men, and transported provisions will no longer sustain useless personnel; expenditure will follow established rules, and budgetary funds will no longer meet expenses lacking a legitimate designation. Moreover, require repayment of arrears, punish illegal exactions severely, restore the military agricultural colony system, and prohibit unproductive undertakings. Provisions will then become sufficient without our having to seek sufficiency. There will be no need to request funds from the treasury or transport grain from the Tongzhou granaries. Is this not a far-reaching and lasting plan?
Someone may say: “Consolidating defensive positions to concentrate troops may suffice as far as troop strength is concerned. But are the Three Passes not strategically vital places in our territory? Abandoning them without defense does not seem a sound plan.” In my humble view, this is not so. Since antiquity, those defending the frontiers have necessarily occupied natural strongpoints. Yet they do not defend merely the strongpoints themselves; they must defend positions beyond them. Thus, when the ancients defended the Yangzi, they invariably defended the Huai. When the Tang resisted the Turks, they initially took the Yellow River as the boundary. Later, Zhang Renyuan built three fortified cities beyond the river, thereby seizing the enemy by the throat and breaking its ribs. From then on, Shuofang [?] did not dare cross…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
山牧馬而朔方益以無虞歲省費億計減
鎮兵數萬此守在外而不在內之明驗也
若卽險而守則險與敵共矣然則守大邊
而三關之防益固夫孰以爲非策之完也
哉或又曰減冗兵以省食於食足矣而寡
弱非兵家之大忌耶減而不增未見爲至
計也愚竊以爲不然夫所貴於兵者以其
禦盜賊則弭姦宄戎敵則制勝非徒張皇
人數也故光武以六千人而敗王尋百萬
===
之師苻堅以百萬衆而不能當東晉八萬
之卒曹操以三十萬師而敗於呂布其後
以二萬破袁紹四十萬兵此兵在精而不
在多之故轍也若兵不足恃則與無兵同
矣然則選軍徒而行伍之實益精夫孰以
爲非計之至也哉雖然猶有說也嚴武備
以敦攘外之基固有賴於兵食總兵食之
柄而要其成功則大將之任也今之將領
果得其人乎吾不得而知也果非其人乎
punctuated: 山牧馬，而朔方益以無虞，歲省費億計，減鎮兵數萬。此守在外而不在內之明驗也。若卽險而守，則險與敵共矣。然則守大邊，而三關之防益固，夫孰以爲非策之完也哉？或又曰：「減冗兵以省食，於食足矣，而寡弱非兵家之大忌耶？減而不增，未見爲至計也。」愚竊以爲不然。夫所貴於兵者，以其禦盜賊則弭姦宄，戎敵則制勝，非徒張皇人數也。故光武以六千人而敗王尋百萬之師，苻堅以百萬衆而不能當東晉八萬之卒，曹操以三十萬師而敗於呂布，其後以二萬破袁紹四十萬兵。此兵在精而不在多之故轍也。若兵不足恃，則與無兵同矣。然則選軍徒而行伍之實益精，夫孰以爲非計之至也哉？雖然，猶有說也。嚴武備以敦攘外之基，固有賴於兵食；總兵食之柄而要其成功，則大將之任也。今之將領，果得其人乎？吾不得而知也。果非其人乎？
translation_en:
…the mountains to pasture their horses, and Shuofang became still more secure, with annual savings reckoned in hundreds of millions and garrison forces reduced by tens of thousands. This is clear proof that defense lies in holding the outer approaches rather than the interior. If one defends only at the strategic barriers themselves, those barriers are shared with the enemy. Thus, defending the outer frontier makes the defenses of the Three Passes still stronger. Who could say that this is not a comprehensive strategy?

Someone may further object: “Reducing superfluous troops to conserve provisions may suffice as regards provisions, but are small numbers and weakness not things military commanders must above all avoid? Reducing rather than increasing the forces hardly seems the best plan.” I humbly beg to differ. What makes troops valuable is their ability to suppress evildoers when resisting bandits and to achieve victory against foreign enemies, not merely to make an impressive display of numbers. Thus Guangwu defeated Wang Xun’s army of a million with six thousand men; Fu Jian, with a million men, could not withstand eighty thousand soldiers of the Eastern Jin; and Cao Cao, with an army of three hundred thousand, was defeated by Lü Bu, yet later defeated Yuan Shao’s four hundred thousand troops with twenty thousand. These precedents show that what matters in troops is quality, not numbers. If troops cannot be relied upon, it is just as though there were none. Thus, selecting the soldiers makes the actual strength of the ranks still more effective. Who could say that this is not the best plan?

Even so, there is more to be said. Strengthening military preparations to consolidate the foundations for repelling external enemies certainly depends upon troops and provisions. Yet exercising overall authority over troops and provisions and securing success is the responsibility of the commanding general. Have the right men actually been appointed as today’s commanders? I cannot know. Are they indeed the wrong men? …

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
吾不得而知也然竊計夫選將者咨衆會
薦之實未修而債帥無恥之徒尚在故夫
平居坐食但知剥削以肥家逐隊趨營未
聞閑兵而識律問虜寇之名則掩耳驚心
論戰鬬之事則縮頸股栗以是望其能馭
兵善戰以收全勝之功萬萬不可得也然
則選將非今之急務耶故任一將也必公
之以會薦廣之以咨謀若有不得已者而
不敢以輕授必欲其智勇兼全才德並著
===
得若人而任之而又要之以久任之法使
兵將相識上下情通則庶乎將足以馭兵
兵足以利用而區區小虜無難制矣噫此
固所謂經久不易之規而非徒爲達權濟
變之術者執事倘不以爲迂幸進而教之
爲我
聖天子告
punctuated:
吾不得而知也。然竊計夫選將者，咨衆會薦之實未修，而債帥無恥之徒尚在。故夫平居坐食，但知剥削以肥家；逐隊趨營，未聞閑兵而識律。問虜寇之名，則掩耳驚心；論戰鬬之事，則縮頸股栗。以是望其能馭兵善戰，以收全勝之功，萬萬不可得也。然則選將非今之急務耶？故任一將也，必公之以會薦，廣之以咨謀，若有不得已者，而不敢以輕授，必欲其智勇兼全，才德並著。得若人而任之，而又要之以久任之法，使兵將相識，上下情通，則庶乎將足以馭兵，兵足以利用，而區區小虜無難制矣。
噫！此固所謂經久不易之規，而非徒爲達權濟變之術者。執事倘不以爲迂，幸進而教之，爲我聖天子告。
translation_en:
…I cannot know. Yet I venture to consider that those who select commanders have not put consultation with others and joint recommendation into actual practice, while shameless men who incur debts to purchase military commands remain in office. In ordinary times they draw their sustenance without working, knowing only how to enrich their households through exploitation. They follow the ranks and bustle about the camps, yet we never hear that they understand military affairs or know military discipline. Asked the names of the enemy raiders, they cover their ears in alarm; when battle is discussed, they shrink back and their thighs tremble. To expect such men to command troops effectively, fight well, and achieve complete victory is utterly impossible. Is selecting commanders not, then, an urgent task today? When appointing a commander, the choice must therefore be made impartial through joint recommendation and broadened through consultation. Even when an appointment is unavoidable, one must not dare confer it lightly: the candidate must possess both wisdom and courage in full measure, and display both ability and virtue. Having found and appointed such a man, one must further apply the principle of keeping him long in office, so that soldiers and commanders know one another and those above and below understand one another’s circumstances. Then commanders may prove capable of directing their troops, and troops fit for effective employment; petty enemy raiders will be subdued without difficulty.
Ah! These are indeed what may be called enduring principles that remain unchanged, rather than merely expedients for responding flexibly to changing circumstances. If you, sir, do not consider these suggestions impractical, I hope you will offer me further instruction and lay them before our sagely Son of Heaven.

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
山西鄉試錄後序
嘉靖丙午秋八月山西鄉試
事竣錄亦遂成〔之〕以執事從
諸大夫後乃昌言曰夫山西
者平陽蒲坂之墟而陶唐有
虞之遺民也昔堯舜立極開
統爲執中精一之傳通變神
===
化之治率先被焉
皇上敬一傳心遠紹聖統道化殷
盛流布海隅山西則嚮邇
畿甸漸漬浸灌獨深且厚矧士
生其間又民之秀而頴者乎
故其爲人沉毅剛直公廉節
儉最爲近道發於文章精深
punctuated:
山西鄉試錄後序

嘉靖丙午秋八月，山西鄉試事竣，錄亦遂成。〔之〕以執事從諸大夫後，乃昌言曰：「夫山西者，平陽、蒲坂之墟，而陶唐、有虞之遺民也。昔堯舜立極開統，爲執中精一之傳、通變神化之治，率先被焉。

皇上敬一傳心，遠紹聖統，道化殷盛，流布海隅。山西則嚮邇畿甸，漸漬浸灌，獨深且厚，矧士生其間，又民之秀而頴者乎？故其爲人沉毅剛直，公廉節儉，最爲近道；發於文章，精深
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shanxi Provincial Examination

In the autumn, in the eighth month of the bingwu year of Jiajing [1546], the Shanxi Provincial Examination was concluded, and its record was duly completed. Having served among the officials, following behind the other gentlemen, [I; the annotated character 之 is unclear here, ?] thereupon declared: “Shanxi comprises the ancient sites of Pingyang and Puban, and its people are the descendants of the subjects of Taotang [Yao] and Youyu [Shun]. In former times, Yao and Shun established the supreme standard and inaugurated the succession of sage rule. This land was among the first to receive their transmitted teaching of holding fast to the mean, exercising discernment, and maintaining singleness of purpose, and their government that responded to change and wrought wondrous transformation.

“His Majesty reverently maintains singleness of purpose and transmits the teaching of the mind, continuing the succession of the sages from the distant past. His transforming moral influence flourishes abundantly and spreads to the farthest shores. Shanxi lies close to the capital region, and has been steeped and nurtured in this influence with exceptional depth and richness. How much more must this be true of the scholars born there, who are the outstanding and gifted among the people? Thus, in character they are steady and resolute, firm and upright, impartial and incorruptible, restrained and frugal—qualities that bring them especially close to the Way. Expressed in their writing, these qualities are refined and profound…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
邃密昌大閎博辨而不詭華
而不浮則典謨稱堯舜往往
能窺敬一之奥以及夫執中
精一之旨然後知
聖人之化作人之神也於乎盛哉
按晉之疆大河委注太行拱
護恒霍鎮立昔人所謂表裏
===
山河者精氣融結靈秀鍾毓
洩於人文寧無丕應昌辰翊
賛
昭代若臯夔稷契在唐虞之際
者乎夫堯舜之道布在方䇿
不以是而事其君非忠也不
以是而治其民非良也凡爲
punctuated:
邃密昌大閎博，辨而不詭，華而不浮，則典謨，稱堯舜，往往能窺敬一之奥，以及夫執中精一之旨，然後知聖人之化作人之神也。於乎盛哉！
按晉之疆，大河委注，太行拱護，恒霍鎮立，昔人所謂表裏山河者，精氣融結，靈秀鍾毓，洩於人文，寧無丕應昌辰、翊賛昭代，若臯夔稷契在唐虞之際者乎？夫堯舜之道，布在方䇿，不以是而事其君，非忠也；不以是而治其民，非良也。凡爲
translation_en:
…profound and meticulous, expansive and comprehensive, discriminating without being aberrant, ornate without being superficial. They take the Canons and Counsels as their models and extol Yao and Shun, often attaining insight into the mysteries of reverent oneness and, beyond these, the purport of holding fast to the mean and remaining refined and single-minded. Only then does one understand the wondrous power of the sage’s transforming influence to cultivate men of talent. Ah, how splendid!
Consider the territory of Jin: the Yellow River courses through it; the Taihang Mountains enfold and protect it; Mount Heng and Mount Huo stand as its guardians. This is what men of old called a land with “mountains and rivers within and without.” Its essential energies mingle and coalesce; its numinous excellence gathers and nurtures, finding expression in human culture. Could there fail to be men who grandly answer this flourishing age and assist our illustrious dynasty, as Gao, Kui, Ji, and Xie did in the time of Tang and Yu—that is, Yao and Shun?
The Way of Yao and Shun is set forth in the written records. To serve one’s ruler without following it is to lack loyalty; to govern one’s people without following it is to lack goodness. All who are…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
士者恥焉矧二帝之後人矣
乎夫二三子去聖人之居若
此其近也被聖人之化若此
其久也頌其詩讀其書嘉樂
其道羨牆羹夜寧無親見之
願哉今
皇上聖神文武協德勲華二三子
===
又行將有民社之寄其惠疇
若采陳力宣猷必爲德與民
以皐夔稷契自待丕襄
熙盛躋美唐虞斯無忝於二帝
之後人爾矣若時自獻之義
奭成身之信以蹈於非忠與
良者豈惟二三子之羞抑亦
punctuated: 士者恥焉，矧二帝之後人矣乎！夫二三子去聖人之居若此其近也，被聖人之化若此其久也，頌其詩，讀其書，嘉樂其道，羨牆羹夜，寧無親見之願哉？今皇上聖神文武，協德勲華，二三子又行將有民社之寄，其惠疇若采，陳力宣猷，必爲德與民，以皐夔稷契自待，丕襄熙盛，躋美唐虞，斯無忝於二帝之後人爾矣。若時自獻之義，奭成身之信，以蹈於非忠與良者，豈惟二三子之羞，抑亦
translation_en: …scholars regard this as shameful; how much more should the descendants of the Two Emperors! You gentlemen live so near the dwelling places of the sages and have received their civilizing influence for so long. You recite their poems, read their writings, and delight in their Way. Yearning to behold them as though against a wall or in a bowl of broth [?], could you lack the wish to see them in person? Now His Majesty, sagely and divine, accomplished in civil and military affairs, matches the virtue of Yao and Shun. You gentlemen, too, will soon be entrusted with the people and the altars of the soil. Whom will you follow, and whose example will you adopt [?]? Exerting your abilities and carrying forward great designs, you must act for virtue and the people, taking Gao, Kui, Ji, and Xie as your standards. Greatly assisting this flourishing age and raising it to the excellence of the ages of Yao and Shun, you will thus bring no dishonor upon yourselves as descendants of the Two Emperors. But if you [neglect?] the duty of dedicating yourselves and [abandon?] the trustworthiness through which you perfect yourselves [?], thereby falling short of loyalty and goodness, this would be a disgrace not only to you gentlemen, but also to…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
執事者之恥也先是北虜匪
茹侵犯三晉
皇上眷言西顧屢降德音申勵將
率慎固封守山西守臣敬共
武服肅將
明威宵烽晝燧
神機火鏃扼三關而守之武備
===
既飭文事告成執事者有私
幸焉二三子登進之始遘兹
嘉會經文緯武樹勳揚烈有
基兆矣乎夫應龍驤首則雲
雨霈流雷電皆至
聖王拊髀則豪俊奮興群策畢舉
機使之然也唐虞之世分北
punctuated: 執事者之恥也。先是，北虜匪茹，侵犯三晉。皇上眷言西顧，屢降德音，申勵將率，慎固封守。山西守臣敬共武服，肅將明威，宵烽晝燧，神機火鏃，扼三關而守之。武備既飭，文事告成，執事者有私幸焉。二三子登進之始，遘兹嘉會，經文緯武，樹勳揚烈，有基兆矣乎！夫應龍驤首，則雲雨霈流，雷電皆至；聖王拊髀，則豪俊奮興，群策畢舉，機使之然也。唐虞之世，分北
translation_en:
…a disgrace to those administering this examination as well. Previously, the northern barbarians, unrestrained in their ferocity, invaded the Three Jin—the territory of Shanxi. His Majesty turned his concerned gaze westward and repeatedly issued gracious pronouncements, exhorting the commanders to strengthen the frontier defenses with care. Shanxi’s defending officials reverently discharged their military duties and solemnly manifested imperial might. With beacon fires by night and signal fires by day, ingenious firearms and incendiary arrows, they held and defended the Three Passes. Now that military preparations have been put in order and the literary undertaking has been brought to completion, those administering the examination privately rejoice in their good fortune. You gentlemen, at the outset of your advancement, have encountered this auspicious occasion. Surely this provides the foundation and promise for ordering civil affairs and organizing military matters, establishing meritorious achievements and making your valor renowned!
When the winged dragon raises its head, clouds gather and rain pours down, and thunder and lightning arrive together; when a sage king slaps his thigh, outstanding men rise eagerly and every stratagem is brought forward. It is the propitious occasion that makes this so. In the age of Tang and Yu, the separation and banishment…

title: 嘉靖二十五年山西鄉試錄
text:
孔昭文德丕洽象刑祗敍亦
惟諸臣是庸二三子顧學臯
夔稷契者也執事者有厚望
焉夫采薇之什出車之篇聖
人以次鹿鳴此又外寧内之
道仁義並施之術也〔之〕於試
事之竣敢忘是規二三子其
===
懋哉二三子其懋哉
直隷保定府易州儒學學正
蔡〔芝〕謹序
punctuated:
孔昭，文德丕洽，象刑祗敍，亦惟諸臣是庸。二三子顧學臯夔稷契者也，執事者有厚望焉。夫《采薇》之什、《出車》之篇，聖人以次《鹿鳴》，此又外寧内之道、仁義並施之術也。〔之〕於試事之竣，敢忘是規？二三子其懋哉！二三子其懋哉！
直隷保定府易州儒學學正蔡〔芝〕謹序。
translation_en:
…were brilliantly manifest; civil virtue spread far and wide, and symbolic punishments were reverently put in order. This, too, depended upon employing the various ministers. You gentlemen are indeed men who take Gao, Kui, Ji, and Xie as your models, and those administering this examination have high hopes for you. The Sage placed the ode “Gathering Ferns” (Cai wei) and the poem “Sending Out the Chariots” (Chu che) after “The Deer Call” (Lu ming). This, too, is the way to secure peace within through action beyond the borders, and the art of applying benevolence and righteousness together. [The annotation 〔之〕 is unclear here: ?] At the conclusion of the examination proceedings, dare I forget this admonition? Strive diligently, gentlemen! Strive diligently, gentlemen!
Preface respectfully composed by Cai Zhi 蔡芝, Instructor in the Confucian School of Yizhou, Baoding Prefecture, in the Directly Administered Region.
